Much cheaper than buying mapeline online and the large bottles will last a long time.
Just what I was looking for.  Made maple syrup right away, and my family loved it.  Thanks!!
This product seems a little weaker than competative products but if you are using a lot of you can double the amount and still be far ahead of supermarket prices.

We like to smoke chicken and turkey and I always soak the birds for about 24 hours in a brine solution with quite a few spices, liquid smoke and Maple Flavoring. It gives the birds a wonderful flavor. I make Maple Nut Rings for special occasion breakfasts/brunchs which calls for Maple Flavoring. I also like to make my own pancake syrup so I use a lot of Maple Flavoring. It is so convenient to be able to buy these large bottles and always have it on hand. Thanks Amazon, you made my life a little easier.

I decided to take a test on this product. I am making large batches of cinnamon rolls to raise funds for a charity. I needed a source for good, cheap maple flavoring. This is a keeper! I would definitely buy again. I may have to use a little more than my normal dose, but not by much. I have even used this flavoring in my coffee!

Bought this at Kroger for $3.64. $11 from this vendor? WOW.When I got it home, I was anxious to try it. I opened up the jar and ate a big spoonful. Didn't know my face could pucker up that much. This stuff is super salty. On a sandwich, the saltiness gets toned down but I can only tolerate it in moderation. I had to scrape a lot of it off the tomato sandwich. Its better if mixed with regular mayo.About 20 minutes after eating this, my lips got numb from all the salt. Kinda like theater popcorn lip numbness.I like the idea of bacon mayo but I think I will try another product or making my own.=========2/29/12=========Tried this in cole slaw and it was pretty good. Every comment about the cole slaw was positive and the huge bowl went quickly.My opinion of the product has improved but the saltiness is still an issue. We cooked a big batch of french fries and used this as one of the dipping sauces. The salted fries along with the Baconnaise was too salty for 3 out of 4 people.Still looking for an alternative with less salt.=========7/14/12=========Have you ever tried something and at first disliked it but then grew to really like it? That is me with this product. I really like it now. We have used it in everything from potato salad, cole slaw, deviled eggs, pasta salad, homemade salad dressing, a coating for chicken before breading then frying, etc....and it adds a new twist that most everyone seems to like.

column9: A bacon lovers dream come true!
column10: Baconnaise -  I first discovered this treasure when a relative over seas asked for some "ham flavored mayonaise" they heard was available in the U.S.  I sent for this product through Amazon and it has been the  "go to" item for anyone who loves the flavor of bacon but doesn't need all the calories.  It has been a great hit with the men around my home as a pre-game snack with a cracker, a little Baconaise and ham or chicken.  I started giving it out as a little host gift or stocking stuffer at Christmas time.

I first heard of this product while reading an argument over Jack-in-the-Box's new bacon milkshakes.I went to the manufacturer's website to do a little comparison shopping, and they had a tool for searching local stores to see who carries their products. After finding one, I paid a visit and came home with one jar of regular, and one of light.The consistency is of a thick spread, not quite as gelatinous as mayo, and the consistency feels appropriate to the flavor when you eat it. The sauce has very small bits of bacon or bacon-like substance in it. It is not sweet, not particularly salty (5% RDA for one tablespoon), and has a light flavor of smoked bacon. It's pretty high in saturated fat (14% RDA for one tablespoon), but, compared to actually eating bacon, that's pretty good.My first experiment was to try a fried egg sandwich: two slices of whole wheat, egg, Baconnaise. The egg and bread overpowered the sauce. I'll try a Baconnaise-lettuce-tomato sandwich next and post my results, but I suspect this stuff will do best as a dip for crackers or a veggie tray. If you could find a mild-tasting bread, it might also work in place of butter on toast for someone who can't eat bacon but who wants the taste.Experiment 2: substituted Baconnaise for mayo when making tuna salad (plain, just tuna + sauce). This made an EXCELLENT tuna, lettuce & tomato sandwich.Verdict so far: it tastes pretty good, but the only bacon in the world is... bacon!
If you are a fan of bacon you're going to like this stuff. J & D makes good products. I will buy again! Makes a killer addition to a BLT.

column9: It is a good idea but a poor execution
column10: I should have looked that the label more closely before purchasing this mayonnaise at my local grocery store.  However, when I saw it sitting there on it's shelf I immediately thought, "Bacon + Mayonnaise = Perfection!"  The big problem is that there is NO bacon in this product (the label even says that this spread is suitable for vegetarians).  Bacon flavor? Kind of.  The smell reminds me of the bacon flavored dog treats that I give to my little hounds and then rush to wash the smell off of my hands.  Not a pleasant association.The mayonnaise itself is a little thick and heavy.  I often make my own using fresh egg yolks, safflower oil, lemon juice and a little white pepper.  This has a very strong Liquid Smoke flavor to it which I find off-putting.  I can't help but wonder, why didn't they just put real bacon in this product?  I would gladly pay more if it was the real thing.  There is a product on the market called Bacon Jam and they get close to 20 bucks for a 7 ounce jar and people can't get enough of it.  If you use quality (i.e. REAL) ingredients people will stand in line to buy your product.  I would recommend that you skip this stuff and make your own, that's what I am going to do from now on.

I tried this since I love bacon everything. I found it to have this odd after taste that gets worse every time you eat more of it. If you want bacon mayo try taking your favorite mayo and add J and D's bacon salt to it then let it sit for a few minutes and you'll have a good tasting mayo with bacon flavor.

Let me start by saying that I love salty foods, love love love! But this beats even me, it is poisonously salty!!!! Disgusting and unbearable, even when mixed with regular mayo. Also, instead of bacon I'd say the flavor is closer to anchovies (which are pretty salty themselves). So instead of baconnaise this should be called anchovaise. Gross and overpriced!
My son discovered this product and loves it, had to go to Amazon to find it again.  He is very happy and can't wait to make his sandwiches with it.

I had SUCH high expectations of this product!! I LOVE the creativity and the humor of the J&D company. But THIS is so darn terrible.. I tried it right after opening, and thought OK.. this is not good when it's warm... So.. after a while in the fridge I tried a sandwich with it.. But, not really sure what I was eating I was not tempted to try it again.. So, it stood in the fridge and today I threw it out. It comes across as 'very weird' tasting, instead of being blown away by a Bacon Taste.. Not really I believe. Then I'd rather bake the real stuff, only every now and then ;-)

column9: Grossest thing I have ever tasted.
column10: This stuff is one of the worst things I have ever had. It makes even the best of dinners inedible.To tell you how it tastes, it tastes like something in your recipe went bad, like you used chunky milk in your dish.I hate it with a deep burning passion, and would never recommend it to anyone who has taste buds.
The flavor is quite good on this product. unfortunately throughout the day, i enjoyed that flavor more and more times.... then again during the night, and with breakfast the next day.

I have tasted most Moroccan teas in the US and have drunk heaps of the stuff in Morocco. This tea is excellent. Though i don't like the way Moroccan tea is brewed (boiled for 10 minutes and then drowned in sugar), I use a tea ball and put it into hot water for 3 minutes. I love it without sugar and find this brand to be excellent.

column9: First time was not a charm.
column10: I did not enjoy this tea & I love tea. This was the first time I had tried a loose leaf tea & I did not like the experience at all.  It was messy & didn't enjoy the taste, like my other teas.  A big disappointment, especially when I see I can't even return it.  It was a waste of money for me.

I LOVE the taste of Coombs Family Farms maple syrup. It's pure and fresh tasting, not sweet and sugary like store bought brands. It has a dark rich flavor too.I recently learned a lot about the Coombs Family Farms and their organic products. They have the most amazing recipes on their site too using maple syrup.The Coombs Family Farms maple sugar and maple candy are great too!

I much prefer artichoke hearts, but I ordered the artichoke bottoms because my husband "thinks" he doesn't like the artichoke hearts and this is one way to include healthy,  beneficial artichokes in salads, omelets, etc.As far as the product itself, it is the same very good quality that we have found in all of the Roland products we have ordered.

those artichokes are so hard, and no taste at all, all 6 cans were bended, that cut my taste for artichoke for a long time and I uses to love it.I had bougth the small one , they are a bit better.money in the drain as I had to discarded the whole shipment.

I had never tried artichoke bottoms before, but I love fresh artichokes, and I found a couple of recipes using the bottoms, so I thought I'd give them a try.  I bought a package of six cans, and I used them a lot faster than I thought I would.  There were just so many ways to use them, and they flavor and texture are great.  I often dice them and use them as a substitute for potatoes in stews and such for a lower carbohydrate alternative.  I also like them stuffed with scrambled eggs, topped with lowfat shredded cheese and baked.  Yum.  Also, I am not a huge fan of canned artichoke hearts, because I find the brine or whatever annoyingly overpowering.  Not so with the bottoms.  They have a sturdier, yet still buttery quality.  I'm hooked. I am buying more right now.

column9: Taste like metal, 4 of 6 cans badly dented
column10: I was not happy with these art heart bottoms. Only 2 cans survived the trip, and the product in those tasted heavily of the can, yuck.  I will be looking for art hearts in glass jars...and not ordering them online so they stay intact.
Cattlemen's Barbecue Sauce is delicious.  It is hard to find in grocery stores and I was happy to find it on Amazon.
Safeway stopped carrying this thicker and flavorful sauce.  I too was glad to find it on Amazon, but be warned this supplier is slow.
I received my gum so quickly. My son and I are addicted to it,always have to stock up on it.
gum doesn't stick to paper, long flavor, yummy, quick fix on having sugar if needed, good product, will order again.

Tastes so good it's hard to believe it's zero cal.  While a bit thin, perhaps, compared to a typical full-sugar syrup, it has no artificial swetener taste to it that some low/no calorie product substitutes have.  Besides using it on pancakes, waffles and the like, I've started using it on cereals and other things that I would normally sprinkle sugar on.  I was so happy with my original purchase that I ordered a half dozen bottles the next time around.

column9: Next best thing to the real thing!
column10: Okay, it hasn't seen the inside of a maple tree.  But this is an excellent imitation -- far better than the calorie-full or calorie-free brands you'll find on your grocers' shelves.  Strongly recommended!

I purchased this syrup based on customer reviews and I have to agree - this is great stuff! I used it on my Medifast pancakes this morning and was 100% satisfied with the texture and taste. I'm extremely sensitive to the sugar-free aftertaste that so many low calorie products have and this didn't bother me at all. I really don't think I'll use any other pancake syrup in the future. Thank you Walden Foods!

Heard rave reviews about this product before purchasing and I see why. While there is a difference in this and traditional maple syrup, it's not off by much in the flavor department. Considering how many calories are in regular syrup, this is a great way to enjoy french toast or waffles and not feel guilty when you slab on the maple syrup. The texture is thinner, but I was blown away at how close the taste gets. After while you'll get used to it too and not miss the old stuff.

Honestly, I like this stuff better than actual syrup. It's just the right sweetness, and yeah, it's kind of runny, but it's good on just about EVERYTHING--it can take the most boring pancake/muffin/waffle/whatever in the world and make it DELICIOUS. Seriously, this is one of my all-time favorite "foods". Top 10 list of best grocery purchases I ever made, for sure.

I have been using Walden Farms products since the company came to North America and they are a regular part of my shopping list. Their pancake syrup is thick and fantastic. This is so versatile and great on Salmon (maple glazed), chicken, turkey etc, in chili and stews instead of molasses, great in butternut/carrot/pumpkin pureed soups, in milkshakes, on toast (french toast, biscuits, bread puddings, or breakfast bakes, on eggs, pancakes, high-fiber cereal, in puddings, hot and cold cereals, desserts, ice cream souffles,and in steamed milk and hot coffee! This is great on waffles, or to bake with (great for cakes/muffins etc); I love pouring it on top of crumb cakes and letting it soak in. I especially love mixing it into Greek yogurt or cottage cheese. Adding it to pumpkin puree with some cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, and sweetener makes it tastes like pumpkin pie in a bowl, but healthy. Great way to have flavor without the added sugar.
I use this frequently on Carquik waffles.  It's good, but I've found that if I use too much, I get a, how do I say it, aversion to it.  So, as long as the waffle isn't swimming in syrup, it's OK.

column9: How can this be calorie free?!
column10: Generally, when tasting zero-calorie diet products, I advise people to first recognize that its a diet product and won't taste as good as its full-calorie counterpart.Forget about that in this instance.  This pancake syrup tastes every bit as good as any other pancake syrup (sugar free or not) I've ever had.  Sure, its a tiny bit thinner than Aunt Jemima, but its not water!  And the flavor is spot on!Does it taste like pure maple syrup? Probably not.  Does it taste like every other imitation maple syrup out there? I think so.Seriously, if this can taste this good with negligible calories, why ever use the other stuff?This is great. Try it. Seriously.  You won't regret it.  And, if you do, Walden Farms will refund your money if you saved your receipt.  Risk free deliciousness!

The consistency of this syrup (as with almost all 0 carb, 0 cal products) is considerably runnier than a normal syrup. If you can get past that, the taste is actually much better than I expected. My husband didn't care for it much because he tried to keep it cold and put it on his pancakes. It wasn't good this way. I recommend leaving the bottle be room temperature, and pouring it over the pancakes right off the stove (or griddle) so that it soaks into the pancakes and warms up a bit.Note: We used Bob's Red Mill Low-Carb Baking Mix to make the pancakes according to the recipe on the back of the package. The syrup may taste different with different pancakes.

Wow! I was hesitant to try this particular Walden Farms product, but when I did, I found that it's great! It has real maple syrup flavor. I even used it in place of syrup in a recipe and it tasted like the real thing!
for a sugar free syrup i found this to be very good. let some frindes at work try it they liked it to.

column9: Best Walden Farms Product; Truly Delicious Pancake Syrup
column10: Best product in the entire Walden Farms line.Tastes better than the light pancake syrup my husband uses from the grocery store (which is 50/calories per Tbsp) and more delicious than any other diet/sugar-free/light syrup I've ever tasted.Doesn't have any weird aftertaste.Consistency is nice and thick...not watery like some light syrups.Comes in either a medium-sized jar or in a six-pack of small, individual-sized packets (which you can take with you if traveling or going to a pancake house for b'fast).I give this product my highest recommendation.

After reading many pro and con reviews, I thought I'd try Walden Farms Pancake Syrup since being diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes recently.  The taste is very mildly "maple" flavored....not bad, but I like more flavor.  It pours somewhat thickly and spread over things well.  I tend to pour more of this product than other low-carb syrups as they still have carbs that will add up fast into the "significant carb count" zone.  I pour more since it's sugar free, calorie free, fat free, and carb free, but if it's that free of anything then it must only be made from water plus lots of chemical stuff.  What I really do miss is regular syrup's sticky texture as you eat it with pancakes, French toast, or whatever.  I may not buy the product again, but it was worth a try.

This stuff is disgusting. All it is, is nothing more than thickening agents and some maple flavoring. It has the consistency of snot. I was so grossed out by it, that I threw it way. I strongly recommend you DON'T buy this.

column9: Try these out of the fridge or freezer; yum!
column10: The hot fudge sundae pop-tarts are the only pop-tarts my son eats. He calls them "birthday cake." They are messy because the filling is like marshmallow fluff, but runnier. I think that's why my son likes these--they aren't as dry because the filling is like the consistency of thin pudding. Sometimes it's too messy for his taste, so I stick it in the fridge or freezer for 10 minutes and the filling freezes and he likes that. It's a great flavor to try. I'm glad I could get the family pack in bulk here for $28.11 with subscribe and save.
Love the chocolate and creamy goodness and it's oh so bad for you. Promptly shipped as ordered.

Kids love them for snacks at school..and it gets them thru to lunch...the product provides about 38 grams of CHO, or fuel for the body to be used as glucose....19g come from pure sugar and the other 19g from grain....and it is low fat..and the 5 grams assure that the fuel is metabolized slowly....it is not the best of choices, but better than chips or a soda....now if the school only sold milk!!!
Nice alternative for syrups that is fairly priced. Worth a try if you are looking for something different.
My husband is from Hungary and craves foods that he grew up with. This is one of them and he is delighted beyond belief to have a taste of "home". I love it too!
I really enjoy these rice cakes. I put them in the toaster and toast them and put butter and jam on them and they are just as good as eating toast for breakfast.

I'm allergic to wheat, so I use these rice cakes like crackers or toast. I put one in our microwave for 40 seconds, and it comes out crispy. I eat eggs on them, hamburgers, anything I would eat on bread or toast.

column9: Once again, this is a great product.
column10: We travel to Hawaii. We have tasted this Guava drink. It is a natural produced item.  They only add Pure Cane Suger as a sweetener. Nothing else.  We love it.  This is a great item for mixing with those Rum/Tiki drinks you make.  Man, I know what I am talking about.  Try it. You will like it.  It is great all by it's self. No Rum required.

column9: Just the way I remember it!
column10: I lived in Hawaii as a kid and drank these everyday. They were my favorite and was so excited to see that I could now enjoy them in PA. They taste exactly the way they did when I was a kid! So yummy! Word of warning, there is a little pulp, so if you are very anti-pulp, this may not be for you.
It is nice strong coffee. I learned of it in Costa Rica. It is whole bean, and I grind it up every day. It is good stuff !!!

This is the easy way to swallow a teaspoon of cinnamon in 30 seconds or less!  Just use this Cinnamon Matcha instead, and whisk it in hot water.  You'll be gulping it up at record speed!  It is so yummy!Yeah, yeah, I know, that's not the idea behind the cinnamon challenge.  But, I assure you - this is much easier to swallow in 30 seconds, and better for you too.  (Yes, cinnamon is good for you, but it is very questionable, indeed, whether or not its healthy for you to swallow a teaspoon of dry, ground cinnamon.)This is really delicious.  The cinnamon is a spicy-sweet kind of cinnamon, reminiscent of Saigon cinnamon.  Very zesty - it enlivens the palate with its warm, exotic spice.  It makes a really nice combination with the sweet, buttery, vegetal notes of the Matcha.

I'm a sucker for cinnamon, so of course I had to try the Cinnamon Matcha. It smells so good. Sooooo good. Not like fake cinnamon hearts (which I adore too), but like real cinnamon. I want to slather this matcha on toast...but that would be weird. This is another matcha that inspires me to bake. Matcha snickerdoodles? Don't mind if I do! I need to start actually trying some of these recipe ideas. Like cinnamon matcha cinnamon toast! Or a cinnamon matcha apple pie! Nom nom nom.At first sip, it was delicious. At second sip, it was delicious. At third sip...well, you get the idea. There is something I don't care for about it, a bit of a tangy aftertaste, but that's not enough to keep me from drinking it! I'm excited to see how it will taste when blended with the vanilla. Ooooh, I should see if they have an apple matcha, that would be yummy mixed with this. Or pear! Oh dear, my list of desired matchas is growing longer and longer...But really, I just want to dump a whole mess of sugar into this and make some cinnamon raisin toast. And bake my little heart out! I think this is a matcha I will end up mixing more than making straight, but that's okay. I am seeing a wide world of possibilities coming from this little beauty. Cinnamon and I were good friends before, but I think is safe to say that this tea has pushed us over the edge into best friend territory. Plays well with others, makes me feel better, and encourages me to eat tasty, tasty sweets! I can see this becoming a staple in my cupboard, sitting right next to my beloved vanilla.
great taste, good price... Always looking for some flavor to add to my tea muixture, this works better than most of the ones I've tried

I love salmon spread.  I buy it here in MA, but thought it would be better from Alaska.  I ordered this item because I just returned from Alaska and had the best salmon and salmon spread there.  I ordered this item hoping that it would be fantastic because Alaska is known for its salmon.  I was VERY disappointed.  It tasted and smelled like cat food!  I did write to the company, but have yet to receive a response.
I get 4 -6 cans of salmon or trout spread each year and I mix a can with sour cream and dill for a very good dip.

column9: Somewhat Bland and Tasteless. High Sodium Content.
column10: Not too long ago (within the last month) I picked up a couple cans of Progresso soups to have on my shelves in the event that I might need a quick and simple lunch. Today, I had a can of the Rich and Hardy Chicken Pot Pie Style. Well, it looked so tempting on the shelf, but I was somewhat disappointed. It was somewhat bland and flavorless and seemed starchy, Then I noticed the sodium. Way up there. That can of soup was two-thirds of my daily intake. Too much. I'm going to have to read my labels more carefully.Gary Peterson
I use to be able to find these treats local and my two very picky chihuahuas love them more than any other treat and i have tried many. I consider these a must have item at a reasonable price.
My Unspoiled master loves them.M m m m m m m m m m m m m mm m m m mm m m m mm  mm good

According to the hype on the bag as well as the nutrition information, this whole grain is quite healthy.  I've been eating it for breakfast almost every day for several months, and it seems to get me off to a good start.  Since the millet itself doesn't have much flavor, I fill a large bowl with 95% millet, and 5% granola sprinkled on top (plus some ground flax seed); I then add milk.  I get granola with each bite, and it makes the whole bowl really quite tasty, without being overwhelmingly sweet.It's cheap, healthy and filling.  Just make sure you have plenty of pantry space, as you get twelve large bags with this order.

Arrowhead produces several puffed cereals but this is my favorite. First off, it doesn't get soggy. You can take several phone calls or even a shower and come back and find this stuff is still holding up to the milk. And because the kernels are small it's ideal for someone like me with jaw problems. The flavor is similar to popcorn, just milder. Only downside is that occasionally you'll get a bag where they haven't done such a good job of eliminating the hulls...bothersome buggers that have a tendency to cling to your gums etc. I start every day with a bowl.

column9: Wow, that's a lot of Millet!
column10: Um... you get a lot of millet when you purchase this. Despite the size of the box (standard cardboard box size, needlessly double-boxed from Amazon), it was very light. Each bag I'd say is a little smaller in volume than a box of Kleenex, and you get 12. It looks like more than it sounds when you get them! The grains are very light and it's easy to have spills or overpours whether pouring out of the bag or from a secondary container.As for taste and texture, I agree what a reviewer of the Nature's Path version of this cereal said, that they are NOT toasted, just puffed. She put hers on a baking tray and toasted them to make them more crispy, instead of soft. I'm too lazy, and it seems like a possible waste of energy, so I just put up with it. That said, it doesn't really get soggy, either. Just imagine unsweetened puffed rice, only broke into little 3/16-inch balls. It just kind of relents when you crush it with your teeth, think really soft styrofoam (?).Taste-wise, not much taste, but what taste there is, is good. Tastes VERY similar--surprisingly similar--to puffed rice, just smaller... and not rice. Healthier than puffed rice in my strong opinion.It's not substantial enough for me to just eat it straight in milk for breakfast, but that's not what I bought it for. I think I'm like most people who purchase this, in that I bought it to augment other cereals. I add it to my Nature's Path Heritage flakes--which are very hard flakes, too hard, and the Millet being if anything 'too soft', kinda (?) balances that out sometimes. I like to mix different kinds of cereal, and this often gets thrown into the mix.Unlike the big-o box of Nature's Path Heritage flakes I bought, I'm not really sure I'll ever use all of this! Wow. I only bought it from Amazon because I couldn't find it anywhere else. The Heritage flakes have millet in them too, but it looks to be whole or cracked grain, not puffed--and apparently not even turned into millet flour, which is disappointing.As for the hulls, there are some but they haven't caused a problem for me. The hulls are a thin skin, almost the same color (very light brown or yellow), and in small pieces which I rarely if ever notice. I've also noticed that if you keep the cereal in the same vertical orientation, the hulls will, over time, migrate down. So if you're concerned (and you don't need to be), maybe put them in a plastic container, and keep topping off the container, so you're always drawing from the top.In retrospect, I'd like to see a millet-based cereal which is not puffed, and is not just hard pieces of whole millet, but uses ground/milled millet in some kind of creative form, even if it's a flake. Maybe I should start my own company.
Liked this product; seemed to have a little more body tochew on, where Puffed Rice has almost no body.

Once I go through the tedium of removing the hulls, the cereal is good. I mix the puffed grains with rice yogurt. But I cannot tolerate eating it with the hulls included. I feel like I am eating my parakeets' leftovers. I probably will not purchase any more millet.

I actually like this cereal more than the [N ..] organic brand because it is easier on my stomach- not sure why since this does not seem to be organic. However, note that this brand has a LOT of hulls which can spread and float around when you first open the bag. So beware and brush your teeth if you have anywhere special to go after consuming this. They will get stuck in your teeth.You might also want to keep tabs on this product's price which seems to fluctuate significantly. Right now, it is over $31 WAY TOO EXPENSIVE for puffs, especially considering this is not organic.

Great cereal, but it's not organic.  Neither my fresh package from a local store nor Arrowhead Mills' website labels this cereal as organic.  Either Amazon is getting product packaged especially for them, or the organic label on this listing is erroneous.

Why bother creating an alternative grain (that's naturally gluten-free) cereal that's NOT gluten free?!?!?  I bought this knowing millet is generally gluten-free... glad I did more research before I ate it!  Arrowhead Mills has other gluten-free products...  Why not this?  On the packaging, it also DOES NOT include an allergen warning as most food product do now that contain, tree nuts, soy, milk and wheat. Incomplete labeling. Oh well, what could be a great product is sadly not.

column9: Great cereal, enjoyable flavor/ texture!!!  But: any millet not good for digestive system patients
column10: I really love millet, and this cereal is a delight. Big bags, too!!  Arrowhead Mills are doing a good job! If you are looking for a good quality, healthy, weight loss-promoting whole grain that you don't need to cook - here it is.  Get it.Because I rely on reviews when shopping online, here a little warning: recently I found out that millet (in any form) can actually contribute to a pancreatic attack, gull bladder inflammation, it is not advisable for people with gastritis and other upper digestive problems.  A relative who has chronic pancreatitis, got very sick and a research revealed, that the culprit was a big millet cereal meal.  Myself, recently diagnosed with gullbladder & stomack problems, also have to cut down on how much millet i have - otherwise a lot of long-lasting pain is guaranteed...Be well!

Plain, Puffed millet cereal is the product for me, because it gives me the fullnes with long endurance to keep me strong most of the morning. I eat it with sugarless hemp milk and don't crave sugar. Fits in any diet and gives you well being satisfaction.
I love the whole grain (gluten free) puffed cereals. Especially with strawberries & stevia. Excellent cereal and hard to find for a good price at grocery stores (at least in my area).

We were introduced to Puffed Millet when we were traveling in Australia.  We were thrilled to find the product on Amazon and at such a great price.  The box arrived and we were astounded by how much there was.  The product is fresh and our 10 month old loves it as well.  Its great finger food for her to learn the fine motor skills on and it's healthy as well.  My wife likes to mix it into our cereal in the morning for a little extra texture.
No taste but it is easy to eat. It has to be mixed with other sweet cereal or fruits to make them more tasty.

column4: Ruth A. Reynols "book and movie enthusiast"
column9: good stuff for my grown up son!
column10: the puffed millet is what my son  loved when he was growing up - we couldnt find it around Little Rock so I got it from you - what a buy!!
My wife has Celiac and this product is one she can eat. She says it is munchy and great.
My favorite of the True *** products, I was very happy to find it in quantity to get the price down to what I felt comfortable paying per pack.

Strain (I use a coffee filter in a funnel) into another container, and store in the fridge for up to two weeks.  This is a concentrate, so when you pour a glass, mix it with an equal amount of water.If you enjoy iced coffee, please, PLEASE do not hot brew coffee and then cool it down.  It's like looking at a mediocre painting of a mountain range...you sit there looking at it, thinking you're enjoying yourself, with no idea that the actual mountains are at your back.  Turn around and realize what you've been missing: buy this coffee and cold brew it.

She was ecstatic when she received the Postum I purchaed through Amazon.com.

Can also be put into a cup of hot milk. And unfortunately this month discontinued by its manufacturer, Kraft, after 113 years on the market.

column9: What a retro piece of history-great stuff!
column10: Postum was a grain beverage that was the answer to coffee for people who didn't drink caffeine beverages.  My dad drank postum all the time for breakfast or weekends.  The great thing back in those days (1970s) was that even us kids (5 of us) would drink it with him.  It doesn't have that pungent coffee smell but it was soooo good to us kids.  A little milk and sugar made it look like a creamy cup of coffee, add a bagel and donut-YUMMY!. I drank it up until it was discontinued November of 2007.  What a real retro memory.

I decided to be brave, spend the 20 bucks after shipping and buy an 8 ounce bottle of the new release of Postum from [...]  I still have one unopened bottle of the original postum left in my pantry that I just cant bring myself to open,  so I compared at least the looks against the new one.  The new bottle, first of all is plastic.  Thats fine I have no problem with that,  that shouldn't effect the product. I noticed the color of the mix is a lot darker than the original Postum, almost like it has oil in it or is wet  and less "grain like" in its consistancy, more like  a fine sawdust. After comparing the two bottles side by side the moment of truth was now at hand.  I cracked the seal on the little white paper stuff that covered the top of the bottle.  To my suprise there was almost no smell. I do remember the original postum having a distinct smell when you stick you nose an inch or two from the bottle,  and this hardly had any odor to it.  I took my 1 spoonful of mix and dumped it into a hot cup of water.  It created a ton of foam as it mixed in,  which I dont rember the original doing.  I then poured my  small amount of milk in it, and it turned a very light color.  I added a touch of sugar and prepared for the taste.  the first sip was kind of flat.  I had to ask "did I put way to much milk in,  or not enough mix?"  well,  I finished most of the cup and found myself a little let down.  to me the first cup didnt seem like an exact match to the good old Postum of 2008.  Weak on aroma and a little weak on taste.  I will experiment alittle with the mixture and see if I can improve it,  but I probably won't be buying another bottle.  Were my expectations to high?  Maybe,  but if my memory of Postum is better than the real thing I think Ill stick with just the memory!

column9: A GOOD WAY TO AVOID CAFFEINE?
column10: For some people, excessive coffee consumption can pose health problems or it might just make it hard to sleep at night or give them the jitters. ENTER "Postum Caffeine Free Original, Instant Hot Beverage", which has been around since the end of the 19th century.With Postum, the usual mistake is simply to start drinking it in place of coffee. The sharp contrast in taste and lack of caffeine often makes this a solution doomed to failure. A better method is to add some Postum to your coffee or to have the "Postum" at night if you can take the caffeine during the day and simply let your body tell you how much caffeine you are okay about replacing in this manner.Of course, you could apply the same approach with decaffeinated coffee, so it is a matter of taste. By itself, however, I find "Postum" very bland and unsatisfying. Nevertheless, I attempt to replace some of my coffee consumption in this manner every five years or so.

column10: I went through New Braunfels not long ago, and I bought a jar of New Braunfels Smokehouse's Sweet Fire Pickles. All I can say is they are nothing short of amazing. Spicy and sweet, they are the perfect accompaniment for a barbecue, as a condiment in place of a relish, all by themselves - I think it's a surprisingly versatile food. Imagine candied jalapenos and bread-and-butter pickles together, and that's like what we have in this jar. If you're averse to spicy, this probably isn't for you - it's spicy. But the sweetness brings in an additional dimension, an added richness, and I always find myself wanting to have another taste. The sweetness doesn't diminish the spiciness, nor does the spiciness diminish the sweetness; but they both work together to make for a really robust combination of sensations and flavors. I can't help but think that a little bit of this on top of some cream cheese on a cracker would be all the better... the spiciness and sweetness of these pickles, the creaminess of the cream cheese, and the saltiness of the cracker would make for a real treat. Hmmmm... All we'd really need to add is a little bit of New Braunfels Smokehouse's bacon or maybe sausage or ham.Quite simply, this is my favorite pickle. And I'm almost all out of them...

Nothing makes these chicken breasts special whatsoever. They are standard generic tasting chicken breasts, tiny ones at that. They are tender and juicy when grilled, I will say that...but you'll be through eating one in less than 2 minutes. There's no difference between Omahas chicken breasts and regular chicken breasts I can buy in any grocery store Save a lot/Aldi included....for well over 1/2 the price of what they charge for these and for nearly quadruple the amount. So, why charge so much for these? I can get behind their steaks, even though they're overpriced too, and a few other Omaha products like the hot dogs and stuffed baked potatoes, but can't really get behind these chicken breasts. It's not like these are organic chicken breasts that have a decent size to them, which is what the price Omaha charges for them would suggest. These are as generic as generic gets. Would of been fine if 1 of their chicken breasts was the size of 2 of their chicken breasts. Instead it's like they got 1 large chicken breast and cut it it up to make 4 out of it. Luckily, I received these in a comped sampler. There's no reason whatsoever for anyone to buy just these chicken breasts through Omaha Steaks as Omaha gives you no reason to. Omaha really needs to make their portions bigger. People would be fine paying their prices if the portions were bigger...but half the things they sell the price to size ratio leaves you feeling ripped off. Not that I paid for these as like I said they were comped, but if I did no doubt I'd feel pretty ripped off. Change your mentality Omaha. Instead of less is more, think MORE is MORE. Get with the times.

These are wonderful.  They have packed with cranberries and taste great with mixed in the maple nut.  They are great to have on those busy morning when you don't have time for breakfast or you are just on the run.  They tie you over till lunch and you know you gave yourself something good.

Finally I found a lightly roasted coffee that is not too sour, bitter or otherwise unpleasant --- I am not a coffee drinker, but sometimes I enjoy a cup or two. I don't like Java roasts and do not enjoy the burned taste in general. This one is smooth enough for me to drink, but I do take it with milk, also sans sugar.

column9: Worst Coffee I Ever Tried To Drink
column10: Hey Tiny Footprint, light roast coffee beans are light brown; these beans are dark brown. There were mistakes made somewhere! This coffee is BLAH tasting, rather like dog pooh smells. In fact, this coffee is so bad I wouldn't let my dog drink it.Hey Amazon, the cabon negative story is appealing, but this coffee is a reject!

This coffee is for people like me who like a light-roasted (therefore presumably high caffeine), mild, smooth coffee. Those who like dark roasts propabably will not like this because a light flavor accompanies a light roast.Related issue for those who are concerned with "Fair Trade": I misread the extensive writeup of this coffee and so I did not notice that the words "Fair Trade" are neither in the description nor on the package. So, if that is the case, then it might be that this coffee is great for reducing the carbon footprint, but might not conform to fair trading standards for the peasant growers.

column9: This was not stovetop stuffing. I got hormel chkn meals ready to eat.
column10: At least it was chicken stuffing flavored. I expected chicken stuffing mix a whole 48 ounce container. What arrived was nasty tasting Hormel chicken n stuffing prepared microwave meals. 6 of them in case box at 10 ounces each. I have to say there was a large chunk of all white meat chicken in the middle of the disgusting mess though.
The Linden honey is fine texture, unique sweetness, and with an added aftertaste.  Works great in tea, over fruit ( mild acid)and on chicken--as you are to serve.

I LOVE Coffee, but for health reasons,decided to kick the habit.  I stumbled upon the the Teeccino Herbal Coffee (Medium roast- Hazelnut flavor), and found that I am in heaven.  It DOES NOT taste exactly like coffee, but can easily be used as a substitute.  I added brown sugar and Bailey's brand of Irish Creamer to it, and thoroughly enjoyed every sip.  I did not mix it with any regular coffee whatsoever, but instead decided to just try a cup of the product alone.  I must say, it is very DELICIOUS.  I am looking forward to trying some of the other flavors.  What I like even more about it, is that it is made with herbs and nuts; you can hardly go wrong with that!

Served on it's own, like straight black coffee, it's great.  However, I wouldn't recommend adding creamer, milk, sugar, etc., whatever you would normally add, as it tends to take Away from the taste.  If you really have to have a sweetener of some kind, try a hazelnut creamer, as it helps make it palatable to those who need a little sweet with their coffee.

I have tried Teeccino Hazelnut and , while it does not taste much like coffee, it is a great morning hot beverage. I use 2 tablespoons and make on mug of the brew and use some maple syrup sweetner. Yum.Many develop allergy to coffee and not just to caffeine but to some of the 300 other compounds in regular coffee. Beware of this.

While it didn't taste like hazelnut at all to me, I like this product. I just mixed it in with the regular unflavored. I find that I use a little over half the recommended amount per cup, and it suits me fine.

I read the good reviews on Teeccino java herbal coffee so I went to my local Whole Foods to purchase it.  They only had Teeccino original light roast herbal coffee.  I thought I'd try it anyway.  I wasn't expecting it to taste like coffee.  I was just looking for a hot beverage without caffeine, that tasted good.  I can't find the words to describe the awful flavor.  I made my daughter try it too to help describe the flavor.  She said "it smells like plastic".  I wasted my money buying this product!!

I have a 6yo in 1st grade. I introduced these to her by telling her it was like "applesauce in a Capr* S*n pouch" :) She was convinced to try it and now she requests them in her lunchbox on school days. That makes me a very happy mommy to know that she is getting omega 3s, protein, vitamins, and antioxidants in a yummy applesauce-like "snack." She is a fan of the other flavors, too. Sometimes if we are in a hurry I give her a pouch for breakfast on the go. If your child is used to sugary applesauces the flavor of this might take some getting used to, but it's worth it because these are so much healthier. I'm glad Amazon has them in these 16-packs because we go thru them fast! :)

column9: Not Just For Babies or Kids!
column10: I love love love, this flavor and this product.  I am a mom of two young kids and am constantly out and about.  I keep a few of these in my car and eat them up when I get hungry mid morning or mid day.  I also am a big runner and find that this is a great pre or post workout snack.  I love that it has antioxidants and protein packed.  I  am knocking on wood, but I am convinced that these little pouches of goodness are keeping me and my family healthy this winter.

I purchased these for my 18 month old son because he loves the other pouches that happybaby makes and I thought he would like these too. He will eat almost anything but he would not eat these. The other pouches they make have a screw on lid and a plastic spout and he can eat those all by himself with out making a mess. The first time he tried one of the Super Cinnamon ones it got everywhere and he only got half way through it before he refused to eat anymore. He wouldn't even try it the second time I offered it to him which made me curious so I tasted it. It tasted like cinnamon barf. I will have to throwaway the rest of the two boxes. I guess we will just stick with the Happy tot pouches like HAPPYBABY Happy Tot - Stage 4: Green Beans, Pears and Peas, 4.22  Ounce Pouch (Pack of 16) which I can not say enough good things about.

Baby loves this flavor, however, my baby (and I would assume most) would have issues with this one... My 15 month old has been sleeping through the night perfect for months now, until I started feeding her this(1 pouch a day) every other day or so. I'd give her the super banana flavor on other days. All of a sudden she started waking up during the night, multiple times, crying and just a plain wreck. After a couple nights like this my wife mentioned how the baby seemed to have a lot of gas lately. A few days more of this I was going crazy. I started looking at all the things we changed recently and came back to the happymorning foods I just recently bought. Started looking at the ingredients and nothing appeared out of the normal for the super banana flavor. Started looking this one over (super cinnamon) and the 2nd ingredient is PRUNES! My baby doesn't handle prunes well and she has been going through a very tough time lately because of this food. I stopped feeding her this flavor and all went back to normal. So again, just a warning for all.

We have bought Earth's Best organic baby food in a department store previously. After discovering our baby liked it, we went to amazon to compare prices and larger quantities.The baby food is great, no complaints at all. The packaging was sub par. The first thing we noticed was the exterior box wasnt taped or sealed ( It was a clamshell type box that folds over and you insert part of the box back into itself - anyone could have opened the package and closed it again). The jars are shrink wrapped with a cardboard base. The exterior packaging appears undamaged.Inside there were broken jars of food - and grocery items are not returnable. We have contacted Amazon's customer service and am waiting a response.

column9: Nice variety to stock up on.
column10: I wish I had ordered this pack sooner instead of one pack of one flavor. I like to use these to mix with some homemade foods too. I am happy with Amazon's "grocery" business. It is great to have the convenience to order these on-line and have home delivery.  I can't imagine going the store and having to get a whole case and go through check out. I try to make him some meals, but I trust Earth's Best and love the flavor combo's and they are so convenient.

column9: Great Price for Quality food for baby
column10: When I was pregnant I was sure I'd be one of those Moms who has both the time and inclination to make all her own baby food. And I did go that route for a while, until I realized how much money I was spending and how much food (once made) I was having to throw out. A friend had suggested Amazon Moms to me and we had already started getting our diapers via 'subscribe and save'. I decided to try this food and she loves it, I get other varieties than just the fruit and veggies, but my daughter enjoys all of them. I have even tasted most of them myself and they are fairly tasty.Plus the company is a heavy contributor to Sesame Street...so when you buy their products, you are helping out PBS as well. Win Win.
Arrived on time and in tact. Exactly as described. Used every bottle already. Would definitely buy these again. Great work.

As new parents we're also new to the baby food purchasing game.  We've tried a few, all organic, but our little girl definitely prefers the Earth's Best varieties.  We'd been purchasing them in the stores for over $1 a jar so this is a huge bargain for us.  As for those who say your baby doesn't need organic foods, yes it's true that a baby has a liver, but why tax it any more than it already will be through the years?

The price isn't better than you can find at Target or your local supermarket, but I guess it's good to get all your jars in one shot.  All of their jars taste really good and the variety is nice, including brown rice and peas and good fruits.  But shoot - for 80 cents a jar, you may as well buy a big thing of applesauce!

I got this when our baby was first starting solids and it lasted quite a while! I used it to supplement the food I was making and it did the trick. The only thing I would like to see is more unusual vegetables such as beets and spinach, but otherwise it was great!!! Love Earth's Best!!!
Signed up for the subscribe and save, And I am so impressed! My baby has loved all of the favors so far and they came in the mail very quickly. Great quality baby food, and cheaper than in the store.

column9: Good sampler at an economical price
column10: Our family (especially our nine-month-old daughter) is a fan of Earth's Best fruits and vegetables.  Having sampled a bit of each food in this sampler pack, I think it's worth noting that this brand tastes like the actual foods listed on the label, which cannot be said of some other brands we've tried, although they may be cheaper (the old adage is true - you really do get what you pay for sometimes).  In addition to the quality, this sampler offers a great variety of the fruits and vegetables, meaning you aren't stuck with a large quantity of any one item that baby might decide he or she doesn't like.  (And as parents, we've learned that baby can be exceptionally fickle.)  Although admittedly each child will have his or her own preferences, our daughter has enjoyed each of the fruit and vegetable types in this pack.  I would also highly recommend taking advantage of the Amazon subscribe & save pricing, as it makes the price much more economical than you'll likely find in a store (subscribe & save = approx. $0.81/jar, while stores in our area price the same size of jar at approx. $1 each).

I make my own baby food, but had these jarred foods shipped to our vacation destination since I couldn't bring my frozen food.  These were labeled as stage 2, so I assumed that meant they'd have a thicker consistency than water.  I was wrong.  My 8 month old wanted no part of these.
Amazing love these products. Just started making my own because it's cheaper, but if I wasn't, I would be buying these.
I use these products daily, several times a day for both my one year old and my two year old. They both love them. Great quality ingredients and the kids enjoy them, can't ask for more than that.
My lil' one LOVES Earth's Best foods. I love that it's ALL natural and organic. I highly recommend this product!
I love this baby food! My 9-month old loves it, plain, mixed with cereal, warm or cold.  I like the variety of flavors and appreciate that it is organic.  Highly recommended!

As far as I am concerned, this is the best baby food on the market, and my son loves eating every single variety. Very pleased with the quality and variety, I and will continue to purchase this until my son is old enough to eat solid foods.

I bought this for my teenage daughter's birthday because she is a PEZ freak!  She loved this giant dispenser.  I can imagine that PEZ dispenser collectors get a kick out of having the giant Betty Boop head in their collection!

I have ordered the Maple Almond Butter multiple times, and two times, I received a bad batch.  The first time (jars), Amazon (excellent customer service) refunded my money.  The second time (squeeze packs) I decided to contact Justin's directly via Facebook.  Justin's told me that a batch of plain almond butter had been packaged as maple almond butter and that I should send "Todd" an email and they would replace it.  I sent the email, but never got a response.  When you get a good batch, it is wonderful, but for this amount of money, I'd expect the quality control to be a lot better.  I think they may be growing too quickly and they can't maintain the quality with the faster pace of sales.  It's very disappointing because I like the product when I get a good, properly labeled batch.

I first tried this in a famous coffee shop.  They serve it on their bagels.  It tasted great and I was happy to find it online!  The only reason I only gave it 4 stars versus 5 was because it takes a whole lot of kneading of the packet to get it all out.  There are many times that I knead and knead the packet and still can't get the whole thing softened up.  All in all, I do like it though!  And the fact that it's portion controlled is a real plus!
It's a good thing I got the packets, because I would eat this stuff by the cupful if I'd gotten a jar of it.Very tasty. Smells wonderful. The maple taste is slight.

column9: Justin's Nut Butter Natural Maple Almond Butter 10 Count Squeeze Packs, 11.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3)
column10: OMG, SO AMAZINGLY SCRUMPTIOUS!!!!!!!!  I was so scared to try this because I am not a big fan of maple at all, but I love almond butter, and soy nut butter for that matter.  I went on a limb with this one and so glad that I did.  Such a rich flavor and you cant even taste the maple at all, there is just some sweet to it, but it is not a maple sweet at all.  So if you expect to taste maple, you wont be overwhelmed at all, cant even tell but it does add something that I have not been able to detect.  YUM YUM YUM, you wont regret buying this and love the individual sized packets, makes for portion control so you know how much you are getting and just the right amount.  Can take anywhere with you and I like to eat it just out of a pack.  You wont regret getting this product.

Justin's Nut Butter is the best almond butter you can buy.  I first learned about it an Starbuck's and I couldn't find it at any store.  So I looked it up on amazon.com and it was cheaper.  The order was quick and easy.

This. Is. Delicious. I wouldn't expect anything less, because almond butter is delicious and maple sugar is delicious, but man.  You won't be disappointed.I bring these to work and eat them straight. Yeah, I'm not embarrassed.

First, Justin's is the best almond butter ever. It's a joy to eat on anything.I wanted something for snacks/meals at work, and these are perfect. First you never need to worry about the oil separating out in the jar, since you squish each packet to combine before opening. Next you don't need a knife - the corner of the packet tears open easily and you can just squeeze it on to what ever you'd like. And if you only open one, it's automatic portion control.Last but not least, they make great mini-gifts for coworkers who've given you that coffee packet when you really needed it, or that paper plate when your lunch was leaking. Even better, you may get someone else hooked so you can split the order next time.

I tried this product looking for a tasty almond butter. After trying several other brands that were a waste of money, I discovered this one. It has excellent flavor plus there are no hydrogenated oils added to it. A clear cut winner! Don't need to search further, I have found the one I will be purchasing from now on. Excellent that it comes in packets - portion control. A good thing or I would eat too much out of the jar.

Like another reviewer said, it's a good thing this comes in measured amount packets--I would not be able to stop eating it from the jar!  Delicious.  I eat low carb and have eaten almond butter for quite awhile, but the maple adds just the right bit sweetness to make plain almond butter seem unappealing.  YUMMM!  And since I purchased this with Subscribe & Save the price isn't too bad.  Definitely recommend!

The Maple Almond Butter is incredible.  One of the best tasting foods I've ever had.  It is much better in the 1 oz pouches as you can simply eat it plain.  I started putting it on bagels and toast but the flavor of the butter gets masked by the food it is on.  My kids love it.  Easy to put in lunches.  Not to mention it is very healthy and organic.

My husband is allergic to so many things, that when we travel, it is a nightmare to find enough protein for him.  We discovered the whole slew of Justin's Nut Butter packs and keep them in stock at home.  You can put a ton of them in the plastic travel bags for carry-on's (under 3 oz. each) and eat them on the plane.  They are also great for sporting events, as they fit in a pocket of a purse or backpack easily!  Forget the $5 hotdog (which hubby can't eat) and eat a few of these packets instead!  My kids love them too!
Sliced cucumbers and a packet of Justin's Nut Butter Natural Maple Almond Butter makes a perfect healthy on-the-go snack. I love it and more importantly, my kids love it.
Love the single serving packets to throw in my purse when I go to work or in my backpack for a hike - no spoon needed!
I love these portion packs! They're too good though it's hard to stop at one! I would definitely recommend these guys!

column9: Almondy goodness but where's the maple?
column10: Usually I buy a tub of freshly ground, unsweetened, unsalted almond butter from the health food store. But when I need almond butter on-the-go, these single serve packs are great. As a diabetic, I love to spread it on wasa crackers for a healthy snack. Justin's maple almond butter is delicious, bursting with the taste of freshly roasted almonds. However, I detect no maple whatsoever. Almond is a strong flavor, so whatever maple is in there is overshadowed by it. Nonetheless, it is yummy. Hope they expand to include a crunchy version. This would get a 5 star rating from me if it had more of a maple flavor and a tad less salt. It tastes a bit too salty for me, but then I tend to eat unsalted nut butters.

Justin's Maple Almond Butter is the first flavor I tried, which I bought at Whole Foods. I was so glad to find it online because it is cheaper and the single serving packs are so great and easy to use. My favorite way of eating them is on apples which is great because I don't need to take the entire jar with me when I go to school. You won't regret buying these squeeze packs they are the best!

I love this stuff. Perfect for mornings or afternoons when you're rushed and need a quick something in your stomach - tastes soooo good, amazingly portable, I love it! Perfect for school, bike rides, hikes,etc. Just the right amount of sweetness too :)
Loving this stuff! great on crackers or straigt out of the package. having a hard time keeping my coworkers out of the box:)
Very glad I tried this product--it's a great snack with apples and will be very convenient at the office or in a lunch bag. It's slightly sweet and I think kids would enjoy it too.

I can't imagine anything being not good that involves maple. This just proves that to be true. The packets are fine to carry, but I finally discovered that there are indeed larger JARS with a lot more 'stuff' than in the packets for the money...also on a subscribe-and-save deal. NOW...if you would like this to be sweet(er) because it truly is not what I would call sweet, I would suggest that you might want to buy some of the Airborne Manuka and Wildflower Honey that is offered on Amazon. I left a review for that product as well. Combining two heaping spoonfuls of the manuka honey New Zealand Manuka with Wildflower Blend Honey 500g / 18oz with the organic maple almond butter and mixing well forms these two great products into something that is ridiculously (sinfully even) good! I like this mix with whole grain bread. It's a minor miracle to find a combination of super healthy (and organic) things that are this good.  I've been eating this honey for years and am delighted to find the protein-packed organic maple almond butter to go with it. Thanks, Amazon, for offering great organic foods that are still affordable!
These squeeze packs are so good for travel! Love the different flavors and Justin's keeps much better than other nut butters I've tried. Also good if you need portion control help.

Before this I have never had any nut butter besides peanut butter. This is a whole different experience! This Maple Almond Butter has a slightly heartier texture to it with a naturally sweet taste. In addition, the squeeze packs are perfect, providing a perfect serving to put in a sandwich, or a nice little snack to grab on the way out the door. Two thumbs up!!

column4: Emily Davis "Avid Reader of All Non-Fiction"
column10: If you're gluten intolerant like I am, these little packets of deliciousness are the answer to eating outside the home kitchen, when restaurant food seems just too 'iffy'.The taste is wonderful! I've tried the plain, the maple, and the chocolate, and the ease of carrying and eating them can't be beat!I carry a Justin's packet and gluten free crackers with me when we travel, and now I don't have to worry about being 'glutenized' when the waiter at the restaurant has clearly never ever heard the word 'gluten' before in his life, and the plain hamburger that I ordered (after I explained gluten to the waiter) comes on a big seedy bun - and all this when I've ordered from the "Gluten Free Menu" !!!!!!!!So - Thank You to Justin's Nut Butters  - I'll be ordering more of these ... YUM!YUM!

These squeeze packs are just awesome!  All of the flavors are great but this is one of my favorites.  These squeeze packs are convenient, well-portioned and easy-to-use.I use them when I'm biking, hiking, snowboarding, or just need a lunch on-the-go.  I recommend stocking the kitchen with the squeeze packs and the jars of all different flavors.
The maple almond butter squeeze packs are to die for! Absolutely delicious and super convenient! Definitely a great product for an athlete or anyone on the go looking for a quick protein fix!
This stuff is awesome on a wheat bagel, for a tasty and filling, yet light snack.  Love the flavor, as well as the texture!!!

column9: Try it once and you're hooked!
column10: A friend of mine in Boulder told me about delicious Justin's nut butters were, so I ordered some online. I was planning on just buying peanut butter, but when I saw that they had almond butter (which quite frankly I didn't know existed beforehand), I decided to try it out. Good bye peanut butter, almond butter is all I eat now. The honey almond butter is very good, but the maple almond butter is incredible. The squeeze packs are great for bringing along on-the-go. Can't wait for ski season - I'll be packing my jacket full of squeeze packs!

this sooooo good! we just squeeze it into our mouths, spoons be damned! all their nut butters are amazing. one day maybe it will be made from organic almonds. great texture when you mush it up. enjoy!

I've always loved almonds, but this is just so convenient for on-the-go snacking. Not only can I eat it while I'm hiking or camping, but it's also great for anywhere where I don't have to carry around a knife and jar (which is most places :) ).The taste is wonderful; one thing I've always disliked about nut butters was that they contained too much sugar. Justin's Almond butter has has only 4g of sugar, but it still tastes very sweet without going overboard. The palm fruit oil they use is also way more healthy than the palm kernel oil that most food products use, so that's great. I can put it on anything (like fruits) and it'll taste great, but I love putting it on bagels the most!Once you try this, you will NOT want to go back to any other types of almond nut butters!

I am a true peanut butter lover! I never really had almond or hazelnut butters until I tried Justin's and I am totally hooked! The flavors are amazing but even the classic peanut butter and almond butter are perfectly rich in taste. Also, the squeeze packs make my life 100 times easier for my on-the-go snacks at work.

Justin's Nut Butter is a great snack on the go with fruit or perfect for PBJ sandwiches. The protein in this product is perfect for vegetarians, fuel for someone on a long hike or in the fresh powder of the back country and for those of you just lounging around watching T.V. The taste is excellent and blows other nut butters out of the water! Love it!

I absolutely love Justin's Nut Butter!! Initially, I was a bit skeptical, but after trying the squeeze pack (which was a lot cheaper than the jar), I fell in love!! I usually use the squeeze packs when I'm on the go and need a healthy pick-me-up during the mid-afternoon slump.Believe me, TRY THIS STUFF! You won't go back.

I love all the Justin Nut Butters and this one and the peanut butter with honey are my favorites at the moment.  No waste, no mess, always fresh.This is such a brilliant idea, to have perfect portions in individual packets.  I have to watch every calorie and this keeps me from overdoing it.  The Maple Almond has a rich almond flavor with a not-overpowering but luscious hint of maple.  Your local health food grocery store probably has some Justin's packets.  Try a few and find your favorites.  I think then you'll be making sure you don't run out!  The jars are more economical but only if you really can keep yourself from overdoing it!  I think Justin's packets are the best healthy treats around.

I love all of the Justin's nut butters. My favorite is the almond maple but the peanut ones are also outstanding. When I first tried it I ate a third of the jar with just some saltines, it is that good. The packets are awesome for travel and they are fun. By far the best natural nut butters I have tried.

I've tried all of Justin's flavors and this one is definitely my favorite!  When I first started I was putting this on fruit and crackers, now I find myself eating this right out of the pack.  Just the right amount too!  Yumm.

Thank goodness for portion packets! One taste and you won't be able to put it down. I squeeze every last bit out of every packet. Almond butter is okay....but the not too sweet slight maple flavor of the maple almond butter is sublime. You will not be disappointed.I start most mornings with half a banana and half of a packet of almond butter before heading to the gym. It is a satisfying hold over until I come home from working out.

column9: The BEST almond butter out there
column10: I was never a fan of almond butter until I tried Justin's maple almond butter. Not bland, not too mapley, PERFECT. And the squeeze packs are great for portion control. I like to eat this on toast in the morning before class.
love, love, LOVE this stuff.  can't wait until Amazon carries the 100 calorie packs, as they make it much easier to enjoy it as a snack without overdoing the fat and calories.
It shipped quickly.  The taste is perfect.  I'm going to use in in a truffled potato mushroom gratin.  It's everything it claims to be.
Looked for something other than chocolate and found these organic cookies which were well received by the grandchildren.  Would certainly look at this seller again.
This was purchased as a gift.  My sister said they tasted very good and were really cute.  However, for the $$ you pay, she only got 8 cookies.

I didn't get a chance to sample these organic cookies myself, but I sent a box to my sister in law as an advance Easter pick-me-up surprise and they have been a phenomenal hit. The cookies are delicious and look great, and  Beautiful Sweets has a whole variety of themes for year-round occasions.One very minor issue, I wish the product page had specific information about shipping times. It took Beautiful Sweets about a week to ship my order; there's nothing wrong with that, but it would just be nice to know, especially when you're used to Amazon shipping everything so quickly.On the positive side, they emailed with tracking number as soon as the package shipped.I will definitely be ordering more from Beautiful Sweets in the future. Sister In Law doesn't know it yet, but she's getting the Halloween special!

These aren't the hard candies with the gooey center we all love.  I was so disappointed when I ate one and it tasted like bubble gum.  when I see the strawberry wrapper I expect the arcor brand candy and I can't believe people get away with this false advertisement.
I should have read the prior reviews because they captured my opinion exaactly. The gooy stuff inside one of the candies from a few years ago could supply a days production run today.

I've been looking for the strawberry bonbons of my youth, and, unfortunately, these didn't quite make it. This particular variety of bonbon has a strong banana flavor, overriding the pure strawberry goodness. I've also get the occasional impression that I'm sucking on a salt lick with these things. Now strawberry-fidelity aside, these bonbons are still pretty good.
product arrived on time in perfect condition exactly as described. These are the best hard candies we have ordered. Cannot find them anywhere in the retail world.

These buns are spectacular, and I feel sorry for anyone who just rips the package open, slaps a hot dog in, and takes a bite. To be edible, they *must* be heated in the microwave until they're hot to the touch. I usually heat mine on a plate I've splashed with a tiny bit of water. Or sometimes I'll try flicking just a bit of water onto the buns themselves before heating (you can easily overdo it).Done properly, they're awfully close to the real thing. Which is an amazing treat if you can't have gluten.***UPDATE***I've found that if you *really* want these to turn out well, steaming them is the way to go. My current favorite approach is to put a layer of water in a big pan, put the hot dogs in the water, stick a steaming insert above the water, put the buns in the insert, and then simmer everything for about ten minutes. The buns can get a bit *too* damp on the outside, but they'll be soft and tasty. Play around with it, experiment a bit, and you should be able to find the softness/moistness balance which makes you happy.

My dad started selling these traps in the 1950s. They originally were a treated wood but eventually they would get chewed on by gophers (revenge motivated), stolen by fox, or decayed by weather (forgotten for months). They sold for $3 each or so much a case. In our area a bounty was paid for the tail (today its at $3 each). I had at one time 12 traps and made some good money trapping gophers. Over the years, I've trapped hundreds of the little bastxxs. Why the hatred? Pocket gophers will eat your garden alive, drop 8' Norway pines, ruin your lawn and destroy underground electric wires. What's worse, if you let them be, the fox and badgers will come in to get them and then you'll see what real dirt moving and destruction means. A war zone!This new plastic version works as well and doesn't get damaged by weather but costs significantly more than other open trap types. However, they work better than any other trap I've used as they are easy to set, no wounded gophers (never seen a live one yet)and will get the gopher 4 out of 5 times. That said, here's some observations:1. To find a gopher run, take a pointed steel rod (I have one with a cross handle on the top and a stepping bar on one side toward the bottom). Go around the outside of the latest gopher mound inserting the rod 6-12" into the ground and about 12" apart. When the rod "falls" through the ground after initial insertion, you've found the tunnel. Take a square head spade and dig a square hole , flat bottom, with the tunnel at either or both ends. (Use two traps or seal one tunnel if your in the middle of a run). Butt the set trap up tight against the tunnel. Lightly cover the top of the trap with dirt (grass over the tiny gaps where the metal parts enter the trap, then dirt). Not too much as it will eventually interfer with the spring strength. Leave the hole open at the end (I've caught many gophers with the air hole closed too, especially if the trap is in a runway - tunnel going both ways).2. You may catch the gopher fairly quick but I leave traps overnight before moving them. If the trap doesn't get tripped after a day, there is a 90% chance its plugged with dirt. If full of dirt, reset. However, each time its plugged, the chance of trapping the gopher (they get smarter each time) is significantly reduced. After plugged twice, your chance of catching him there is near zero. Move the trap to another portion of their maze and try again.3. Wear old, worn gloves so you leave no scent. I've never washed a trap after a dead gopher though.4. To remove a dead gopher, take the box trap, turn it on end over the garbage, hold the spring bar down and shake hard. The gopher will pop out. (A little messy but it works in rural areas...Take the dead gopher and fling him in the middle of the yard. I've never had a gopher still there the next day as many, many other animals love gophers for a decent meal. Is this green or what??)5. Don't settle for just one gopher. I always reset the trap into the same hole and its 50/50 you'll catch another. If you think you have them all, remove the trap and leave the tunnel open. If it fills back up after a day, there's more in the maze.6. Gophers love easy digging so they will follow easy digging directions. Unfortunately underground electric wire make for easy digging and a gopher will follow the wire. For some reason (revenge again?) they will chew on the plastic wire coating as the enjoy the easy digging. Weeks or months later when a wire nick corrodes and when the lights go off, you'll know they were busy.7. If you have fox, coyote or badgers in the area, stake your trap down with chain and an anchor. If not, a predator will gladly remove the dead gopher but unfortunately with your trap. And you'll never see the trap again.8. With minimal care (flag so you don't forget where your traps are and anchor when necessary)these traps will last almost forever. I'm still using an original wood box trap from the 1960s. All beat up but still catches gophers.If catching gophers with minimal effort is the goal, you can't go wrong with this proven box design. Good hunting!

I usually do not write reviews on Amazon (or anywhere else for that matter), but I really have to make an exception in this case because of how well this device works.  It is rare for any device to work exactly as expected, but the Victor Blackbox Gopher Trap works above and beyond any expectations that I had for it.  I do not work for the Victor company, and I have no financial stake in the sales of their products.  I am simply an exasperated homeowner who got fed up wih gophers tearing up his property and decided to give this device a try.I had used poison pellets, smoke bombs, water hose, and those silly sonic devices... nothing worked and those gophers were probably laughing at me.  With the Blackbox, it's nearly a sure thing.  Also, you actually get to see the results with a dead gopher right in front of you, unlike smoke bombs and poison which are always a guessing game as to whether or not they actually did their job.Within 2 day of getting this product, I had already caught 3 gophers.  One of those gophers was caught less than 1 hour after I set the trap.  Free lunch on my property is now officially over.The key to the effectiveness of this trap is to find a freshly dug up gopher mound.My sure kill method:1) Find a freshly dug up gopher mound.2) Dig out the mound until you find the tunnel.3) Place the activated trap flush with the entrance of the tunnel, with the small round hole (on one side of the trap) facing outward.4) Cover up the gaps at the top, sides and bottom of the trap with dirt so that it looks like the tunnel extends into the Blackbox, but make sure the opening to the trap is unobstructed from inside their tunnel.The idea is to make the trap seem like an extension of the gopher's tunnel, and by instinct the gopher will head towards that small open hole on the other side of the trap to plug it up (they don't like any openings into their tunnels).  Once he enters the trap, it's goodnight Gracie.  This trap is so strong that the gopher will be nearly snapped in half.Before getting the Blackbox, I had also tried using a "Macabee" gopher trap (the one with the 2 pincers that snap together) but the gopher simply pushed that trap out of his tunnel.  The Macabee is also a lot more risky to use and harder to set (in terms of triggering it accidentally on your hand).  The Blackbox is safer to use and much easier to set because the trigger mechanism and the killing device is contained fully within the box itself.  The Macabee trap can also be dragged away by a dying gopher if it is not properly secured.  There is definitely no chance of a gopher dragging away a Blackbox.In summary, I wish I had used the Blackbox from the beginning.  It would have saved me a lot of time, money, frustration and parts of my yard.UPDATE Aug-17-2011:  I have just posted some pics as proof of the effectiveness of this device.  After 13 captures within the first 4 months of use, I have not seen any more gopher activity since April 2011. I guess word got out in the gopher community that there is now a steep price of admission onto this property.

I had struggled with gas bombs, flooding & metal traps.  These work....in time.  I'm far too impatient & frustated by seeing my yard destroyed while gophers out smart the above methods.  The Victor black box has been great!  I have a 100% kill rate for the last 2 weeks and generally get my gopher within 4 hrs of placing the trap.  Also, you can see if the trap has been tripped without disturbing the trap.  Unlike the metal jaw style trap, where I had to trip it when pulling it out of the hole (because most of the time I had nothing.)  I put a little bit of carrot in the bait hole in the back of the box & so far, I'm very happy.This trap appears more humane in terms of a rapid kill (snaps the spine) & it less messy as the gopher doesn't have any wounds to deal with.  It's worth the money.  There is no way you are going to lose this thing underground either.

column9: Works GREAT - you HAVE TO follow the instructions - read on
column10: Have had serious gopher problems for YEARS.  Most effective up to this point have been (for me) the "smoke bombs".  those cost about $7 for 4 of them, and for them to be successful I needed to locate about 10 or so holes, make sure they did follow a tunnel and them bomb them all at one time.
