It was somewhat effective, and with no bodies to account for you never really knew.THESE TRAPS HOWEVER:  WORK GREATIve never liked traps because theyd say something like "find the main gopher tunnel, and then place it in there...etc"  And Id think "ya right, point ONE out to me and Id be GLAD to do just that..."Ive killed 4 gophers so far using these traps.  Two yesterday, and one so far today (=3 dead gophers) and one a couple days ago...What I have found effective SO FAR (still getting the "hang of it") is to EITHER:1) find an OPEN HOLE and use a stick and "TRY TO" determine which direction it leads, and THEN dig an opening in that direction about 1-2 feet AWAY from its opening large enough to put TWO of these traps inside it BACK TO BACK.  THEN (set the traps) put them inside, cover up ALL the holes so NO LIGHT PASSES INTO the tunnel.  And WAIT - come back in an hour Im sure MOST LIKELY you got one!  no kidding, see my uploaded pictures.Ive gotten 1 this way2) IF YOU FIND A HOLE THAT IS CLOSED / PLUGGED **AND** THE DIRT PLUGGING IT IS "POWDERY" (is literally the consistency of powder) THEN (most likely) a gopher is INSIDE THAT TUNNEL.In THIS SCENARIO put ONE TRAP facing INTO the tunnel, cover up all holes so NO LIGHT can enter.  Come back in about an hour, or the next day (for me 1 hour is suffice) AND *ALMOST CERTAIN* YOU CAUGHT ONE!  no kidding, Ive gotten 3 this way (1 yesterday, one today within 1 hour of setting this trap this way).ONE THING TO CONSIDER ALSO: THREE GOPHERS SO FAR were not dead when I pulled the traps out of the ground so I had to kill them myself... they were hurt but no way dead - all others were dead (fyi)AND A NICE POINT / IN ADDITION:IF you see the spring portion UP IN THE AIR when you approach your trap after youve set it in place, this means 100% you caught a gopher.  SPRINGS UP = CAUGHT GOPHERFINAL POINT / IN CONCLUSION:GREAT TRAPS! THEY WORK BY FAR THE BEST OUT OF ANYTHING IVE TRIED SO FAR... BY FARGREAT GREAT TRAPS!remember find and ACTIVE HOLE, and set them in there using the methods above and YOU WILL kill gophers!GREAT TRAPS, wish I knew of them 15 years ago!I hope this review helps! I think these traps work GREAT**update**killed 22 gophers so far (as of 06-29-12)1 4-5-12 gopher leaving tunnel2 4-8-12 (one of these was killed using 2 traps back to back when gopher was re-entering the hole, the other gopher leaving tunnel)1 4-9-12 gopher leaving tunnel1 4-10-12 gopher leaving tunnel1 4-11-12 gopher leaving tunnel2 4-12-12 gophers leaving (separate) tunnels1 4-14-12 gopher leaving tunnel2 4-21-12 gopher inside tunnel / leaving tunnel - one was caught in SAME TUNNEL as previous caught 4-12-12.  The second today was caught in a different area of the yard when my foot sank into the ground, I dug the area and found a large "fresh" looking tunnel - within 2 hours I checked back (daily routine) and caught a gopher - took pictures and uploaded them, set the trap and within 2 hours caught a gopher1 4-25-12 gopher inside tunnel / leaving tunnel - one trap near opening, inside tunnel1 4-28-12 gopher leaving tunnel1 4-03-12 gopher leaving tunnel / 2nd kill SAME tunnel - took about 7-8 days, left trap in tunel, surprised to have caught another in the SAME tunnel (about 7-8 days later)1 5-05-12 gopher leaving tunnel - saw a fresh / new hole back filled with LOOSE / POWDERY dirt, set trap, about 6 hours later (I check every couple-few hours regularly) CAUGHT GOPHER #151 5-6-12 (same tunnel / hole as #15... there was no other hole to set this trap in, so I reset it in the same hole2 5-9-12 gopher within tunnel AND the second gopher THIS day was same tunnel as #15 and #16 (3rd gopher in SAME TUNNEL) 18 gophers so far1 5-12-12 gopher inside tunnel - used two traps1 5-18-12 GOPHER #20!!!  :-)  gopher inside tunnel... was walking and heel sank, dug into ground and found hole, set ONE TRAP, a few hours later was on the computer looked out window and saw the spring was up in the air (only means ONE thing) = caught gopher #20 - happy happy day (see uploaded pic)1 6-3-12 gopher inside tunnel - was leaving tunnel - saw a new / fresh powdery dirt plugged hole and set trap - next day spring was up1 6-29-12 OLD TUNNEL, two traps had been in their for a couple weeks and I never took them out, today ONE of the springs was up, caught another one a small one but a dead one (gopher #22)WHAT IVE LEARNED AFTER KILLING 22 GOPHERS:It *SEEMS* as if each gopher has its own set of tunnels which ARE NOT shared by other gophers... (W/ FEW Exceptions that is).  Gophers went unchecked / ignored and RUINED our entire yard, and front of house - HUGE "gulleys and VERY uneven ground is what remains, you walk around out there and sometimes your entire foot sinks to your ankle...After having caught a gopher in pretty much most of the tunneled areas, NONE have come back so far... SO FARBUT:  IT DOES SEEM as if each gopher has its own tunnel system.  I have ONLY caught gophers in different tunnels areas, NEVER in the same tunnel system / area.It just seems this way, and like mentioned none have come back as of yet, and I am going to be digging into ALL tunnels and back filling them with dirt... of course THEN EVEN MORE SO a new opening / entrance will mean an active tunnel - this was how I caught my 9th gopher... it dug a hole and then back filled its opening, then later below it on a hill, it dug another and I could see its head shooting in and out throwing out dirt - I stood over witha shovel and made eye contact... I then came back in about 10 min and set a trap in the FIRST backfilled hole, about 45 min later I checked and the spring had popped up - caught that gopher #9ALSO - and END OF THIS POST (for now) - 8 of 9 gophers only ONE TRAP was used, saw a fresh hole which was plugged from the inside, which I also now know / feel means it is an active hole / tunnel - set ONE TRAP FOR WHEN IT LEFT - 8 out of 9 kills went THIS WAYI CAUGHT ONLY ONE GOPHER USING TWO TRAPS BACK TO BACK:  gopher hole was OPEN, I dug infront of it about 1-2 feet, set TWO traps and the gopher was caught on the way back inMY CONCLUSION:  if a hole is OPEN set two, and youll most likely catch it upon its re entranceIf a hole looks fresh, and plugged, dig it open wide enough to set one trap, then WAIT, just go about your day, and come back later, almost certain you caught one if its an active hole"ACTIVE HOLE" = a hole that is OPEN or PLUGGED FROM THE INSIDE and the dirt that is plugging it is POWDERY *NOT* compacted like the desert ground all cracked looking, it will look like fresh dirt was used to plug it VERY RECENTLY meaning that SAME DAYtake all of this info and use it, it worked for me!  8 out of 9 were killed using ONE TRAP when the gopher was LEAVING its tunnel - I literally destroyed its opening by digging it open with a shovel, the felt for a hole, found the tunnel using a stick made sure it went on for some ways, then I set a trap butted up against the opening that I widened - used some leaves to cover the holes in the set trap, sprinkled loose dirt lightly and MADE SURE NO LIGHT ENTERED FROM OUTSIDE INTO THE TUNNEL - then waited / went about my day - EVERY TIME SPRING WAS UP = caught gopher.  3 of 9 werent dead had to kill myself, but they were caught in the trap.  The sprung trap makes a very nice and ironically convenient handle to just grab and removed the whole thing from the ground with the butt of the gopher staring you in the face when you pull it up - you NEVER even have to touch the gopher, I never cleaned mine off, just reset the spring and reused the trap - if it was an "active hole" I caught anotherSIMPLE SIMPLE SIMPLEgood luck!***ALSO see my uploaded pictures

column9: works great for Florida Pocket Gophers
column10: My first suggestion is to make sure of what exact pest is digging up your yard. My husband and I had first thought these mounds or hills were made by moles, or maybe armadillos, and after research for local yard problems, found they were made by the Southeastern Pocket Gopher. We have the other 2 pests here too, but their habits are different, and we'll have to get something else for the moles.We had tried everything to repel or remove this critter, and finally ordered one of these traps after reading good reviews here. To my great surprise, we got the pesky Pocket Gopher the very next morning after setting the trap. We did use the carrot trick at the back of the trap, as shown on the instructions.So much damage was done to our yard and shrubs, and it appears it was just this one pocket gopher all along. But if another one moves in, we will be prepared with this Victor Black Box trap. Very satisfied customer!

I remember my dad using a similar item (made of wood) years ago to keep our yard gopher free. The new generation Black Box is plastic, but works just as well. The snare is very strong and seems to do its job very quickly (at least none of the gophers have been alive when I've gotten to them). Once tripped, it requires a bit of muscle to release the spring and a little shaking to get the gopher out, but that's just a testament to its effectiveness. I hate to kill these little guys, but they're destroying my yard! The Black Box is a a definite Gopher Getter.

This trap works the best, built very well and solid.  Just make sure you set the trap at the last or most recent gopher mound.  Once set, the gopher is usually trapped within the next 12 - 48 hours.  If it doesn't, then you probably didn't get the right gopher mound or the trap was not in the proper direction.  The trap with the little hole at the end, needs to be like an exit, as if the gopher was trying to push the dirt out to close the hole.  Once the gopher goes into the "Black Box" and tries to push dirt up into the little hole...  "SNAP!" the trap grabs the gopher and holds it in the trap.  Good luck!

I live in Washington state where there are quite a bit of gophers roaming around. My father's been having troubles with them in his yard for years. So I've been trying to find the best trap for him to use. I came on Amazon to find some and just bought a bunch. One of them my father said worked relatively well was this one. It has a good design and an alright killing speed. Though he said the absolute best was Black Hole Rodent Trap. He says it's definitely worth the extra dollars. He absolutely loves it.

column9: Very effective trap; caught one in less than 30 minutes
column10: This year we have rodent problems, mice in our front lawn and a pocket gopher in our backyard.  The backyard is where we grow vegetables and it has become our pocket gopher's heaven!  The mouse traps are pretty effective in catching mice in the front lawn.  But for the resident in our backyard, we've been outsmarted in more ways than one.  The gopher came out to munch on my plants at night and each morning I found another dead plant.  We've tried everything under the sun including a professional exterminator but all to no avail.  I wanted to get the Black Hole traps or Macabee traps but they were not available in this part of Canada.  I was about to throw in the towel when I saw this BlackBox.  I was very skeptical at first but I really didn't have anything to lose so I decided to battle the gopher one last time.I got two traps in a local store yesterday then came here to read the reviews.  Thanks to those reviewers who shared their experience in such detail that I was pretty confident when it came to to setting up my trap.I found a new mound and a new hole in our vegetable garden this morning, blood went straight to my head and I began to dig down like MAD.  I found a one-way tunnel that came from outside our fence.  I set one single trap there, following the directions of a couple of reviewers here (big thanks).  I covered the trap with loose leafs and a bit of dirt then I went to plug the mouse holes in the front lawn.  When I was still plugging holes I heard a "thud" and my heart jumped!  It was not even 30 minutes after the trap was set, could that be??When I got to the trap I found the trigger lever up and something was struggling inside the housing!  I didn't want to pull it up immediately hoping the rodent would die in a few minutes.  Unfortunately the spring was not strong enough to kill the gopher at first snap.  To me, digging the tunnel was work, setting the trap was easy, but killing the gopher was difficult.  But I really had no choice.  If I let that thing go it would come back and tear up the rest of our garden.  So it got to die!The pocket gopher was not very big, about 6.5" in length tail not included.  It got tiny eyes and very long teeth and claws.  The gopher got cheek pouches to store food and there was still a bit of green left in one of its cheeks when it was killed.Since the tunnel came from outside our fence I reset the trap just in case someone else decides to move in.  Overall I am very happy with this trap.  The design is simple but this little trap performs better than those exterminators come with big price tags.My only complaint about this trap is the instruction, or the lack of it.  There is a  brief instruction printed on the box without details.  If Victor could provide one single sheet with printed diagrams to go with written instructions that would be nice.This trap is pretty safe to use and there's very little chance to catch a finger inside the housing.  However, once the trap is set you must be very careful when moving it around. One of my traps is more sensitive than the other. The first time I set up the sensitive trap and tried to move it inside the tunnel, I was not paying attention and the spring was trigger.  The metal lever sprang up and hit my ring finger! Fortunately nothing was broken, just a big bruise.  I have uploaded a few pictures of the captured gopher.  Revenge is sweet!Overall, I am very pleased with this product.  This trap definitely deserves 4.5 stars!

For over 20 years we have tried traps and at first when we moved out here we were new to these things and I tried running water to drown them. (LOL) Well, we all know that is just costly at the end of the month. Then I ran across a person on here 88Ronin who had detailed, step by step instructions on how to do it and he had me convinced that even I could do it. I was petrified to set the trap and asked him questions, (several) and he walked me through it. I have successfully caught 5 gophers within 2 weeks. I had to get my husband to remove the carcass. I bought poison too, but I have four dogs and one of them likes to hunt the gophers, so I was a little worried about poisoning my own pets. And this is way less inhumane. AND It is quick. So all of you that are against killing these over-sized rats, they are not only pests, they make huge holes in your yards, land, and garden. So if you have horses, animals, or kids that like to run and play, get ready to either shoot them or take them to a ER. Their legs to go through the holes and they will snap. They also tear up your lawn, and eats up your food in the garden.I can tell you what I did. Found the freshest hole and I ran water to get the hole opened. I peeled back our grass to make the hole bigger and placed the black box down inside and sprinkled dirt back on top of it and left just the little hole at the end open. They will come through to start covering that hole up. But, I suggest you to look up the reviews on here and find 88ronin's review. He has a detailed excellent way to get'em. I wouldn't have got even one without his help.Goodluck

column9: Death Comes Quickly to the Pesky Gopher.
column10: This gopher trap was effective.  I placed this in a tunnel the day I received it and when I checked the tunnel 24 hours later the gopher was dead in the trap.  You will need to do some personal preparation before you place the trap. I first watched some videos on youtube on how to find gopher tunnels and then how to place the trap and then made sure I knew where the gopher tunnels were at.To find the great videos by UC San Diego on how to do this, go to youtube and search "pocket gophers finding tunnel systems".  It should be the first video.  Watch the other video they have on how to place a trap. Once you've done this you are ready to go kill the gopher.  While others have said to handle it with gloves, I did not and the trap was quite effective anyways.One warning, when using a trap you need to know that the death of the gopher is not sugar coated as with poisons.  You will see the dead gopher up close and personal and will have to release the trap to get the gopher out of it.However, if your goal is to get rid of a gopher as soon as possible, you can't go wrong with this trap.

We live in the country where there are a LOT of gophers, moles, voles, etc. I have tried several gopher traps and had a success rate of about 1 in 5 settings.....and with a lot of work trying to fool the critters. But, the Black Box caught 2 of my problem gophers (they were killing our trees) in 3 settings. And I didn't have to try to fool the trap shy beasts. The Black Box gopher trap is a fantastic tool for getting rid og gophers.

I finally got the big fat gopher that has been ruining my garden. We dug down where I saw the activity and found the hole. We set the trap with no bait, covered it up and within a 1/2 hour he was caught. This trap works.Victor 0625 The BlackBox Gopher Trap

Gophers ate up half my garden.  I bought this thing and WHAMMO!  I set it in the afternoon and the next morning my nemesis was in gopher heaven except I am pretty sure gophers don't go to heaven but to the other place.

Yeah, this gopher trap is pretty amazing!I have a terrible gopher infestation and I had been using the wire Macabee style traps for about two months. I had been using the Macabee traps exactly as instructed but the success rate was very low with them. If I was lucky, I might catch one or two gophers a week.I would spend a ridiculous amount of time every day setting up the Macabee traps just to find them buried by gophers the next day. It is incredibly frustrating because you can't just look at a Macabee trap to see if it has been sprung. You have to completely pull them up and check everything and then reset everything all over again.With the blackbox I've had a 100% success rate so far! I've caught a gopher every single day for the past four days and I suspect that I'll keep up this pace until I've decimated the gopher population for my entire neighborhood!This trap is WAY BETTER than the Macabee style traps. The Macabee traps say "easy set" on them. HA! What a joke! The black box is much easier to set and is much more powerful so it kills more humanely. I've had Macabee traps complete eviscerate gophers but somehow leave them alive to die painfully. I've had nothing but quick and clean kills with this blackbox.It is also much easier to "release" the dead gopher from the blackbox than with the macabee traps since the blackbox always leaves the rodent in one piece.Oh and my favorite part of the blackbox is that you can actually walk right up to it and look at it to see if it has been sprung, unlike the macabee traps which requires them to be pulled out to check on them.*UPDATE*On Day 5 of owning this trap, I killed 4 gophers in a single day with a single trap!

These traps are the best.  I used to have a wooden one but kept losing the trigger wire.  When I did use it I used it in combination with one of the little metal spring traps (putting one each direction in the runway).  This was a successful means of killing gophers until one day the metal trap disappeared into the ground and I never have found it.  I even had it tethered to a stake.  This was one tough gopher.  The nice thing about the box trap is that it stops them cold and they don't move after it is triggered.  They are toast.I purchased two of these Victor 0625 Blackbox Gopher Traps.  They are very durable, made of very heavy, dense plastic plastic.  I put one in each direction in the runway and catch them every time.This is a very effective gopher trap and I highly recommend it.

My boyfriend set up the traps in the backyard, two traps back to back (like the box recommends), and we caught one 3 hours later. He said the gopher didn't look very happy when he took care of the trap, so these are probably not what you are looking for if that bothers you. I let him do it, and try not to think about it too much.They work though!

It was a LONG battle with gophers in our backyard.Trust me I'm all for repellents and humane methods of prevention. But just as one reviewer said, you'll end up with "big fat organically fed gophers". If you have gophers it's a WAR, and don't take hostages, you want them dead!1. We'd tried spinners(the guy in the nursery had sworn by it) but as my husband said "the only way this might work is if gophers die of laughter". Well, they didn't die or left the yard but I'm sure they laughed at us, because we would find two new mounds every morning. At least kids enjoy having noisy spinners in the yard:)).2. Step two was "The Giant Destroyer Gas Bomb" which seemed to work for a few days. Then we would find another mound, not so big though! We tried to smoke them again, making sure we put a bomb in each hole in the ground we could find. Then quiet for a few days, yet again a tiny mound appeared one morning. That was it.3. My husband put this trap in the ground and.... the very next morning I was happy as any predator can be. I didn't know I'd be so excited to see a dead creature.  At the same time I was happy I didn't have to deal with the trap and dead gopher, my husband disposed it. Hopefully it was the only one that was left. We'll keep the trap for a couple of days, to make sure nobody comes back.Some details on how we set the trap. I thought it wouldn't be trivial but to my surprise it was.If you have a mound on your lawn, using a flat spade cut out a square peace of the  grass with roots about 6 inches deep and a bit over 1 sq.foot right where the mound is. You'll see a little tunnel, set the trap in the tunnel and cover with the grass. Check it daily.Good luck!Usually I'm a very peaceful person but when your garden is being destroyed right in front of you..., sorry, no mercy:  !

column9: Works like magic for a novice
column10: I'm not agriculturally proficient at all, and rather not deal w/ dead critters. But I just couldn't stand the backyard full of gopher hills, and wanted to give this a try. I've been flooding the holes, and noticed one hole that kept on getting filled back up every day or so. So I set the trap (i still wasn't sure it I followed the directions or not), and the next morning... Let's just say that I haven't seen any new hole for the past week or so. This one really works well, just follow one of the reviewers directions, and you'll get you yard and sanity back in no time.
After trying other types of gopher traps at a particular gopher hole, I was finally successful using this box trap.

column9: These traps work better than expected
column10: After reading other articles on gardening forums regarding the difficulty of getting rod of gophers I was not sure of how effective these traps would be. I learned of them through a gardening forum post.  I thought I'd give them a try.  I nailed three gophers out of 4 trap sets in my first two days! Using only two traps. The only trap set that did not catch was set back in the same hole as the first catch. Package instructions say to try placing back in the same hole as a kill for up to 3 more days to catch others.  I have so many mounds I'm just moving to fresh ones each day. Low-hanging fruit, so to speak. The traps are very sturdy and well made, and I like the very quick kill.  I'm not interested in poisoning animals or slow kills.  These work so well I am buying 2 more for a total of 4.  I have 2 acres which are gopher ridden.  Soon they will be rid. Highly recommended!

column9: the ONLY thing that has worked fo rme
column10: I had just moved into my new home, only to find that there were some pests waiting for me. Within a couple of weeks the new lawn was being dug up like crazy by moles.  Like most people, I went the non-lethal route of sonic spikes, pellets that are supposed to make the dirt smell/taste bad, etc etc.After reading the reviews on Amazon, I decided to give it a try and purchased 2 - one for the front yard and one for the back.  Within a day, I had already caught the first mole in the back.  Thankfully, it appears that was the only one.In the front yard, it took a little more effort. The mole would keep pushing dirt into the trap and setting it off. Based upon a recommendation from a friend, I smeared some almond butter (any nut butter would work) on the inside of the back of the trap.  The next morning, the only thing the trap was filled with was dead mole.I highly highly recommend these traps. They are literally the ONLY thing that has caught and killed the pests. Don't waste your money on other traps or oils or pellets or spikes.

I had a couple of gophers tearing up my lawn and was looking for traps. Saw the reviews on this item and decided to give them a try. Set the traps as instructed and caught both gophers in the same evening. They work!!
Item was listed as gopher- mole trap. Really is designed for gophers. I feel mislead on this item. However it should work well for gophers. Not really designed for moles.

The trap work very good, got the two pocket Gophers that were in my orchard in a few hours. I would like to see a little better design  on the trap so that it kills quicker, but it works very good and is easy to set.

We had a few gophers and they were digging holes in the lawn. I got this trap (two of them) after reading the reviews. It was easy to set, and I used baby carrots as the bait.As there were no tunnels, but just holes in the ground, I kept the trap near one of the holes.The first day it caught one gopher, and since then it has caught 4 more (in 5 days total)Very pleased with the purchase

I've tried gopher gas bombs and water hose down the hole (neither worked).  I just used the Black Box for the past 24 hours and I've killed 3 gophers so far.  I found the most recently dug holes, dug it out a bit more so I can place the black box into the hole.  Make the box flush and semi-level with the tunnel so it seems like it's a part of the gopher tunnel, then place soft dirt around the edges so the main light is peaking thru the hole in the box.  I placed baby carrots near the hole in the box to entice the gophers to move fully into the box.  This contraption isn't for the squeamish.  You'll have to handle the box with the dead gopher, but if you press the metal handle back down the gopher falls out.  I would recommend this to anyone who has a gopher problem.

The trap is well built but not sure if it is really a pocket gopher trap. The trigger wire is set so far back from the entrance numerous times the gopher hole gets plugged before trap triggers. Small pocket gophers are really tough as they can trigger trap but still be in front of the catch wire!

This is a solid well made trap that works really well. Took a little tractice to get the traps positioned correctly but now they are working great. 6 gophers down so far vs one for the black tunnel kind of trap. Much easier to work with and I don't need to worry about the gophers getting spooked walking on plastic floor. Highly recommended trap and I would get at least two for your garden.
So far I've had one confirmed kill with the Box golpher trap. The only draw back is the size of the hole you have to dig to insert the trap.

column9: Didn't work for me - useless instructions
column10: I live in southern california and my yard is over-run by gophers. I bought this trap first from amazon as it supposedly is meant for novice users who are just beginning their gopher-eradication journey.The trap arrived in a paper box, which had pretty much no useful instruction in placing the trap. Should you place one trap in each direction of the tunnel? Should you cover up the end hole? the top opening? Should you place bait? Should you wear gloves? Should the joint of the trap and the tunnel be air tight? Should you use it in the main run? Or can it be used in the lateral openings? No help on any of these items in the instructions.Anyway, I set the trap 3 times, and each time the little critters filled them up with dirt. I finally got fed up and bought a couple of the victor easy-set traps. With those, I have had good success after placing them in the tunnels. This one is a waste. I don't know how it got such high reviews.

After more than a year with no success and a torn up lawn, within hours of setting this trap I finally caught one! I have hope now that I might be able to rescue my lawn and finally get this gopher problem under control. I love that you can see if the trap has been tripped without digging it up.

A friend of ours told us about the "black box gopher trap" and how effective it was.  I went to Amazon (my favorite on line shopping center), typed in the description, read the guys pitch, and bought one trap.  Delivery was quick.  We immediately set the trap and within one day caught a monster gopher.  It was easy to unload the gopher from the trap.  No guts, no fuss.We almost immediately bought 3 more traps.  I gave one to my neighbor.  I highly recommend this trap to anyone with gopher problems!!Sincerely,Mike Barret

I purchased 2 of these black box gopher traps and didn't need both of them! The very first night I inserted this trap at the end of the tunnel, I checked it after school and sure enough the gopher was dead as a door nail. You may ask, is it humane and does it kill quickly? Definitely. Looks like this gopher was killed on impact. I'm very pleased and look forward to killing many more gophers with it!!! I can't believe how much time we wasted with gassing out gophers and grub killer and poison peanuts and such.... wish I would've tried this a long time ago!!!!
Gopher killing machine.  I put this baby down and have had caught four in one week in different areas of my yard.

I was chasing a gopher all over my yard for years. I went online to get a car exhaust kit for gophers. After seeing the reviews for the BLACK BOX, I thought I'd give it a try. Two days later I recieved it, I set it up carefully according tothe instructions and other reviews. After 2 years and over $200 spent on useless traps and other crap from Home DepotIN LESS THAN  30 MIN my problem was solved!!!!!

column9: KINDA SMALL TRAP- APPROX 3.5 or 4 opening X 7 inches long
column10: This trap is made for "minnie mole", or "Geo the gopher". You know the tiny chevrolet Geo?Honestly, don't think it will work for me 'cause I actually saw the one that has taken up residence in my front, and back yard, and he aint that small. I should refer to him as a ground hog instead :) Maybe this trap will catch something roaming around, that doesn't belong.... If it does catch gargantuan gopher I'll report back.Sorry to say the lever let me down. The lever on the trap has to be set on the edge of the hook for it to work. I even decided to dig the trap up, because I noticed that overnight, still had no catch, but the bait was gone. I wiggled the hook, this thing did not even budge. So I am assuming that the hook on my trap is bent too far closed. Washed it, and disinfected it, and sent it back. I am trying the huge rat trap with bait, then I'll report back with my results.
I set the trap according to the instructions and the gopher was in the trap the next morning--couldn't ask for better!

column9: Mixed feeling, effective but not as easy as people describe
column10: I really don't like how everyone makes it seem so easy to use.  This box is large.  You have to dig a sizeable portion of dirt to make a flat area that fits the whole box.  Due to this, you are going from a small tunnel size hole to a giant hole.  It takes practice to carefully flush the front of the box to the hole and then gently pack dirt in the gaps to close the light.  Even when I thought it was perfect, I had gophers pack them a few times even when a carrot piece was in the back.  I have been using them for a few weeks and got 2 gophers and 1 mole.  With each kill, they are definitely dead so I didn't have to worry about one squirming.  Also, finding the hole and ensuring the gopher has easy access into the box is not easy!  The tunnels are at angles or are not clearly defined even with using a long stick or some type of rod to probe around.  The boxes do work but don't expect this to be a cake walk.  It takes around 10-15 minutes to find the tunnel, dig the hole and put the trap in while wearing some type of gloves.  Also, if you have dogs, good luck trying to keep them away.  I have to cover the holes with stepping stones to avoid my dogs digging down while still allowing light to get in so the gopher sees the light in the back of the box.  I have a terrier that wants to find out what is going on all the time.

Watching helplessly as our backyard lawn being decimated by gophers, I googled for video tutorials on how to set gopher traps.Most seemed to me complicated and even overwhelming. I am an engineer, and you heard the joke on how many engineers it takes to change the - you know...Using poison was not an option because of nearby vegetable patch.But, one day, looking at our lawn in sorry state, I knew that the gophers left me no choice. It was time to shop for the very first gopher trap in my life.I picked Victor Blackbox, not because I knew anything about it, but the reviews were favorable.The order was delivered, and I opened it up.It had a small piece of paper purported to be an instruction manual, which did not make sense to the novice of novices.I visited their website, but there was really not much info there either.Why not just 2 minute YouTube video on how to use it...My problem was that I could not make which way to place the trap in gopher's tunnel because one end was closed. Of course, I now know with my newly gained skill having caught 5 gophers so far how to dig and expose the tunnel and place the trap in which direction.  But, it was just all unexplained and was indeed a blackbox to me.Anyhow, I managed to set the trap after learning how to do it from Amazon's product review(!) and within a few days, I caught 5 gophers.I like Victor Blackbox because it is designed with safety in mind for users, and reusable again and again.It works each time, and because of strong and quick snap, it is humane kill for the rodent.I highly recommend it - if I can handle it, you will be able to.Lastly, I hope the manufacturer puts up a 2 minute instruction on  YouTube.

column9: Best trap, it's a real killer
column10: We have gophers and they started eating my veggie gardern so it is war. My dogs know where the gophers are and will start a hole but then just watch the gophers. So now we enlarge the hole and set the trap in the hole the dog starts. Generally within 12 hours we have a gopher and each one is dead from the trap. We have eliminated 5 gophers so far in 2 weeks. My husband is very happy with this purchase, he wants me to order another trap so we can catch more gophers and have our veggie garden to ourselves.

Trap with no bait was filled with dirt by gopher, twice.  Put some cilantro paste (bought at supermarket) in trap, behind trigger mechanism.  Gopher couldn't resist.  Apparently, cilantro is gopher ambrosia.
Bought two in hopes of ridding my yard of these pesky critters. First night caught one and no more mounds since then. The other trap is set waiting for their return. Delighted with the results.

Just nailed my first one today. I placed it in what I thought was a fresh hole yesterday morning and left it overnight. At the same time, I knocked down all the mounds (lots of them!) so I could be sure I had a fresh mound. This morning it wasn't sprung, but there were two new mounds. I found the hole and installed it as instructed. I went out and checked it awhile ago and I got him! BTW the box had perfectly adequate instructions, although I had looked at a U Tube video while I was waiting for it. Our property looks like a minefield, so I'm sure this will be the first of many. Hmmm...wonder if I should put a notch on the side? Bwaaahahahah!

A new neighbor turned me on to these traps and they simply work.  I have a 100% kill rate with these traps.  Every time I set a trap, I get my gopher.  The fastest kill was under 5 mins.  Barely had my tools put away before the trap was sprung.  This trap is based on the behavior of the gopher.  When properly set as the other reviewers have described, the fresh air and light that comes in the little hole at the end of the box triggers the gophers natural behavior.  They have a keen sense of smell and the smell the fresh air and sense the light coming into the tunnel triggers the gopher into action.  The gopher simply feels compelled to fix the situation and seal off the tunnel.  Next thing you know the gopher is pushing a dirt plug to close the hole.  The box is large and deep enough to let both the dirt plug and the gopher to enter the trap before the trigger is sprung.  There you have it - 1 dead gopher.  I have tried everything over the years and now would not recommend anything else but this trap.

Well, this trap is extremely effective. I bought 2 and set them up back to back, as is recommended. I also found some videos on YouTube that helped me find their many tunnels, I believe I searched  for "gopher tunnel system" and it was a UC Davis video. In addition I bought the gopher probe on Amazon. It is designed to apply poison, which I don't do, but it makes the tunnel finding task so much easier. First day I caught the real trouble maker who was literally destroying my lawn and inflicting major damage on my beds, too. Since then activity has been minor, and when I see a new mound I immediately set the traps up and the problem is taken care of, sometimes within an hour or two. My yard is on the mend, I wish I hadn't waited so long to start using these.So, what's the "unfortunate" part? For me, it is hard to remove the gophers. Not physically, but emotionally. They are actually really cute. I really would have preferred a non lethal solution, but in my experience there are NONE that work. I spend 15-20 hours a week working in my garden, and hundreds if not thousands of dollars, I just couldn't bear to see it destroyed.

This is a seriously good product.  I live in a very rural area which is plagued by moles and pocket gophers. This year has been especially bad, as evidenced by literally hundreds of fresh soil mounds each week in my pasture and garden.  Like other reviewers, I tried a number of other products in an attempt to avoid the dreaded trap.  And nothing worked.  The gassers were useless, and although the poison was effective, I worried constantly about my dog and (for those who think poison is a nice and tidy solution), encountered trails of bloody mucus and entrails on my concrete walkways as evidence of what must have been a prolonged and horrific death.Enter the Black Box.  First, I want to make the point that I'm a woman, a bit squeamish (actually, a lot squeamish when it comes to things rodent), and I have no mechanical aptitude at all.  I was absolutely sure that I was not going to be able to set the trap (or that I would lose a few fingers trying) and was similarly certain that I would not catch anything.  Stuff like this just doesn't work for me.Well, to my amazement, I had an instant success.  It couldn't have been more than three or four hours after I (successfully) set the trap that I had snagged my first mole.  And I have been trapping them daily every since.Let me begin by stating that there is nothing at all difficult about setting this trap.  It sets just like a mouse trap, but with two important exceptions:  First, the metal arm that holds the spring-loaded killing bar down is very easy to set in place and, unlike a mouse trap, does not tend to spring loose while you're setting it.  Second, the killing bar is INSIDE the box, so even if the bar were to snap back while you're setting the trap, your fingers would not be in harm's way.  Yes, it takes considerably more muscle to set than a mousetrap, but it is nothing that this 120-pound woman can't easily do.  I use one foot to help, and I can set the thing in a matter of seconds.  No sweat.Finding the tunnel and placing the trap has been a no-brainer.  I simply dig a hole where the mound is, then feel around its sides with a gloved hand to locate the tunnel opening.  Once located, I scoop out the loose dirt to clear a good-sized opening, then butt the trap right up against the tunnel opening.  Other reviewers have stated that they pack dirt tightly around the sides of the trap, but I've had equally good luck simply setting the trap in the hole and covering the hole with a piece of heavy cardboard (making sure that no light comes through around the edges).  Normally, within a half-day I have either caught something or the trap has been packed with dirt by a mole or gopher trying to close off the tunnel.  In the latter event, I simply reset the trap and try again.  Baby carrots stuck part-way into the air hole do seem to improve the chances of success.Disposal of dead catch has not been all that bad.  I dig a grave, and, using the toe of my boot to hold the bar down, simply knock the dead critter into the hole with a trowel.  Don't have to touch anything.In summary, this product really works.  The only criticism I have is that the instructions on the box are not at all helpful.  However, by reading the reviews on Amazon, a first-time user can get a complete how-to and be up and running in minutes.  The poor instructions notwithstanding, I give this product five stars.

I bought this contraption after a savage group of gophers was ravaging both my front and back yards.  I caught two gophers in about a week.  It is kind of a pain to dig and set it in the ground but it certanly works.  I did not use any bait. There are good videos on youtube on how to set this kind of trap.
After years of traps, flooding, poison bait, and gas bombs, I tried this trap based on the good reviews.  Caught him on the first day!  I have not seen any evidence of gophers since.

I tried poison, hose down the hole, gassing...all of which gave no dead body in return, and mounds kept showing up regularly.  So after some research and a word of advice from a friend, I found these traps.  I read the reviews and ordered two.I set one on early Friday morning in my front yard, following the instructions given by one of the posts.  Woke up this morning, checked it, and caught that sucker.  I checked the backyard after feeling victorious and noticed a fresh mound.  So, feeling confident, I dug around a bit, found the tunnel, set the second trap. Caught the second one within an hour.  I live in regular ole suburbia with a normal size front & backyard. So these can work just fine without tearing up your grass too bad.These traps are fantastic.  HIGHLY recommended.

column9: Works great if you like death (to gophers)!
column10: I use this one and the black hole trap. They both work well and I think it is good to switch off. One old geezer had packed two of my black hole traps with dirt so I switched off to this one and caught the old guy, a big, wise old grandpa type. Great big teeth and claws, been around a while. Kindof sad but it's them or my manzanita.The killing never ends. I clear em out but they come back in waves and I have to put the traps out again, sometimes I get them before they damage a plant, sometimes I am too late. Someone told me to plant garlic around, I don't think it is a CA native like the rest of my garden but I will give it a try, I hate so much killing. I think their tunnels extend under the asphalt road to the park across the street. They even come in the house sometimes, waddling across the Pergo looking for a tunnel...

column9: It works, got gopher #1 on Day 2
column10: Bought two traps to set in various pocket gopher holes. I found the holes by poking around the mounds with a bbq skewer until it was met with little resistance, then opened the hole with a shovel and my hand (wearing garden gloves). On Day 1, the gopher(s) plugged the two traps 2-3 times, so I moved the traps to other parts of their maze. Sure enough, got one this morning. And to my surprise, the other trap was not plugged and the open holes where the traps had been set previously were not plugged either. I wonder if it was just the one gopher? Either way, I reset the traps and will wait a few days. If the traps and open holes aren't plugged over the next few days, I'd say I'm good.Needless to say, these things do work. Just be sure to block out all light, except the small hole on the end. And set the traps in a different place if the gophers keep plugging the traps.
I caught a gopher on the first day!  I;ve never been good with traps, but this one was easy to use.

My first Black Box worked very well, so I bought three more. Some of the new ones didn't work; the gophers filled them with dirt without springing them. I tested the triggers with a postal scale and found that the good traps would trigger with less than two ounces of force, while the bad ones took up to six ounces. I bent the hooks on the trigger wires (the wire the gopher pushes) until I got them all to trigger at under two ounces. I also filed some down a little. Now they all work very well. I am catching a couple of dozen gophers a year. These traps don't work on the moles in my area, because the moles go under them instead of entering. The traps are durable. The wire is either stainless or some rust resistant alloy. As others have said, you have to dig a significant hole to set these. If you are trying not to disturb a lawn, it is best to dig out chunks of sod and keep them cool and damp until the gopher is caught. Then you can replace the chunks in the hole.

If you have pocket gopher problem, get this trap.  Set it up correctly and you will catch your enemy.I was so frustrated with my big-box-store-bought "wire jaw" type of traps.  Forthree days straight, those traps were tripped and buried by the pesky gopher without catching it.  Everyday I woke up in the morning and only to see the holesgot plugged up.  Talking about feeling helpless...Then I found this wonderful device.  That smart gopher is now a dead gopher overnight.  Looking at its dead body in the trap this morning, I felt like at the top of the world...maybe a little exaggeration but I did smack the corpse with myshovel to let out some last bit of hatred toward this pest.Get it now if you have gopher problem!  It's THE gophers' bane.

I purchased this trap 2 months ago after my old wooden trap had caught its last gopher. With all the construction going on in the field behind my house, it was driving the gophers out and into mine and the surrounding yards. Well, no worries. So far five for five on traps set and gophers caught! Heck, I may even hire myself out to the neighbors! GREAT TRAP

This is the first encounter I've had with gophers, let alone gopher traps. When I received the BlackBox, I took a couple of minutes to figure out how to set it, but it was very easy once I figured it out. Smaller, than I thought (turns out, gophers are smaller than I thought as well). I dug up the freshest hole, revealing the pests tunnel, as the instructions described on the box. I placed a single box inside the ground, put a carrot through the vent hole and set the trap.No telling when it was caught, but I let the trap sit overnight and when I came back in the morning to investigate, the box was tripped, and the gopher was dead inside. Clean, kill, not messy. As humane as you can be, killing an animal. Not something I wanted to do, but can't have the little bugger wrecking my yard. Set it again this morning, just to be certain there are no more. However, if there are, I trust BlackBox to catch them.Very pleased with the product. Well worth the low price. I would recommend it, for the sake of your lawn.

I want to express my profound thanks to the many Amazon reviewers who helped me find and decide to purchase this product.  The positive reviews are stunningly correct.  I'm a life-long city dweller, recently moved to an area that borders on wide open spaces.  When the gophers invaded the yard, I went to the big-box home store, bought the usual poison granules, smoke firecrackers, etc.  with no luck.  Enter the Victor BlackBox trap.  I'd never seen one of these things, let alone used one, and the instructions on the box were minimal.  No problem!  I studied the excellent detailed information provided by Amazon reviewers.  Thanks again.  I did what they said, setting the trap under a fresh dig the same day it arrived.  Next morning -- a small funeral for one dead gopher.  Enough said.Addendum:  I've had my traps for several months now (I bought 2).  They continue to amaze.  As of today, I've dispatched six gophers.  Whenever I see a new dig in the yard, I grab my trusty Victor BlackBox traps and go to work.  They just get the job done.  I can't remember being this satisfied with another garden product.  Thank you Victor!

I read the reviews.  I wanted a solution that did not use poison due to our pets.  I bought two.  The directions say to place two of them back to back in the trench.  I am glad I followed directions. Berfore sundown, I placed both in the trench I dig out in the gopher path under a very thin layer of dirt, and waited.Four hours later, the first one was packed full of dirt by the gopher.  The second one was tripped. I found large gopher.  See my photo.  It barely fit into the trap.  Note the first trap still hidden in the trench to the upper right.No blood or mess.  I could not be happier.

At first I thought I was doing something wrong.  It took about two months before I got my gopher.  I would give this item 4 stars but the instructions on usage are very sparse and caused me to do a lot of trial and error before I finally got him.  However, the trap worked well and I can reuse it now.  Reset it and forget it so I would recommend it.

Tried poison bait for a few weeks, no dice, even when I used a screw driver to poke it into their main tunnels from above.Tried the victor blackbox and caught a gopher in about 30 minutes.Pretty easy to use too - all the killing bits are inside the box so it's 100% safe to handle. Digging the hole took a few minutes, but the results were worth it! No blood an guts to clean up either, at least on my first time around.It's made of plastic, but feels very heavy duty.

I hate gopher.  My front yard is infested with these critters.  Pincer traps are good, but quite difficult to set if the hole is too wide.  These beautiful toys fit the bigger tunnel very nicely.I disagree with the other reviewer regarding to the trigger position.  With the factory set position, the bigger gopher will be choked, while the little one will be crushed at the mid section.  The key to successfully use this trap is how to set it.  You have to think like a gopher, and construct this unit into the gopher's existing tunnel.  Then, leave a little opening a bit further down the tunnel.  Gophers' instinct will be to close the opening further down the tunnel, thus activate the trigger.  I have caught gophers 3 hours after the traps were set.  2 from 1 trap in the same day.If you are afraid to dig a big hole in your yard, this is not a unit for you as it requires some space to construct an elaborate trap.  However, if the gopher is already destroying your yard, why not just do it yourself and rid of the problem once and for all.

This trap worked for me.  A major feature of the trap is that it is enclosed, so as long as you don't put your hands inside the enclosed area, it shouldn't bite you.  When setting, I added a carrot as a little incentive for the gopher to check things out.  Box recommends that you have 2 -- I think this is because you can put the opening in either direction to get them running both ways.  Also -- make sure you see Caddy Shack again before use.

Worked great, however the second time we put it out, the fox (I believe) took both the Gopher and the trap so had to buy another one.  No Gopher's since.  Live in a remote area so no way to find the other trap.

Once you learn the correct way to set this trap it works! The first time I set this trap I had it turned the wrong way in the gopher hole (it was a large hole with multiple entrances). The gopher stuffed it full of dirt. After seeing this, I turned the trap so the opening faced a different tunnel. I also made sure I covered the hole and area around trap so no light or air would get into the gopher hole. I was careful about not putting too much dirt on the trigger mechanism. I also put baby carrots and peanut butter in the back of the trap. In less than 24hrs (I set it at night and rechecked in the morning) I had 1 of the critters that has been destroying my yard for the last several months. This trap works well if you take your time setting it up. You need to find a fresh hole and make sure this trap is flush with the gopher tunnel. You do have to dig a bit in your yard as this larger then some of the other traps on the market.  Also, a word of advice, make sure you know the critter type you are trying to trap. At first, I thought I had moles because I had piles of large dirt mound around my yard and the holes under the mounds were plugged. From what I read I thought it was a mole but I received some good local advice and they said I had gophers. Don't buy into the horseshoe shaped mounds theories about gopher holes. None of mine were horseshoe shaped and I caught a gopher. Hope this helps!

We live on a farm and gophers are a major problem. We've tried all of the old favorites with very poor luck. The first day we got the BlackBox, we trapped 3 gophers from the same hole. This thing really works. Follow the setting instructions and you will trap gophers!

column9: The only one that has worked!
column10: This is the only trap that has worked WELL in our yard in our battle with gophers. I didn't want to use poison because of the environment and potential danger to predator birds, so we started using at the recommendation of a friend who claimed "The Black Box is the ONLY thing that really works".We tried something called "The Black Hole" which definitely was not as effective and it may be because the animal has to walk on plastic, or that it actually has to fit into the round contraption, whatever - it definitely wasn't as effective as "The Black Box". I believe The Black Box works the best because the animal is "still feels dirt under its feet and is not alerted.  We simply place a fresh carrot piece in the back of the trap and it seems very effective as bait. As an animal lover, I was also concerned about being humane and this trap I believe kills instantly by snapping the spine so there is no suffering. Removal of the carcass is also simple and not messy (no blood).At times the gophers may fill the trap with dirt and it has been our experience that the trap sometimes needs to be set elsewhere in the tunnel system, BUT sometimes they can be "enticed" by placing a smaller carrot morsel or two further into the hole and "lead into the trap". We think they bury the trap because they are just plugging the hole, they don't even realize the food is available.I'm ordering more as it seems that it is the season for them and they have been popping up in different places on our property.

column9: THIS IS THE ONE TO GET
column10: Please don't waste your money on anything else.  This works like a charm!  I have bought a few of these things!
We caught the critter within a half an hour of setting the trap.  Worked perfectly as advertised.  My husband was very pleased with the results.
Product as advertising. Recommend to other. Easy to used. AAA+++.Don't catch gopher think about Victor 0625 The BlackBox Gopher Trap.

column9: Did not work for my gopher
column10: This is the first set of traps I used for my gopher problem in my yard.  It came with instructions on only how to set the trap, not where to place it in regards to the gopher hole/runway.  After researching how to set box-style traps, I tried for a week in various locations throughout my yard where there was recent activity.  The problem wasn't finding the gopher, but it was that the gopher would push dirt into the trap and not set it off.  He was essentially pushing about three inches of dirt into the trap and sealing off himself from the plastic intrusion. The lever to set off the trap is even further back from that, so he never got far enough in the trap to do what it's supposed to do.  I finally purchased a two-pack of Victor Easy Set metal traps, and caught the sunofagun on the first setting of the traps.  Other people have had success with this type of trap, but not me. Hope this helps people in the future.

I was skeptical because I had tried a lot of other products to get rid of my gopher problem but had yet tried traps.  I could swear this gopher was laughing at me every time I tried a new product and it was infuriating!  Based on customer reviews I ordered this product, followed the directions exactly and caught the gopher within 3 hours!  It kills them instantly, so no suffering and it doesn't leave behind a gross mess to clean up.  Highly recommend this trap!

I too tried everything including the spring traps that are supposed to impale the gopher, but they did not work either. My brother told me about his Black Box and loaned it to me. Unbelievably, I went three for three! Three days, three gophers, and no errors. I bought one and loaned it to my son and it worked for him too. Now, I have a new gopher in the back yard. I have tried three times to get him, but he filled the trap with dirt each time. The only thing different is that my brothers trap had a piece of cardboard cut to cover the hole at the top of the trap. This time I'm going to get the bugger!

Got this to get rid of a family of gophers that was tearing up my yard. We tried everything, but nothing worked, even our dog seemed to be getting exasperated. The trap arrived the next day (thanks Amazon Prime!) and caught 3 of those annoying gophers in 4 days! I'm going to leave it out a few more days to make sure, but I dare say this trap cleaned house! Don't waste your time and money, and risk your health on poisons and other methods that claim to work. Buy one, you won't regret it. Think of it as an investment for your home!

We just got a new house last year. It came complete with a large yard and pocket gophers. I spent 9 months trying different poisons always following the instructions. All it did was make them stronger as I saw more and more of my yard destroyed. Based on reviews and research, I chose the Blackbox trap. It came quickly and I read the directions and suggestions of other reviewers. I did not get a chance to set it for a couple of weeks, but I set it out about noon and came back a couple hours later and found the trap had sprung. I had seen some birds in the area and thought they might have tripped it. Nope, I had caught my first gopher. A big fat one. I dumped it and reset the trap, leaving it there for 3 days. No hits, but no more mounds in that area. I reset it in another area and within a couple of hours, bam another one. This trap works well and is worth the effort.Suggestions: Follow the directions. I picked mounds at the end of the tunnel with only one way out by using a metal rod to probe the ground. I dug out a lot of dirt to get the trap to match the hole properly. I used baby carrots as bait and carefully used dirt clods over the top hole and rear air hole to allow air flow but block light. Make sure you cover what you can to block the light. I have not washed the trap yet as there is not mess and it doesn't seem to prevent their buddies from joining them.

I set the Victor version of the Macabee traps in opposite directions in a burrow.  I found one of the traps triggered, buried in dirt, but no gopher.  After four days of the same thing happening, I tried this box trap and got him.  However, it trapped the back end of the gopher and didn't kill it.

column9: Works great with a little creativity
column10: My father is a bail bondsman with a lot of free time so he chooses to work in the yards of our roughly one acre of land. We have always had gophers around and my father has tried countless ways to get rid of them and never had much luck until a friend lent him a wooden version of this product. The friend's suggestion was to dig a small hole where the gopher's tunnel is, place the trap inside, cover the top with a leaf, and check back in a few hours. It worked so well that my father had to have a couple more. I found this one here on Amazon and ordered two. Thanks to Amazon Prime it was at my door in two days and within a week my father had captured four gophers and we noticed the lack of gopher activity for a few days. He has been giving them to good friends and we keep ordering more since more gophers show up every once in a while. The other day I visited a friend's house and noticed that he had 4 of these in his back yard and he mentioned that he spends a little more buying them locally but to him they're definitely worth the price. He puts a potato at the end to attract the gopher, so there are probably plenty of clever ways to trap those pesky gophers, it just takes some effort. I can say with certainty that this is an excellent product based on my father's and friends' successes.

column9: Winning at the Gopher Game - Gotcha!
column10: Such satisfaction to win over these critters that have destroyed my previous yard and now the freshly layed sod after just spending $3000+ refreshing.  I caught one within minutes, yes minutes, thanks to the other generous reviews, directions and aid in finding videos to help in the setting of the trap.  Ahh, now I can sit back and know the next mound of freshly churned soil will be mine for the attack.  Gophers watch out, here I come with my Victor BlackBox Gopher Trap --- Ha, Ha --- Gotcha!

Although described as a gopher trap, I have killed 2 moles in my yard with the black box.  It doesn't involve any chemicals or pesticides, is sturdy and can be re-used year to year, a great product.It takes a little learning and patience.  I tried 2 end-to-end but ultimately both my kills involved a single box at the end of a tunnel. Watch where they mound frequently and set it in that spot.  Take the time to dig out a hole with a flat compacted bottom, big enough for the black box.  Cover the holes at the top of the box with patties of damp soil so light will not enter.  Good luck!
This gopher trap is easy to set and use.  It has a quick and easy to release trigger that will trick any but the smartest gophers into the trap and to a quick end.  Highly recommended!!

The Victor Black Box gopher trap worked for me the first day I used it. I tried other methods without success- the Victor Out-of-sight Trap was a total bust, and, yes, I followed the many directions for its use. I thoroughly and heartily recommend the awesome Black Box!

We have spent three years trying to get rid of pocket gophers in our N.M. back yard. We have spent many hundreds of dollars on other traps, store-bought gas bombs, "professional" gopher trapper, and "professional" gaser (from the pest company--they use aluminum phosphide). Nothing worked. The first day I set out four of these, I caught a pocket gopher in one of them. In one case, I didn't have the trap positioned precisely enough and the vermin got around it.Placing the traps does take time and practice, but it's the only thing that has worked at all. Unlike poisons, you see the proof of its success. I do not use carrots in the traps. I've used a piece of sandstone or paper on the outside of the trap to keep dirt out and then cover the trap with soil again. I have to dig out the trap in a day or two, but it's the only way to be sure no light is getting through.

column9: Just what I have been looking for.
column10: After trying every means to get rid of gophers without killing them I had to step up to something like this. This little box is the only thing that has worked for me. After dealing with gophers for the last 8 months I was able to trap three gophers in 48 hours you cant beat that. Just find a new spot where dirt is pushed up fresh, dig a small hole in the tunnel, I used a little dab of peanut butter inside the trap, set it, cover with loose dirt, and check periodically throughout the day. One gopher did get trapped and not killed so I did have to kill it myself. Do yourself a favor and save your landscape and money by just starting with one of these if you have a gopher problem.

column9: Didn't believe it would work... But it did.
column10: Tried everything... smoke bombs, poison, repellent... nothing worked.  Should have tried this trap first.  It worked the very first time.  Just make sure to use carrots in the far end and completely bury the trap. And Bye bye gopher.

I bought this trap as an ultimate resort.  For two years our gopher chomped away happily in the garden undisturbed by us.  We were ok with him until he started heading for the patio and the pole barn floor and chewing through front garden plantings.  I had tried caster oil granules, battery and solar powered noise making devices: even my dogs tried to scare him off. All attempts at deterring his path failed (including fire ants) and we finally had to trap him.  This device works exactly as described (we placed a carrot in the ventilation hole to stop him packing it out)  and while we were unhappy to have to use it we can recommend it as a last effort.  It would be better if the coyotes did the job for us. Be very careful where you put your hands!

It worked but after trying several times. No instructions are provided that's why I give it less than 5 stars. I wish Victor Company would care a little bit more and add some good instructions on how to place the trap. The box has some ideas on the outside but not use instructions...Update:  After learning and using it several times it works perfectly, a kill every time, just make sure you put a couple of little pieces of wet (for enhanced odor) carrot through the light hole. Gophers can not resist it and fall for it every time.

Best trap on the market. Yes, you have to excavate a bit to place the trap. The dirt floor of this trap is great at tricking the gopher! I baited with peanut butter and carrot and bagged a large, female, gravid western pocket gopher. She killed half of the baby native coastal live oaks on my property and destroyed the hillside. I excavated out the region of this same tunnel which might have a dead smell and have reset a second Victor trap (fresh with no dead smell). Wish me luck.

We have a winner.  No more gas bombs or poison...those are a waste of time. I feel bad killing these cute little guys...but I care more about my yard.Update: 3 dead within 36 hours...I would suspect it would be more If I were able to check the trap more often.  Still feeling horrible about killing them...but they are tearing h*ll in my yard and my young trees are at risk.  Bottom line, I can't believe anyone has not had success with this death merchant.

I was a bit skeptical of gopher traps in general since I've never really heard of them. Well, after watching my lawn get torn up by a gopher, I turned to Amazon and found this trap. I opted for this one since it was enclosed, which would appear to "funnel" the gopher into the trap. Anyway, per the instructions, I found an appropriate spot, and lo and behold, caught a gopher within a day! Totally satisfied and recommend this trap.

column9: Work GREAT to snuff out Seattle moles !!
column10: I tried the black box based on input from a friend who is a golf course greenskeeper. He uses them with great success  to eliminate moles on his golf course. Remove surface dirt from mole mound and dig down into the dirt with a hand shovel to locate the tunnel. Locate the tunnel holes on each side of the hole you have dug out and dig enough dirt  to be able to put 2 black boxes back to back into the hole you have dug. Be sure that the black box opening is even with the tunnel floor and  right up against the mole tunnel hole on each side of the hole you have dug. Set the trap (similar to setting a mouse trap) and put soil loosely over the set traps to keep the light out but don't pack  the soil down. When the little bugger moves through that tunnel,  ZAP .... you got him!! There are are instructions for use on the box also.

I just don't understand how these guys are trying to sell 120 bars in bulk for 115 dollars, while Amazon sells 10 bars for 7 bucks. Just buy 12 boxes from Amazon for 84 dollars. I really would like to see this product in bulk though. Nature valley sells 96 bars for 20 dollars. That's what I want from Cliff.

This is the best honey soynut butter I have ever had.  I am allergic to peanuts so this is the gluten free alternative which doesnt need refrigeration and it down right delicious.  Its smooth and creamy and sperads very easily on everything peanut butter would .  I cant taste the difference.  Its safe for schools.  Made from NON GMO roasted soybeans, cholesterol free, gluten free, no trans fats dairy free, panut and treenut free.  Nutritional label says :  2 tbsp are 190 calories, total fat 14 grams, sodium  100mg, total carbs 10 grams, fiber 4 grams, sugar 4 grams, protein 7 grams.Its pricey but worth the money.  I buy this and other varieties of this brand all the time.  5  ( if not 10 )  stars. Truly DELICIOUS

column9: So good could eat it like ice cream
column10: Smooth, nutty with hint of honey. It doesn't need refrigerated, but I like to keep it in there, I sometimes eat it with a spoon like ice cream...I really love this.

Our daughter's school went peanut-free, so we needed to find something besides our organic natural peanut butter for quick, economical lunches that she would actually eat. I just gave our daughter a whole wheat 'pbj' sandwich made with this and her favorite jelly, and she did not know it was soy nut butter. When I told her, she said it was good and tasted the same.  I will say, it does not taste like peanut butter if you try it straight from the jar, but on a sandwich it is pretty close. Makes a good nut butter-banana sandwich too. It is smooth and soft, easy to spread. The jar says no refridgeration needed. There are no hydrogenated oils so it is a healthy choice.

I love chocolate, I love white chocolate. I love tootsie rolls, and this is an extra special treat. The bank is a lovely novelty for the kitchen counter, and the refills go fast. Everyone loves this vanilla flavor. Yummy!

Well, some 10 years ago I began chewing Trident White, then switched over to this. I haven't been to the dentist in just as much time, until recently. Dentist gave me a clean bill of health, and was very surprised I had not had a clean up in over a decade.Has to be the gum.

column9: Dentist-approved, although the flavor isn't everlasting.
column10: My dentist recommended this gum (apparently the Recaldent stuff isn't just advertising).  The cool mint is a good mint flavor, comparable to any other mint (not spearmint or peppermint) gum.  Only problem is that the flavor doesn't last particularly long.

I have an adult foster home and always look for ways to make it easier for my hired help to cook delicious meals with less time.  Now---this sauce mix is so easy to make, you add water.  You do have to condense the amounts made (it takes a gallon of water to make the whole package) but I use 1 cup mix to 1 1/4 cup boiling water and sometimes I add a bit more water or milk to make it creamier.  But I use it on everything!!!  Chicken, shrimp, lobster, crab, small scallops.  It will easily serve 6 with my condensed recipe.  The best thing to remember is IT IS DELICIOUS!!!  Try it.
This cereal is really good, but the price keeps going up and the boxes keep getting smaller. I like that some of the money goes to good causes, but unfortunately I had to switch to a cheaper brand.
took a little too long to arrive.  cereal is broken up bad within the box.  this cereal is usually pretty chuncky in the box from a grocery store.
I love this cereal, but it's expensive to buy in a store IF you can find it.  Amazon has a great deal on it.

Cereal was Ok, but a bit too sweet and not as good as I expected. You can't really taste the almonds.  FYI: There is no dried fruit in the cereal. The picture on the cover shows fresh raspberries, but you will need to add those yourself if you want them. The calorie count is a bit higher than I expected (nearly 300/one cup) but not bad if that's all you will eat in the morning. Better than a lot out on the market, in both taste and nutrition, but I prefer others, such as Post's Cranberry Almond, Wal-Mart's version of Special K with Strawberries, and Frosted Mini-wheats.It is nice to know that part of the profits are going to community projects (10 percent).

column9: Great product at a great price
column10: I have looked high and low for vanilla almond Peace cereal and usually the price is about $1 more than what I got it for on Amazon. Our whole family loves this cereal so we are so excited we could get it for such a great price.

If you are someone that likes the feel of crunchy softness, that reminds of snow-capped mountains with a cool breeze running up against your face in the morning where rolling green pastures and the smell of nature await you as you sit down in the morning for breakfast, then this cereal is for you!  It has the taste of an all natural, healthy but extremely tasty bite of mixed textures that will reenergize you for the day.  It goes especially well with 8th Continent Vanilla Soy Milk if you like it a little sweeter.  This is the best cereal on the planet and you WILL enjoy it!  It is all natural and you are actually contributing to a good cause when you buy it.  So don't even think twice, your stomach, heart, mind, and soul will thank you!

column9: one complete breakfast...at last and tasty too
column10: Got first time from Vons for my husband to replace his Post Live Active Nut Harvest Crunch that has been discontinued for some time. I was little skeptical but he loved everything about this cereal - taste, crunchiness, stuff, nutrition and last but not least, its price. At other regular stores its close to five bucks, but at Amazon.com we simply subscribe and really save big. The cereal is good enough to satisfy your mid morning hunger yet not heavy to overfill you.

I love this cereal because it's organic and simple. It's not loaded down with many ingredients, and the few that they do have in there are (mostly) organic and not genetically modified. All together, we are presented with a healthy, elegant, and VERY tasty cereal. The granola is rich! The cereal is nice and crunchy. I can eat it all day, everyday. :)
This is my favorite cereal, serve it with Orange Juice and there are the perfect combination!
I work in a warehouse and take this as a quick pick me up during work. I eat it dry and the flavor is great

column9: Tastes great and good for you!
column10: My wife and I both really like this cereal.  It tastes great, especially the granola clusters.  If you like those clusters, try their French Vanilla Granola (unavailable as of 10/2/07).

Having a wheat allergy I am somewhat limited in cereal choices.  My husband tried them and we knew we should subscribe - the first shipment of six boxes disappeared within a few weeks so I upped the subscription to monthly.  The ingredients are absolutely fresh and delicious.  And the cereal serving as suggested on the box has only 250 calories but it's so filling that it suppresses the appetite for hours!  No more urge to nibble!  It's helped me lose several pounds without conscious dieting.
Understand before you order this that it is 3 small pieces -- like the size that the hotel puts on your pillow at night.
If you like smokey, sweet, molasses based BBQ this is as close to heaven as you will get! I have found no better.
These peanuts are very hard, not a good mix of seasoning on them and not hot at all.  I don't recommend thesr at all.  I will keep looking for some good hot peanuts.
These are the best peanuts ever! Just the right amount of spice.I buy them by the 3-pack!Love em!
This gluten free pasta cooks up like wheat versions and tastes yummy.  Leftovers are good the next day, too.  Italians really do know how to do gluten free.

This is by far not only one of the best gluten free pastas I've had , but one of the best pastas period.  Meaning I would pick this over most glutenous pastas.  Has a very great taste to it and will continue to buy this pasta for as long as it's around!

column9: This is the absolute best gf pasta!
column10: My entire eats gluten-free due to having 3 celiacs. We first tried this pasta at an Italian restaurant in San Francisco and were blown away with the taste and texture. It was just like wheat pasta! We've tried many brands of brown rice pasta, corn pasta, corn/quinoa blends and this is our absolute favorite.

I don't need gluten-free pasta but I like trying new foods. I was pleasantly surprised with the ditalini in the 250 gr box (9 ozs). I like this small pasta to put in soups and sides. It is a beautiful yellow color and tastes great. I was also very happy that it comes packaged in a bag within a box.  That means no chance of little critters getting inside the inner sealed package, love that. Most pastas out there do not have pastas in a secondary plastic insert and I've had to throw boxes out b/c I didn't get to eat them b/4 the critters did! The expiration date on these is also great--Sept of 2012 and it is only February of 2011 as I type this. On the ingredient label I do not see any listing for the fiber content which I like to know b/c I'm on WW; but that's a small negative.  This is made in Italy which seems to me a place that knows their pasta.  All in all, a good find and I will share it with friends, celiac and non-celiac alike.

column9: Best gluten-free pasta on the market
column10: I have several family members with celiac's so cooking for a large italian family gathering is a huge challenge if you want to keep your meals simple when pasta is a must have menu item.  I've tried all the brown rice based pasta brands with mixed results.  They are either cook up too gummy, release a lot of starch in the water while cooking, fall apart when mixing the cooked pasta with other ingredients or they do not make great left-overs the next day.  The Le Veneziane pasta is fantastic!  My very picky daughter didn't even realize she was eating gluten-free pasta (she always turned her nose up for the brown rice pasta).  This corn based pasta cooks, feels and taste like the "real" deal and my entire family now prefer this brand over all other wheat based or gluten-free pasta.
In almost 30 years of a gluten free diet, I have tried a lot of GF pastas. This is head and shoulders above all the other fettucines and pennes.

I first discovered this pasta at the NYC restaurant Nizza (if you're gluten-free, you NEED to check them out!). The first time I had this pasta, I was not on the gluten-free diet but I tried some of my Mom's dish (she has Celiac's). As someone who knows what the real thing tastes like, I was absolutely amazed that this pasta was gluten-free. I actually preferred this to regular pasta. It doesn't give you that heavy feeling after eating, and it's great with basically any recipe. I'm now eating gluten-free, and we order this by the case.
