I have been purchasing this Paprika for at least a year, and am very impressed with not only the price, the flavor, the strength, and the speed of shipping, but when compared with the prices in the store this is beyond a bargain, and to top it off the quality is superb. I love it so much I joined subscribe and save to get it sent every three months. When I first tried this paprika I thought there was no way I would be able to use five pounds. Was I ever wrong, the flavor is outstanding, and has become a go to spice for so many of our favorite dishes.
What a wonderful flavor.  Just mix it with Mexican Chili Powder and Wahoo. Great seasoning.  I will get it again when I need it...  Thanks... Cathi

****Stash's Wild Raspberry Caffeine Free Herbal Tea is strong and fruity, great if you love the taste of raspberry and hibiscus, which I do. It contains hibiscus, orange peel, lemongrass, rosehips, natural raspberry flavor, licorice powder, and citric acid. The package says it also contains soy, but that makes little sense to me---but everyone should know this in case they are allergic. It is a fine tasting herb tea.If you like a more subtle tea, you may not be crazy about Wild Raspberry. But if you like Celestial Seasonings and other commercial teas, I think that this is a good one. The reason I gave this tea four stars instead of five is that it isn't as pure as it could be (contains additives and flavorings) and I can tell. I prefer a more subtle tea. And I save five stars for the very best teas I've tried. But for those of you who like a lot of flavor, and can't taste the additives, it's just fine!Recommended.****

I lived in New England for 26 years and have eaten more than my fair share of lobster bisque. It's one of my favorites.The stuff that came out of the can is very dark orange-colored which is not typical for lobster bisque, devoid of any flavor, and just plain gross. It could not be eaten out of the can because of the dreadful flavor. There is no cream in this soup and any bisque is heavy with cream. There's milk, wheat flour, and teeny dots of lobster. I'm a good cook but I doubt that I can doctor this up to taste like anything worth eating.When I read the other negative reviews, I thought...oh well. Folks from other parts of the country don't know what real lobster bisque tastes like, but surely Bar Harbor is doing it right.  WRONG. As a New Englander, I know what good lobster bisque tastes like and it's not this.Unless you enjoy mystery food and dislike lobster, I'd advise against purchasing this.

The reviewer Jo Ana Starr is right, this canned "lobster bisque" is plain gross.  I am a lifelong New Englander and I've been enjoying lobster bisque for 30 years...this stuff is NOT lobster bisque. It's an odd-colored concoction of canola oil, milk, and "native tapioca starch." I paid $3.89 for a (tiny) 10-oz can, and I'm very disappointed. There is so much canola oil in it, you can feel it on your tongue.  No lobster flavor at all.  It's a travesty that they're using the name "Bar Harbor."

Love this soup, excellent lobster flavor with small pieces of lobster meat throughout.  Great thing to have on hand for entertaining!  I disagree with the other review, didn't think it was too tomato-flavored at all.

We just bought 3 cans for $3.00 each at JobLot.  Granted, JobLot is a discount place and these cans sell for $5.00 each. We love Lobster Bisque. We love all types, restaurant, canned, supermarket, whatever....  We opened up one can up today and four of us tried it. It tasted horrible!!  It was brown and tasted like bad fish.  No lie. All of us were repulsed.  I looked up the reviews on the internet, like here, thus wondering if Bar Harbor made a bad batch and sold them off to Job Lot. Anyways, we have two more cans to try. We will certainly not buy this brand again.

Shame on the Bar Harbor Soup Company for falsely inflating their review, with a five-star one of their own. The color doesn't bother me, but the taste certainly does. It's just not lobster bisque. I don't expect much from a can in the first place, but this falls far below expectations. It is edible, but not by much.A few years ago in California lobster bisque was quite hard to come by, so I paid five dollars for a can of this stuff. Waited expectantly while it cooked and threw it all out after the first bite. This product is a bust. Sad though, because the city of Bar Harbor, Maine has some of the best lobster bisque in New England.

I agree with all the other New Englanders that this soup is gross.  First time I tried it, I opened the can and already had my doubts.  But added some cream (as is suggested on the can), I even added some lobster meat!!!  It was just awful.  Fishy smell and fishy flavor.  Not worthy of the name "lobster bisque".

I am a huge fan of lobster bisque so I thought I would give this a try. I did not have high expectation since it's canned but this is NOT edible! The soup is so nasty and taste nothing like lobster bisque. I tried adding cream but it didn't make it any better. I can't believe I paid $3.99/ can for this garbage!!

Bar Harbor All Natural Lobster Bisque, 10.5-Ounce Cans (Pack of 6)Thanks to all who reviewed this product! We appreciate the conversation and realize there can be quite a variety of opinions on any food item based on the vast majority of palates and individuals' past experiences with foods.As a Downeast Maine company that has been producing Lobster Bisque from a local recipe since 1917, it is believed that the recipe, handed down from previous generations, was the most accurate rendition of this regional soup. This is not to say that it is the only recipe or the most popular in this genre of soup, as bisque originated in France and was handed down through immigrants who settled in the Canadian maritimes and then migrated to coastal Maine.The original recipe included the tomalley, or liver, of the lobster and provided a truly robust seafood flavor and a deep orange tone to the finished product. With concerns over mercury in seafood, the recipe has been modified in recent years and a larger quantity of minced lobster has replaced the tomalley. This along with a bit of paprika gives the soup its distinctively strong color. The recipe does not include any tomato products. As to the cream content, milk is an ingredient to create the true bisque texture, however, we intentionally leave the soup in a semi-condensed state to allow the customer to prepare the product to their liking. By adding a bit more milk or cream and a dash of sherry at the end of gently heating the bisque, true restaurant-quality lobster bisque can be achieved.This is one of our most popular soups and at over 20 annual international trade shows it receives rave reviews. Thought we realize we cannot please every palate, we believe the majority of our lobster bisque connoisseurs provide us the confirmation that we are making a high quality, great-tasting Lobster Bique.Bar Harbor Foods is now on Facebook, so please "Like" us if you enjoy our products and we appreciate hearing from all of our customers!~ Bar Harbor Foods
It's so misleading to call this 'lobster' anything.  It's a real rip-off because there's barely a wisp of lobster in it.  I'd suggest you save your money.

I found this Bar Harbor lobster bisque at my small "Shurfine" grocery store.  It was expensive at $4.69 a can but I bought it to try.  I added about 1/2 can of milk and some port wine and a little salt and I thought it to be very good.  Had plenty of lobster and smelled like lobster.  I didn't find it strong of tomato.  Bisque is made with tomato.  If you want chowder you buy clam chowder.  I guess you can't please everyone's taste buds.  I would definitely purchase again.

column9: You can really taste the tomato
column10: If you're looking for a creamy lobster bisque (like that at Red Lobster), this isn't it.  Not much lobster and the tomato taste is very strong.  To be fair, most bisque is tomato-based, but you really taste the tomato with this product.  If you love tomatoes, you'll like this bisque.

column9: now I can have desserts again
column10: it looks and feels like a very fine powder; however, when you put it in butter it reminds me of flour.  however, it did melt down and the dessert was excellent.  I used same equivalent as sugar as I found this to be very sweet.

I have used other products and even tried scratch. This is by far the best that I have had. Creamy and not too salty. Better than betty crocker. How anyone could describe this as yuk is beyond me, sounds like operator error to me. ( The cook messed up ). I have cooked this in a toaster oven & it turned out just fine.

Two of these reviewers are obviously not cooks or they don't care for Velveeta. I usually don't purchase ready prepared or short-cut items because I am very particular about the food I serve; however, once I tried these, I've kept them on-hand for hurry up meals.  If the directions are followed and you stir in the cheese while the product is hot, they're wonderful.  I make them on top of the stove - and if the liquid gets too low I add a little more milk; then afterwards I sprinkle with a few bacon bits and place in the oven for a short while. I am dismayed that I can no longer find this product in the store.

column9: As good as mine and I'm surprised!
column10: I only ordered these to get an order up above the free shipping level and I don't mind admitting it.  If Amazon is going to be decent enough to try to help us out, I'll sure as heck reciprocate by giving them my business!  That said, I wasn't expecting much.  I mean I like Kraft and I even use Velveeta products in recipes here at home, but I make my own au gratin taters, dangit.  I figured these would go to the hall pantry as emergency stocks/preparedness stuff.  I was surprised.  They're really pretty danged good!  Couple of tips, though; be sure to stir the product well before cooking or the potatoes will stick together, and add bacon crumblies!  This is up there with mac and cheese for a family fav here now.  Saves an hour of prep time over my recipe, too.

Forget the cheese sauce...the only way to use this product is to leave off the last step...they instruct you after cooking the product then to add the thick gooey cheese sauce which just ruins it....I purchased a case of these...so before I cook them I add spices or herbs of choice and then after cooking I top with melted butter...I save the sauce packet for nachos..

Velveeta Au Gratin potatoes will surely change the way you think about little slimy potato chips. The poor quality of this food-type item makes me lose a little faith in this civilization and in the relationship between human animals and a free market economy.

These cookies are obvious rip off of the Girl Scout version but I love them anyway! Now they are available all year long for a cheaper price. If you love the "Samoa" then you will love the "Coconut Dream".
These cookies are delightful.  The caramel and coconut are perfect with the shortbread and chocolate.  Much like Girl Scout version but available all year.

column9: Need a Samoa fix?  Grab these!
column10: I just saw and bought these recently because they looked just like the Girl Scout cookies I have always loved over the years ... SAMOA cookies.  If you are a fan of the classic Girl Scout Samoa, then you will undoubtedly love these.  Not sure how or why Keebler decided to bring this cookie to the regular store shelf, but it's a winner.  For a little history: Keebler-Wyl Bakery became the official baker of Girl Scout Cookies in 1936.  It's only natural that the recipes and cookies would make it to the consumer shelf.When you can't find a Girl Scout selling cookies and you need a fix ... these will do.  Love "Thin Mints"?  Try these:  Fudge Shoppe Grasshopper (Mint) Cookies, 10-Ounce Packages (Pack of 6) and you will NOT be disappointed.I feel like I hit the jackpot.  Not that I won't still support the Girl Scouts (cookie sales are integral to their fund raising efforts) but sometimes the cookie availability is not there.Yummy, yum yum!  Love Samoas?  You will love these too!

These vanilla cookies are coated in caramel, sprinkled with toasted coconut and laced with chocolate stripes. They take me back to the days when my sister sold Girl Scout Caramel deLites (aka. Samoas). I've long since stopped buying Girl Scout cookies as the boxes got smaller and the prices went up, so three cheers for Keebler and their willingness to take on the hordes of angry girl scouts who's cookie sales will surely take a small hit.For reference, Girl Scout cookies are currently four dollars for a 7.5 oz box. Keebler's 8.5 oz retails for under three dollars and can even be found on sale for much less.

column9: Great if you are cutting back on sugar but eat in moderation!
column10: These jelly beans are much harder and difficult to eat than regular jellybeans.  That said, they satisfy a craving when I wanted something sweet to eat.  These jellybeans come with a warning to not eat more than a moderate amount because they can cause stomach upset.  This is true, believe me!I wish they were offered in more flavors.
Buyer beware.  I am very disappointed in this product.  This size is very small and the quality appears average.  It is definitely not worth the money.

I bought this item for my daughter's friend who plays tennis. The chocolate had mottled/whitish spots on it which means it has been sitting around the company or warehouse for a while, also the handle of the racket was broken down the middle. Needless to say it was far from suitable as a gift. It when into the garbage where my money had gone. Stay away from this product and company! It's a waste of time and money.

first, this brown rice flour is absolutely the best!  can be used to substitute for wheat flour in recipes. this brand is always fresh, tastes great & no off flavors.  however, i agree with the other review, regarding how amazon is selling this: without being a "prime shipping" item, the customer shipping cost would be so astronomical for 25 lbs, that i would never order it. i also will continue buying it from whole foods market.  i would order it from amazon if: the price were competitive with whole foods & there was "prime shipping".  customer beware of the cost & shipping charge as currently advertised.  only buy this: if you have allergies to other grains, do not live near a whole foods, and are willing to pay  huge shipping.  also, you may want to consider purchasing directly from  lundberg.

I bought this flour when it was $36 and got free shipping. It's going to last a long time and is very fine. I like it just as much as I do Authentic Foods brown rice flour. Would buy it again if the price went down again.

Brown Rice Flour is a staple in my household due to the digestive needs of my household, so I needed to find a way to purchase it in bulk without buying out Whole Foods every month when I went so I checked on Amazon since I had Prime. It was really awkward at first and we considered not purchasing the item because instead of a bag of Brown Rice Flour or the like, there's a bottle of Calcium/Magnesium plus minerals liquid vitamin. And not even by the same company that the rice flour is claimed to be from. But we've always had a good experience buying from Amazon, LLC. So we risked it, knowing we could get our money back if something was wrong.Yet, once we got it and liked the product I went to bookmark it's location on Amazon and came across the fact that it was now TWICE as expensive as it had been, and we're not talking a $2 item going up to $4 but a $34 going up to $69. That's a helluva large chunk. I get Rice flour at retail for about $1.99 from Whole Food's. At $34, this was just slightly cheaper but now it's even more expensive to buy as a bulk than I'd have to pay at Whole Foods? I won't be purchasing again. Not only that, but now despite the fact that I bought it from Amazon, LLC in my orders list, the link sent me back to it now being sold by Nutricity. It may be more of an annoyance to buy from Whole Foods, but at least I know the price won't change on me the moment I purchase another bag.Five Points/Five Stars1. Item Quality - Good2. Company Behavior - Bad3. Timeliness - On Time (Amazon Prime)4. Price - Was good, changed the moment I bought it = Bad5. Experience - BadTo make a note, I know it's expensive to ship something which is the reason I suspect the price was changed when they realized that with Prime they had to cover a helluva shipping price but they should have figured that out before putting an item up for sale. I would have been buying a 25# bag every month or so at that price and now they've lost me as a customer completely because of their bad practices.

My husband is GF and a vegan-- we make these using egg replacer and do the option with oil instead of margarine.  They are really really good!  Very moist!  Easy to bake and never last long in this house!  Yummy!

column9: Way way way too much nutmeg
column10: If I had wanted a nutmeg muffin I would have made nutmeg muffins.  You can smell the nutmeg in the mix the second you cut open the bag.  If you're not a BIG fan of nutmeg you will want to pass on these.

I've been gluten free for almost two years. I have tried many diffrent mixes for muffins, brownies, breads, etc. King Arthur is one of the best I've found. These muffins are great because you can add whatever you want to the muffins to suit you or your families taste. I make a batch then freeze them to use as needed. They defrost great!

column9: Good crumb and texture. Too much nutmeg.
column10: I was happy to see that the cupcakes baked up golden and beautiful. They were moist and had a nice texture. Very very close to the non-gluten free kind. What I wasn't happy about was the overwhelming flavor of nutmeg. If KAF tweaks this recipe and reduces the nutmeg, they'll have a star winner!

These muffins are SO moist and delicious.  One comment said if you don't like nutmeg, don't buy, but I don't taste a trace of nutmeg in this.  We added in chocolate chips and substituted 4 Tbsp of the butter with pumpkin puree.  Still tasted just as good and just as moist with the substitutions or without, plus you get the added vitamins and reduction of fat!  This will be a staple in my pantry!
Excellent muffin mix. Add in blueberries or peaches and it makes quite a few more muffins than the box estimates. Only muffin mix I will buy.
Very moist, freezes well.  My 9 YO loves the mix with added banana with chocolate chips.  I have tried raspberry and cranberry as well.  Have tried many mixes so far, and this one is a keeper.

So far this is the best gluten free muffin mix. I've tried so many products available out there. I was actually shocked that this one was sooooo good. I didn't think that gluten free baking products can ever be that good compared to regular ones. I'd prefer this over a regular muffin. I add berries. There's no grainy texture and the flavor is good. My daughter is gluten free (I'm not) and it feels good to enjoy food together and not have to have separate food. I'm just so sad that the only specialty store that has this brand in our area is no longer selling it. I'll have to get it online now.

These muffins are dangerously tasty! It's hard to not eat them all immediately. They are light, springy and sweet without being too sweet. I've made them with fresh blueberries and dried cranberries--both were excellent. Made these for guests recently--none of whom are gluten free and they all raved about them and ate at least two per person. Highly recommend.

I loved these muffins! I added a cup of blueberries instead of the recommended 1.5 cups. It was plenty! I didn't taste the nutmeg like some of the other reviewers stated, and I thought they had a nice flavor-- I don't think they tasted gluten-free at all, and my gluten-loving husband agrees!! They have been out of the oven for an hour and half of them are already gone :)I look forward to buying this mix more often and trying out different mix-ins: chocolate chips, pumpkin+streusel, cranberry almond, etc. These are fabulous and so versatile!!The box says that it makes 12 muffins, but after adding the blueberries, I made a batch of 16... not too shabby for a gluten free mix!!

This is the best taste and best result I can get. I tried other brand but the taste was far worse than this one. Interestingly, I can't found this from Whole Food. I used olive oil to replace butter, it is good and healthy.

Wow. I have tried a lot of GF stuff over the past 8 years and I have to say this is something I will buy over and over. It's been 8 years since i had a muffin and these were just like I remember muffins being! It could have been a regular wheat flour one! It calls for 1.5 cups of chips or whatever-add-in, but I put in less than 1 cup of little choc chips and they were SO good. Moist, great flavor, not grainy texture. AND they didn't dry out in a day like GF corn muffins or cookies seem to. If I have a complaint at all it's that they are WAY TOO expensive.

column9: King Arthur Gluten free muffin mix.
column10: GREAT product! My husband and I are new to Gluten free products.  These were so lite and fluffy!!  I added Walnut pieces and raisins.  Sooo Good.  I will be  placing another order soon!!

These muffins made me so so happy. They didn't crumble in my hands, they didn't weigh 5 lbs, and they froze/reheated well which is important to me since I only bake GF for myself (although these were honestly so good, I ate WAY more than I should have before saving the rest for another day!). TRY THEM.

column9: Delicious, and surprisingly passable as a normal muffin!
column10: Ok, I agree that there was a strong scent of nutmeg when you opened the bag, but I don't find it overpowers the flavor of the muffin. But, I like nutmeg and keep whole nutmegs to freshly grate into my baking, so I might not be the best to say it's not too overpowering.The first time I made these I didn't pay enough attention to the instructions. I figured hand mixing would probably be fine, and my batter was super thick. I made 'coffee cake' muffins with a layer of streusel inside, then a little on top. They completely caved in and while they actually tasted good they were a huge crumbly mess and had holes in the center.The second time I made them I did it exactly as instructed and they turned out great. I put in 1.5C of fresh blueberries and they did sink to the bottom. I found that to be too many as well, it was just a mouthful of blueberry in the lower half and no cake. Next time I'll just use fewer blueberries. But they rose well, stayed in one piece (so long as I was gentle with them, not for toddler hands), and tasted fantastic! I would say almost the same as gluteny muffins. They were light, airy, spongy, and delicious. I sprinkled the tops with a touch of plain white sugar just for fun.I'll make these again and again. I like not having to mix out a million flours and starches that are light as air and fly all over my kitchen when I make homemade recipes. So I'll take the convenience, I think King Arthur hit the mark on these!4/5 stars b/c if you follow the instructions, they are a total pain to make, to be honest, and b/c they don't really brown on top, take a little longer than expected to bake, and still have a tendency to crumble if you're not careful. But pretty darn good for a boxed mix.

This muffin mix is awesome! When you first open the package, the nutmeg smell is pretty strong. At first I was worried that it would be too overwhelming but it wasn't. I made a sampler batch (using oil instead of butter) of cinnamon muffins, blueberry muffins, and chocolate chips muffins and they were all delicious. I had to remind myself that they were in fact gluten free and I wasn't going to get sick from them! Now my sister and I are both addicted to these, they taste just like the muffins we grew up on.

The whole family (including the still gluten-eating grandparents) enjoyed these muffins.  The texture was wonderful.  We did see that our "mix-ins" mostly sank to the bottom, but I did not mix until thickened as the directions stated.  There were a lot of very specific directions - read carefully before you start.  I see several others had issues with nutmeg - I did not notice any nutmeg in the recipe at all - the flavor of the base recipe was perfect.(We used Dari-free milk in the recipe and added in frozen blueberries and mini chocolate chips, with cinnamon sugar on top)

Combine Millet flour with White Rice Flour (3/4 C Millet + 1/4 White Rice) for most baking recipes.  The White Rice gives the Millet the needed glutinous texture to resemble gluten flours.  You can use most recipes by just substituting this combination. I caution you not to open the Amazon box or the inner box with a box cutter or anything that might puncture the bags of Millet flour. I learned this by experience and having to repackage the product.  Happy baking!

With rare exception, the Amazon site is the most cost-efficient for purchasing gluten-free flours. This BRM Millet Flour is no exception to this! (Plus, it's actually in stock, which can't be said for many of my local stores.) I've used this flour in a recipe for GF fig newtons and now GF flour tortillas. It is terrific to have this in my repertoire so I can add the texture and weight of millet to my baked goods!
This one from MTR is a sure hit in our family! This is a must-have for us on camping trips - breakfast is quick, easy & tasty before heading out to hike or bike!
..of "big cups." These are two regular Reese's in one. They arrived still half-chilled from the post office. You wouldn't want to buy this for yourself...let me have it. :)

I got these for my sister, she loved them, although when she got them they were somewhat melted.. If you like Reeses then this is your dream...lol. I personally boycott all Hershey products due to their production of candy in Mexico. If Hershey cared more about American jobs I would rate the it five stars. I feel all processed food from Mexico questionable...lead content and such.

The Republic of Tea - Pineapple Lychee Hibiscus tea is one of the best teas that I have had in a long time.  The fragrance of the tea is amazing and the taste is just as fresh. Steeping two bags in a cup of hot water and then pouring over ice is a refreshing pick me up in the late afternoon.  I would have never known how well Hibiscus Flowers and Pinapple Fruit compliment one another if I hadn't tried this tea, it just tastes beautiful!

column9: A favorite from Republic of Tea
column10: Pineapple Lychee Hibiscus has a very pleasant flavor, fruity and sweet.  It's a pretty light pink color when steeped - it tastes great warm but it's also very refreshing as a cold tea, especially in the summer.  This is a great alternative to juice!Another benefit of this tea is that some sources say that Hibiscus can lower blood pressure!  On another note however, if you have low blood pressure already, then you may not want to consume too much hibiscus in any form... This is just what I've read from multiple online sources - google hibiscus & blood pressure for more information.
I love this tea. i bought a couple of flavors, Pineapple, and Blueberry. The flavors are really good and I highly recommend them.

I don't know why but my dogs are not interested in these treats.  They love chewing on other brands of bully sticks but not this one.  I guess they all have their favorites like people do. They don't compare to bully sticks which are meatier and tastier looking.  But who knows, your dog(s) may like them?

My darling dog is a picky eater.  We have given away a lot of snacks because she refused to eat the snack. She paused on it for a little while but she eventually chewed one.  After that, she would eat one every time we put it out for her.  She likes beefy chews and this one meets her criteria.Beefeaters Beef Twists, 5-Inch (Pack of 75 Twists) Its so nice to give her a good treat with a good price.  Of course, I would like to see the price cheaper but it is comparable in price to others and this one meets a picky eater and wins.
I love this gum and it last quite a long time.  Best way to buy is in bulk so buying the 10-pack is well worth it.

Purchased this gum from Amazon since it is hard to find in the stores sometimes. Price is about the same as buying in the store, but subscribe and save is convenient. This gum is delicious; it is minty without being too strong and just a little sweet. I find many other similarly packaged gums (like Eclipse) just too strong and kind of bitter. Oh, and it also has a gooey center. Always have it in my purse!
I couldn't find this gum anywhere, but have subsequently learned it is available in a package of three at Target.

I was excited to try this tea, but was a little disappointed when I finally did. I like my tea strong, and I had to use a lot of this tea to give it the strength I desired. It doesn't have a whole lot of flavor, either.

column9: RIP OFF ALERT! DO NOT PURCHASE!
column10: Same comment as previous reviewer. Only rec'd 1 bag not 30. Weight is 3.5 oz NOT 7.9 lbs as advertised. RIP OFF!  Pop N' Bites Choice Cubes Dog Treats, 30-Count
I received ONE TINY BAG of 30 treats instead of 7.8 pounds (30 bags.) There must be a glitch because after reporting it twice, it still hasn't been corrected.

Sorry, I've had far better Kona coffee than this. I guess I'll have to suffer through the high prices if I really want the flavor. This particular coffee was no better than the average stuff, non-Kona, that I buy at the grocery store.

love this coffee.. i was a little skeptical at first because you have so many "kona" at the grocery store and with different brands but by far this is the best I've ever tried! totally recommend it! It's a little expensive though, but totally worth it! :)

Yehuda hummus is equally as good as the hummus you'd buy in the deli case of your grocery store.  It is a good hummus but I wouldn't rate it outstanding.  It certainly is more convenient to have it on hand than to have to run out to the store in bad weather.  The texture is smooth and the taste is not offensive, actually it is on the bland side if you are a garlic lover.
I like hummus, but this stuff is not nearly as good as fresh. We tired of it quickly and ended up giving away most of it. Its not "bad", its just not that good, rather bland and oily.

I typically make my own hummus at home, but this past week for lack of time I bought some Yehuda Hummus in the grocery store here in Panama. The picture on the front of the can looks a lot like what I call Hummus, thick and creamy, full of healthy ingredients.  When I opened the can to eat it I was quite surprised that the "Hummus" was really really watery and looked like it was better suited for drinking than for dipping.  It wouldn't stick on my carrots and you certainly couldn't spread it as nothing would stay on a knife.  I'm not sure if I just received an off batch or if they are trying to get more profits by watering down their hummus, but that was a big disappointment and I would never buy this brand again or recommend it to anyone!

column9: It's okay... just okay. And overpriced.
column10: Not so impressed with this hummus. Then again, I've not been positively impressed with any canned or bottled hummus I've had. My search continues, but for "emergency hummus" to have on hand, choices are slim. I see a business opportunity for someone.Despite the claim of being made in Israel, this hummos reminds me of someone talking in a "Ja'fakin" accent. Taste and ingredients don't really add up.Check out the Ja-fakin' ingredients:Chickpeas, tehina, water. Good so far. Vegetable Oil (Cottonseed and/or Soy) ["what what WHAT?"], Dextrose, salt, "Edible Starch" (huh?), Citric Acid, and "spices".Let's break this down:- No olive oil. They use literally the cheapest edible oil obtainable.- Dextrose. That's potato sugar. What's that in there for?- "Edible" starch? I would hope so! Does the fact that it's edible need to be mentioned? Just what kind of starch? And why is it in there? Clearly a thickener, to stretch their ingredients (saves them $ while they charge you a lot). So they can add more water and fewer chickpeas. As if chickpeas are expensive.- Citric Acid. This is to provide the tartness that LEMON JUICE would normally provide in a "real" recipe.- "Spices". LOL, seriously. They're not keeping any big secrets here! Traditional hummus would call for cumin, and perhaps garlic. Why so vague?Okay, okay. Search for a positive point.Okay: no preservatives. I wouldn't buy a non-perishable hummus with something like sodium benzoate in it. Most of the fresh mass-produced versions do (think the stuff you find in the refrigerated non-frozen section at Costco), and while the fresh variety taste much better, the preservatives really bother me with those.Some might also see as a positive that these cans come with a pull tab and a soft plastic cap to put over the can when you put it in the fridge. I find that wasteful. I now use a Kuhn-Rikon safety can opener, which enables me to put can tops back on, and I also get no sharp edges of the pull tab.To me, Yehuda hummus is noticeably thin. I haven't seen anyone mention this. It will easily run out of the jar if you upend it. By the way, I always open these jars on the bottom, because they're too full to stir (shaking beforehand doesn't help), and getting to eat the thicker hummus first which has settled to the bottom, almost reminds me of eating real hummus <lol>.The taste? Not much taste. The first taste I get is an weird almost peanut buttery flavor (a common ingredient in REALLY fake hummus), though I'm sure it's not and probably has something to do with the kind of tahini they use (I actually have a can of Yehuda tahini too but haven't had the nerve to try it yet). After that, I feel a little tang of the ja-fakin' citric acid. After that, I notice the watery and overly-smooth texture of this hummus. I then notice I don't have much of a chickpea taste. I then feel glad I'm eating hummus at all. I then realize that these cans are too small, and I shouldn't be able to finish a whole one myself in one sitting, even if I do really like hummus and yes I was hungry.I've tried the Wild Garden variety too (in little glass bottles). It was a long time ago, and the ingredients are also ja-fakin, but I think the taste was better, and IIRC it was a little thicker. No preservatives either. Jars are a little bigger than Yehuda cans, and it's cheaper to boot, but not by much. I can't understand why hummus is so expensive, since chickpeas are dirt cheap.Amazon does actually sell a legit bottle hummus in its 'gourmet' section ("L'Epicurien Chickpea Cream Hummus"), but it's fantasically expensive for what you get. However, its truly legit ingredients read almost like a recipe book: chickpeas 51%, tahini (sesame paste), extra virgin olive oil, sunflower oil, lemons, cider vinegar, garlic, concentrated lemon juice, spices (of which cumin is 0.22%). Looks like someone makes it in their kitchen. I told you there were opportunities with this stuff.I also found some canned "hummos" in the international section of a grocery store which came from an Arab country, like Lebanon or something. Now THAT stuff was not even passable, unlike Yehuda and Wild Garden, which are passable, just not great. I've even tried dry hummus "mix" in desperation, one of those big dry mix names like Fantastic (I don't remember), and that was a disaster, on the lines of my canned Arab hummos, actually worse if that's possible. I do like the Falafel from dry mixes, just not hummus.I've never had a fresh hummus which wasn't better than a non-perishable variety, and that includes the fresh mass-produced stuff at Costco, which is remarkably consistent in flavor and texture, despite them sourcing from different brands. I've also tasted fresh hummus made by a friend, and had hummus in two different restaurants, one a vegan retaurant and another a fancy mediterranean place. So I may not be an expert, but I've been around.My opinion is anyone who thinks this is great hummus, has never had great hummus. Or even "good" hummus. You can't have "great" hummus made with fake, corner-cutting ingredients.For now I plan to go back to Wild Garden for my "emergency hummus" quick fix (yes I keep whole wheat pitas frozen for such occasions!). But I'm still searching! I see Amazon sells a Manischewitz brand hummus, but as of this writing it's unavailable. Any other alternatives? Leave me a comment.Oh, if you're in doubt, my hummus philosophy is: don't go with those trukey fancied-up kinds ("roasted red pepper", etc). It's hard to improve on a recipe which is thousands of years old. YMMV. If you're not sure, get the "traditional" kind (Yehuda is at least legit in the sense that they only sell one kind of hummus: "Hummus"! Not "Traditional Flavor", not "Original Flavor", just Hummus!). You also may want to drizzle some olive oil on your serving, too.
I just opened a can of this hummus, and I really hope it's just bad-tasting, and not actually *bad* (spoiled).  It was a bit acidic, and just tasted bad.  I would never buy it again.

Best Hummun in texture and flavor...and always available.  We've been eating this Hummus ever since my husband discovered it in Israel.  When living in Chicago we could get it locally.  But since moving to NM we have my husband bring some back in his suitcase...at $3.40 a can.  This was even cheaper!

Once again confusing profiteering with prophet steering-Rabbi plays the bait and switch. Ingredients on amazonclearly state soybean oil but on the can is listed ascottonseed a potential pesticide and industrial chemicalladen oil which is unfit for consumption and is used inonly the poorest quality big agribusiness-sellout items.I will send this back or throw it in the trash and not purchasethis poor excuse for kosher product line again.Why detox when we can prevent putting toxins in our bodiesto begin with. Yes I am Jewish.
Must be cold for best flavor. Hummos, olive oil and pita bread make for a delecious and healthy lunch.
This is by far the best hummus I have ever experienced. It's good on anything edible.

My son recommended this, as he had discovered it while living in Miami. I had to order an entire case; it's in cans so it keeps and I'm still enjoying it. I have mailed cans to the same son as he has moved from place to place and pines for good hummus.
No complaints at all about this product.  It's healthy and convenient.  What more can you ask for?

A little of this is the secret to my baked goods. Put some in waffles or pancakes, they taste like the restaurant. You know that cookie dough dip that's making the rounds on Pinterest? It doesn't taste right until you add some of this. I can't describe the flavor other than "bakery" or "buttery caramely."I believe this was a limited run, and it's become extremely hard to find.

For those people with dry hair, this will help. You can rub a little on your hands and run your hands thru your hair and it will definitely look less frizzy. I usually put a little on my hair and leave it for a few hours and then wash my hair since I can't stand it looking the least bit greasy. My hair seemed more manageable after only a few uses. Great product and smells good too.

column9: Great for really dry brittle hair
column10: This product is, IMO, more for African American hair, or for very wiry, curly hair with a dry scalp.  It's light, smells great, and is very moisturizing with shea butter.  I've been using it on someone that I care for, and it seems to be working good to stop breakage.  It is greasy, but that's called for! Most products like this are.  I've taken care of a diverse patient population for years and this product is very helpful for some scalp and hair problems.  I use a glove to apply it, and after 2 weeks I'm noticing a lot less scalp 'crust,' flaking, and hair breakage.  The fragrance is pleasant but it is not overwhelming.  One jar is lasting nicely.

column9: This Caucasian family loves this stuff
column10: We have lots of long hair at our house.  We live in a very dry and windy area.  We farm so my kids spend a lot of time outside.Consequently, my girls hair is very dry and brittle.  I don't mean it is kind of dry.  I mean it looks and feels like straw.  So I was excited to try this product.We use this by putting a tiny amount in our palms and rubbing them together until the  balm is warm and liquefied.  Then we rub it through the dry ends of our hair.  We use it on damp or dry hair.It is not a conditioner or hot oil treatment (I think- there are no directions).  but using it this way has been great for our hair.And it smells divine.

I have very dry curly hair, and tried this on my hair after washing. It doesn't blend well with wet hair, so I tried it after my hair dried. The balm is oily, rather than creamy, and a little bit goes a long way. A touch on the fingertips massaged into the hair and scalp gives hair a nice non-frizzy curl. My scalp also didn't get the dry itch it sometimes does. I wouldn't recommend it though, for other than very dry hair as it can get the hair oily if too much is used. Another thing is that it doesn't wash out easily if you find you did use too much.
This is a specific product designed for a specific customer.  If this is the type of product you use then it works well and is reasonably priced.

column9: Great for my Taiwanese daughter's skin and good, in small amounts, on my hair
column10: I didn't get this to use on my daughter's dry skin, but I realized how moisturizing it is - meant for scalp and hair care - and thought, "Perhaps this could solve our dry skin issues?" And it has! I've tried a lot of products since we brought her home from Taiwan, and none have been as effective. I think it would work really well on scaly cradle cap on babies too, since some of the patches of skin I treated on her were kind of like that. I use it about once or twice a week, and it absorbs well, making a HUGE difference in her complexion. In the winter, I'll try it on the areas where I get dry skin - my feet, elbows, knees, and hands.For me - a Caucasian woman - I just use a little on my palms and smoothed through my hair to increase shine and moisture while taming fly aways. Works well for that!

I have very curly hair that tends to get dry and frizzy quickly. I use this balm on my damp hair right after washing. As other reviewers have said, it is best when used scarcely. It can turn your hair into mush if you use too much of it. But it really is a good product. When I use it my hair dries looking nice, healthy and moisturized, with no frizz. It's not oily or greasy either, and it doesn't way my hair down at all. I really like this stuff.  I think other reviewers really gave this product a bad rap. It really works and it works well.The only reason I'm going to give 4 stars instead of five is because you have to be SO careful in not using too much.

First of all I find that the perfume on this balm to be a bit too much.  So much that it becomes noticeable to someone near you.  Some people may like the perfume on it, but I did not like it.Next - it leaves the hair sticky feeling.

My son is biracial and has VERY dry hair.  I had tried the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil and had problems working it into his hair evenly, but not so much with it making his hair greasy (my hands were a different story).  Because of my experience, I knew that this product was designed for African American hair (even though it doesn't state this anywhere on the packaging).I picked up the container and started looking for directions so I'd know how much to use.  No directions at all.  Wonderful.  So, I just scooped out about 1/2 tsp and my first thought was, "This is basically scented Vaseline."  I was able to work it into his hair much better than the oil and it didn't make his hair greasy at all, but remember, his hair is extremely dry.  In about 5 minutes, I couldn't tell I had put anything in.  I've been using it daily it does seem to make his hair a little softer, but I'm afraid to use too much and turn him into a giant grease ball.  So, for a biracial child with very dry hair, this is a decent product.  It's not the best out there, but isn't the worst either.I knocked two stars off my review.  The first was for having no directions on the container.  The second was for not specifying that this is made for African American hair.  I find it very misleading to make the product sound like it can be used for all hair types.

column9: Ok if you use it wisely
column10: In case of any confusion, this is marketed towards ethnic hair as far as a mask.  That being said,  I just have very dry hair, and I've found that it's good as a moisturizer for my ends.  It also adds a lot of shine!  Basically it's vaseline that smells really good.  It makes my hair look a bit greasy at first, but does soak in after a while.  Hope this helps!

Here are the instructions:1. Cleanse2. Smooth3. Soothe4. SealI am not kidding. Those are the complete instructions for this hair care product.I have a Ph.D., and I'm baffled.I've used it a few times, and I can definitely tell you that you don't want to use too much of it. A tiny (teeny tiny) amount worked best on my hair, though it still felt somewhat greasy.The product does smell good. Since I don't like wasting anything, I'm thinking about using it as a body butter or hand and skin cream.There's plenty in the container, so I'll probably think of other uses before it runs out.

I recently tried Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy Ultra Shea Smooth & Nourish Conditioner and I really liked it, so I was excited to try this intense scalp nourishing balm without knowing much about it other than it's the same product line.  When I received it, I was surprised to see that the main ingredients are, Petrolatum, Mineral Oil & Lanolin Wax. Not sure what to do with it, I googled it and found a video saying you should rub it into the scalp, which sounds like a bad idea to me - rubbing petroleum jelly, a sealant, into your scalp. Wouldn't that just clog everything up? I also found the company seems to have mounted a massive blogger campaign so that most of the search results were bloggers who have been given the product to review and are all "hey, they gave me this to review, so you should consider going out and buying it". I was hoping to find just somebody on a forum somewhere talking about the uses they found for the product or something, but no such luck.I finally figured maybe it could help the ends of my hair. I have fine, thin hair that is down past my bra strap and I recently used Color Oops on it four times over the course of about six weeks to try and remove henna buildup and the ends are looking a bit dry and raggedy, but I am loathe to lose any length. I finally caved and cut about an inch off the ends and then after washing and conditioning my hair and letting it dry about halfway I put a little of this balm on my fingers and smoothed it through the last maybe six inches of my hair. Since petroleum jelly is a sealant and the first/main ingredient in the product, I figure this will seal in moisture as well as any conditioner left on my hair from the shower. I've done this a few times now and it works pretty well. I've found that with this on the ends of my hair it curls more easily and the curls last longer than normal.The jar says "Moisture Lock Nutrium 10(tm) With Shea Butter", and I have no idea what that's supposed to mean, but I think they are referring to the last ten ingredients in the tub, the ones that come after "fragrance".I don't think I'd buy this again because 1.) this container will probably last for years! and 2.) I think it's a little pricey for a tub of mostly just Petrolatum, Mineral Oil and Lanolin Wax. Plus Lanolin Wax is a little gross in my opinion. It's a yellow waxy substance secreted by the sebaceous glands of wool-bearing animals. I have my own sebaceous glands, thanks.

column9: Like Using Crisco On My Hair...
column10: Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm may work for some women, but for me it was like using Crisco on my hair.  Described as being able to nourish the scalp deeply and to seal in moisture, Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm seemed to be a product that would work well for me.  Regular color "refreshment" and age have dried my hair so that I need a good, deep conditioning product.  Unfortunately, it left my hair greasy, dirty-looking, and weighed down by its residue.My first clue that this was not the product for me should have been the ingredient list - paraffin is the primary component.  Upon opening the jar, I thought that someone had filled it with beeswax that is used as furniture polish and to seal wooden kitchenware. Unfortunately, what the description omitted was that Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm was, according to the label, for "Relaxed and Natural" hair.  Had there been more information provided, I would have chosen another product.  Nevertheless, I attempted to use it in hopes that I would get a better result than some of the other reviewers.Women who do use chemical relaxers or have natural hair may find this product useful.  Those whose hair is fine and straight like mine will probably want to avoid Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm.Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm has a pleasant fragrance.  I discovered it does work well as a hand cream.  I found that just touching my finger tips to the surface and then rubbing my hands together, my skin was smooth and soft.  I believe it may also work well to prevent hangnails and dried cuticles.  For me and despite its alternative usefulness as a hand cream, Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy Ultra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm is a one-star product.  If you have relaxed or natural hair, you may rate this product more favorably.

column9: CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm
column10: I did see a lot of people commented this was mainly for black women but I think if you have a dry scalp, like I do, and you use it VERY SPARINGLY.... it works great and doesn't get greasy in your hair but I can see where if you use too much where it would do that. I just put a very small dab, about the size of a dime, in my hand and rubbed it in good into my finger tips and then rubbed my fingers on my scalp and massaged lightly for a minute or so and it really made it feel softer. I am caucasion with almost white hair and it did not make it look like it was somewhat dirty or greasy like gels and other products do.

column9: Definitely needs a better instruction/labeling system
column10: I've been outside a lot this summer and unfortunately burned my scalp a few times (apparently I'm just not all that skilled with the sunscreen).  I've tried several products to get some moisture back into the scalp, and honestly, who doesn't want more full, 'nourished' hair?Upon getting this, I scanned for directions.  Hmm.  Literally one tiny line on the back of the bottle that could not be more unclear.  Shampoo.  Apply.  Then what?  Do you rinse it?  Do you leave it in for a while?  I decided to wash my hair like normal and apply it to still damp hair.  It smelled great going in, but felt very greasy after it dried. I tried washing again, and even after that it was still a bit greasy.  I saw another reviewer had put it in dry hair and washed the next day.  That actually worked better and did seem to leave my hair more moisturized, but it doesn't feel very good walking around with visibly greasy hair waiting for the nightly shower.  I felt like I had to hide my hair under a ball cap at the grocery store.I also was not aware this product was more aimed at African Americans.  Perhaps my problem with the product stems from using it on red hair, I'm not sure.  I again am open to the possibility that I've been misusing it due to the complete and utter lack of direction on the jar...

column9: Smells Great I use the night before washing my hair in the AM
column10: There are so many bad reviews for this product.. Part of the problem is no directions on how to use.. I used a tad after the shower, I felt my hair seemed greasy.. used the night before I washed my hair ( I wash my hair every other day ) my hair seems stronger and love the way it smells.. I have thin hair.. I think it does a great job nourishing my scalp when I sleep like other balms claim to do.. So that is how I use now- I like the product- Been using for two weeks- My hair seems fuller.. but will update if any extreme differences..

Ok, I should have read the reviews prior to selecting this item.  Hopefully, my mistake of not reading the reviews will save you time & money.I have tried several of the Clear shampoo products and they were great.  I have long (middle of my back) thick wavy hair - not too dry but I do experience a dry scalp sometimes - so I thought that a nourishing scalp & Hair Balm sounded great.  However, this product seems to be for ethnic hair.  Needless to say I applied a little to my scalp - I didn't think it was ever going to wash out; my hair still seems greasy/oily a week later.The product advertising needs to be clarified.

I hesitated ordering this product, but since I often use similar products and conditioners for ethnic hair (I love the Motion leave-in and deep conditioner) I wanted to try it. After a good look at the ingredient list, I've used in in a number of ways, with very good results.  First, it has a pleasant scent, lightly tropical-ish. I gave a friend a manicure, and used it as the cuticle softener. I put it on his soaked nails, used the wet pusher tool to clean and scrape, and then used a damp towel to remove. Then applied a bit on the clean nail and rubbed in as a conditioner. Perfect!I've used in on the very dry ends of my hair, it keeps them from being fly-away. I even rubbed it on my dry feet, put white socks on for a few hours, and boy, I feel like I've just had a spa pedicure!After a shampoo and condition, I put a SMALL amount all through to seal the moisture in. Pretty pleased, just wish it wasn't mainly a petroleum based product.

column9: Don't Know About It's Use on Scalp/Hair But.......
column10: This stuff is great for facial moisturizing!  I have Caucasian hair and my creme rinses do enough to keep my hair and scalp moisturized, besides, no directions came with it to tell me how to use it on my hair.  But the skin on my face no longer produces it's own oils and I am always trying to find a lotion product that goes on smoothly and lasts for a few hours before I have to re-apply it.  This product can be used for that since it has all the ingredients in most facial moisturizers anyway, and you get a LOT of it!  It should last me for about a year if I don't gob it on too thick.  I like to try to always find more than one purpose for an item and this is how I plan on using this product.  It also makes my lips shiny and relieves chapped dryness.Also, I am very sensitive to perfumes and get sick after smelling them for too long.  So far, although this product is lightly scented and I've smeared it on my face, I yet don't feel icky.  Time will tell though....after a couple more hours if I get urpy I'll update this review.

For me, the CLEAR product line has been a mixed bag ranging from really nice to not so nice. I received this early this morning and used it before I bathed  This product has given me a problem. There were no instructions for usage so I used this as a pre-treatment. I dampened my hair and applied two quarter sized globs on my hair. I massaged it lightly on the scalp and then combed it through my shoulder length hair. I put a plastic shower cap on and gave it a half hour to absorb. Right now my hair is pretty dry as well as over exposed to sun and salt water. My hair is also straight and extremely fine.I showered and washed my hair. It felt smooth and soft in the shower, however as it started air drying I realized that my hair was seriously greasy. I ended washing it with a clarifying shampoo three times in total to get rid of the greasy consistency. Frankly, I thought I might have to use Dawn (my perennial degreaser) or Tide to get my hair clean. My hair is still over moisturized but presentable at least.I can't recommend this product based on my experience using it.  It is quite possible that it might work better on coarser hair, but it doesn't do it for fine straight hair. I also think it would help if the manufacturer provided instructions for usage.

column9: The product works but nobody knows how to use it right due to packing issues.
column10: Okay, based on a You Tube video that I found, the product is applied post shower and hair drying/styling.  Part the hair in sections. Rub one finger lighly over the product and then apply directly to the SCALP only.  Repeat only over areas of the scalp needing treatment.  Minimal product is needed.  One jar should last quite awhile and, on the areas I've tested, the product does work.I give this product four-stars because it does work but I'm deducting two stars because the packaging developers failed to communicate instructions and caused way too many people stress and damaged hair.Although I do hold the packaging developers accountable for the number of bad reviews, I am dumbfounded at the number of customers who used this product without doing any research as how to properly apply it.A quick web search brings up a video on YouTube that would have eliminated frustration and hair damage.  Not saying that the manufacturer should have neglected to put proper instructions on the jar or attached them somehow. Honestly, what if hair loss was the result of mis-application?  If there is computer access available to leave a review...the same technology would have avoided the situation that caused the negative review.  The negative reviews are justified because of the packaging but why risk the damage when a search engine would have prevented it?  That's all I'm saying.
I've only used it once. It seems to do as it says but I can't tell considering this summer heat and sweating so much.1 thumb up

I love CLEAR Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy. It's a light scalp balm that nourishes your scalp and it has a pleasant smell. What I love most about it is that you don't need a lot to moisturize your scalp. I must warn you that this balm isn't for all hair types. It seems to be great for people who have thick or permed hair (It says on the jar: Scalp nourishment for relaxed and natural hair). I use this balm after washing my natural styled hair and when I feel my scalp needs moisture, usually once a week. Would highly recommend this balm.

There are no instructions on when to apply this balm. I applied it to my hair & scalp after shampooing, conditioning and drying it. It presume it could be applied to the wet hair as well. It is very concentrated and so a very little amount should be used each time or else would lead to a greasy hair. A rich blend of shea butter and natural oils helps in sealing in moisture(especially for people with dry hair). It makes the hair soft and silky. It is fragrant too.
This is definitely great for dry skin on the scalp. In terms of hair, it made it super soft, but a little greasy. I think it's better targeted to someone with dry scalp.

column9: Good but not enough product in one bottle.
column10: I requested this item from Amazon vine with the hopes that I could give it to my sister because she suffers from intense dryness in her hair. Upon trying it out she marveled at the wonderful texture of it and how easily it mixed in her hair. To be quite honest I was expecting a larger vial but I was happy to see that she was pleased with what I had picked out for her. Perhaps in the future they could offer an economy size of this since my sister has extremely long hair almost down to her waist and more product is needed for a full month or so.

This product was really messy to apply.  It left my hands feeling very greasy after the application.  My daughter has very dry scalp and I was hoping that this would help. This just left her hair feeling and looking greasy.

First off, it would be great if there were any directions to go with this product, then maybe everyone wouldn't end up hating it. I used some of this on the ends of my hair since it's been really dry. I have straight, color treated hair and very rarely use hot styling tools, but I think anyone's tresses could use a pick me up and a good dose of moisture. Unfortunately, even though I used sparingly, I was left with my hair looking wet 24/7 for 3 days. I had to wash it at least 5 times if not more with a clarifying shampoo. My hair is now in worse condition then before I used it. Would never, ever use again, especially after reading that the main ingredients are Petrolatum & Mineral Oil. I can make a better hair treatment at home on my own with 100% almond and coconut oil with a little Shea butter mixed in.

I love this product! It makes my hair so soft and shiny! Before this, my hair was very dull and had no life to it. I tried every product possible and nothing worked! Then I tried this and it made my hair have life to it! It also made my more manageable to work with.

column9: It has mineral oil and other bad oils in it
column10: It smells good. It's made to be used in African American hair or Biracial hair. It works on natural Black hair an on relaxed Black hair. I'm natural and I only use natural oils on my hair. Two of the oils in this jar are bad for your hair, scalp and it inhibits hair growth. No one should put Petrolatum and Mineral Oil on their hair. I guess some people can use it to seal with if they don't object to the Petro and Min Oil.

column4: K. Hernandez "DailyReadz - One Great Book Eve...
column10: If this product is supposed to be for African-American hair, as some of the other reviewers are saying, then this is one of the worst cases of marketing I have ever seen. And the lack of directions for use is not just annoying, it is a huge mistake. I have tried several other Clear products and liked them very much, but this is just terrible.

My hair and scalp get very dry in the winter so I was excited to try this product for review.  I am Caucasian, and have used products for people who are not in the past and they have worked wonders.  Not this one.I put in a small amount and have now washed my hair 4 times and it still looks greasy.  It is very shiny, but the greasiness is just gross.I would not ever buy this product but would recommend it for those of different ethnicity.There are no directions on the container, I wasn't sure if I should put it on wet or dry hair, leave in, rinse out, etc.  I went for putting it in wet hair and rinsing, which obviously still caused problems for me.On a good note, this product has a wonderful scent!

While I liked the Clear oil for scalp therapy, this product wasn't for me. Even though my hair is very thick, wavy & tends to be dry (gets frizzy with humidity) this product was far too heavy and made me feel as if I just coated my hair with Crisco. I tried it on both damp & dry hair & just couldn't get it to work for me. It did have a pleasant scent, that sort of reminded me of how certain sun products smell. But it was clear that it was more intended for ETHNIC hair. It took a few shampoos before I could remove it entirely, my hair feeling greasy in the meantime (and smoke emanating from from flat iron). If you're African American, or have similar hair (Puerto Rican, etc.) this may be the product for you. But for this Native American/Caucasian it didn't work. A better product would be the oil version instead (but use sparingly....a little goes a long way!).

My wife and I spend a lot of time outdoors and were looking for a hair product to keep our scalps from drying out from our Florida sun.  This stuff sounded good.  It was obvious when we tried it, that it is not for our type of hair.  I have short hair and I just used a small glob.  It took a lot to shampoo the stuff out of my hair.  Same with the wife.  The bad thing about this product is that there are no instructions or directions ANYWHERE on the jar, inside the label, NOWHERE.  I was disappointed.  Too bad the manufacturer couldn't market this product with better information.

I have noticed that the clear product line has really been making a name for themselves. I have been seeing them in alot of stores that I frequent. The first product I tried was the shea oil which I loved very much so I was excited to try this Scalp Nourishing Balm. The first thing I noticed was that the balm its self was very thick, like a thick yellow grease but it smelled great. Im not really a fan of grease so I mainly used this on my edges and to moisturize and seal my ends. It also works pretty good on wet or dry hair.But be careful of using to much because I can tell that it can cause alot of build up. Once again,a little goes a long way.
Not a product for my hair. I didn't like it at all. No matter how little you use, it is very heavy and greasy. It was hard to get out of my hair, even with washing.

column9: For a Very Specific Hair Type
column10: I was disappointed that there was nothing labeled on this product or in the description (other than the picture, which I still think is deceptive because just showing a picture of a model doesn't necessarily mean that the products are for one hair type)to note that it's specifically for ethnic hair. Furthermore, there are no directions for use whatsoever - no indication of how long it needs to stay on the scalp to work, or whether its a leave-in or rinse out. You'll want to rinse this out regardless. It's just very poorly packaged. There's one line in the fine print that mentions it works for natural or relaxed hair types which clued me in - anyway, I'm lucky my husband tried it first with his shorter hair as if I'd gotten this in mine I'd probably still be crying about it. All this feels like is scented petroleum jelly. Just go stick that in your hair and you'll get the same effect. It's pure grease, it doesn't rinse out, and it stays locked in your hair after a few washes - unless you have a very specific type of hair, please don't waste your money.

I absolutely love this Clear Hair Therapy. It's light enough to not over saturate your hair with oil but heavy enough to provide the proper amount of nourishment for you to feel and see the difference. Since I've gotten it I've started applying it to my hair every night. I can feel the difference in my hair and having a background in hairdressing I can confidently refer this product to friends and family.

after receiving this product I tried it out. I found it very oily/greasy and hard to wash out. I could not find any instructions on the product itself on how to apply or use it. After reading the Amazon product review I realized it is not for my type of hair. This product is for african - american hair.  I have to read more about Vine offers from now on. I am sure it will be an advantage for my next item I try. I shall  pass this to a friend of mine who can use it.

column9: No instructions, unpleasant feel... but good "curl patterns"
column10: I ordered CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm, 6.7 Fluid Ounce not realizing, along with many other consumers, that this works for "ethnic" or "natural" (read: coarse) hair.Because my hair IS coarse, and very curly, I figured I'd give it a shot.  (My hair reaches my shoulders when it's dry, or to my bra strap when it's wet; it's VERY curly.) After all, it smells good...... and there are no instructions on the packaging.I came to Amazon to read other reviews, and saw that the lack of instructions annoyed many other consumers.  Ultimately, I gleaned from all the reviews, and I think it worked out OK.I shampooed and rinsed my hair, and wrung out a lot of the extra watter. I ran my fingers over the top of the CLEAR Nourishing Balm, rubbed my fingers together, combed them through my hair, and repeated. I am used to being very stingy with Jonathan Product Dirt Texturizing Paste(R) 3.35 oz, so this wasn't much of a stretch.  All in all, I don't think I used a quarter of a teaspoon.After about five minutes, I rinsed. It took more doin' to get out the product than regular conditioner would take.  I'd hoped it would be as easy as when I used to use another "ethnic" product, Queen Helene Cholesterol Cream, but this was far waxier. I did ultimately get it out.I followed with a little Paul Mitchell Super Skinny Serum because it was starting to frizz, and went for a haircut.My hairdresser was less bothered by the waxy finish to my hair than I was, and he saw more "curl pattern" in the back than I could.No one's running fingers through my hair so the waxy feel doesn't much matter, and the overall appearance (with the Paul Mitchell product) and smell are pleasing. No surprising additional breakage. I had hoped that it would cause less frizz, but maybe I need to use it on a more regular basis. (I've been using it for four days.) I don't know if I'd buy it again, and would recommend that any user read reviews written by people with his/her hair type. I'm lucky that I had hair compatible with the product.

I think this is an OK balm at least for it must be used sparingly as it is a fairly greasy mess. I think this maybe best for ethic dry thick type hair it is a pretty good product with a nice smell aswell.

column9: Messy to use. Like the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil much better
column10: I tried both this & the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil in the squirt bottle. The liquid in the squirt bottle worked far better on my hair, was FAR less messy & easier to apply.This product seemed to feel heavier & weighted down my hair much more, giving it a "just out of the pool" look... shiny, but weighted down.If you use this, use VERY little! Although it's hard to do unless you let it warm up & liquefy a bit before using, then you might as well get the lighter, liquid, easier to control formula.Might be OK for an occasional VERY deep treatment, although mayonnaise or oils that you'd eat cost less & are far less messy out of a squirt bottle, which the other product has.Would likely be better for people with thicker strand, very curly hair (afro-american or similar), yet too heavy for my hair.1st two (2) ingredients are petro products, so not my favorite treatment. Has some great ingredients, yet are further down the ingredient list, meaning there is less of them. The liquid hair oil has mineral oil as the 1st ingredient as well, but works well.If you want real natural oils for your hair, I'd suggest food or USP-grade plant oils, such as avocado, sunflower, shea, cocoa butter, palm "oil"(one of my favorites-the semi-solid kind seems to work best on my hair, yet everyone's hair is different,and has different needs, so try different ones out until you find what works best for you) & similar oils/plant materials (some are hard & need to be warmed to use.) Add some vitamin E oil (natural is d-alpha, dl-alpha is made in a lab) & honey can help (& smells nice) as well, although I wouldn't leave it in your hair - give it a good rinse.If you're looking for something to grab quick that does a great job & don't mind the mineral oil, have dry, thinner hair that breaks easy, I'd get the squirt bottle instead here http://www.amazon.com/CLEAR-SCALP-BEAUTY-THERAPY-Nourishing/dp/B007RTR9G0/ref=pd_sbs_bt_1 It works great & is far easier to use.I'm going to keep this for once in a while deep treatment, but for a couple of times a week,this is probably best reserved for afro-american hair & even then, use sparingly.

I may not have truly understood what I was getting when I selected this, but it was horrible. Thick and greasy and nearly impossible to wash out.I think it may not be meant for my hair type- pretty normal (not oily or too dry) dark caucasian hair. It just didn't seem to do anything other than create a gross icky mess for me.

column9: Prepare to do a double wash -a true balm
column10: I wasn't prepared for how emollient the balm would be-I had to get right back in the shower when I realized I hadn't scrubbed it all out. It definitely is "therapeutic".

column9: NO Directions and to greasy and heavy
column10: I could not wait to try this balm, I have fine, thin, long hair and it gets very dry in the summer.  Unfortunately, I used this in the shower and could not for the life of me fine the directions for use on the package!  I put this all over my head and hair and when I tried to rinse it out, it would not come out. I washed my hair with shampoo 4 times afterwards and I still have this grease in my hair.  I would not recommend this product, unless they include directions for use somewhere - but watch out, it might take you many shampoos to get this out of your hair!UPDATE - it is the next day and my hair is SO greasy - I read another reviewers note where they used dish soap, I tried dish soap and liquid hand soap as well as Pantene to wash this out of my hair - it is a bit less but still so thick in my hair - I am just going to keep washing it through out the day (thank goodness it is a weekend!) and try to get as much of this out of my hair that I can.  I have washed my hair over 15 times and it is still thick and heavy on my hair.  This makes me wonder, what ARE the instructions for this product, is it even for your head or hair???

Some hair can really use this - it goes on like axle grease and is thick and heavy.  Like grease, it is very difficult to fully wash off. It wants to stay in your hair.I know this is a great product for a group of of selective people with very dry and damaged hair. Unfortunately, the packaging and the description on Amazon didn't really tell me that.  Fortunately for me, I read the reviews here before using it so I didn't put too much on my hair.  Yet I still left stains on the pillow from the product.It smells nice and I think this would be a great product for the right person with a specific type of hair.  3 stars because it is intensive - less 2 stars for not clearly stating suggested uses or users.

This is made to feed your scalp...but of course it gets all over your hair too...so the thing to keep in mind is to VERY LIGHTLY use this product if you do not have the need for serious moisturizing.  It says it spreads easily, believe them.  A lot of good things in this -if- you need the moisture, has shea butter and vitamin E, sunflower, coconut, almond, soybean oil and more.  Just use with care...I was a little over zealous with my application, its VERY greasy and probably is not for most peoples scalps, it really SHOULD have more info from the manufacturer printed on it.

This product, while appearing to be an easy to use balm, made for one greasy mess and isn't something I'd use again. It took two days and numerous shampoo's to get it out. Other reviews claim that it's for African-American hair, but it isn't labeled or marketed as so and that is why we tried it. We'll be passing it on to a friend with the right kind of hair for this product.

First of all, there are no directions. I've never seen a product without a label that describes how the product is used.I have very dry hair that is varied in texture, smooth and nearly straight in front but very tightly curled in the back. I need a rich conditioner but this didn't work for me. Using less than a drop the size of a pea, my hair is dark and greasy and icky looking.Others have suggested using this as a body lotion but I'd prefer to use plain coconut oil as it's a natural product and solves many skin ailments.Would not purchase again....

My wife gave me the lowdown on this stuff.  Apparently there are no directions for use on the package.....or online!!  Mystery Product!!Now don't jump down my throat coz I don't know about these things, but apparently this product is intended for specific.....ethnicities(We're white, by the way, in case that question was really burning at you).  I'll take her word for it, but that fact isn't really specified anywhere in the product description, and this is further solidified by other customer reviews she read online.However, it apparently makes a good skin moisturizer, but you can't shave with it because it "makes a crappy mess".  It smells great too, and currently is being used as a bathroom deodorizer.

column9: It is Not that I Don't Like It ...
column10: It is more that I can't use it. I think if companies are going to send out their products to be reviewed, they should expressly state who their target audience is in their description. I would not have picked this if I had known it was going to be for ethnic hair. My hair is very curly and frizzy at times but not coarse. I didn't even try to use it because I am too afraid to. After reading the reviews here, I am glad that I didn't try to use it. I would hate to go on vacation with greasy hair.It smells delicious and it looks wonderful. It sounds wonderful ... like a scalp massage, but when it is for relaxed or natural hair, I had my doubts. Here is the product description that "sold" me on trying this out:"Category: Hair CareNEW Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty TherapyUltra Shea Intensive Scalp Nourishment Balm. Nourishes the scalp deeply and seals in moisture for soothing for long-lasting scalp dryness relief. Spreads easily for quick absorption. Formulated with Nutrium 10 Moisture Lock system, a rich blend of shea butter and natural oils, including vitamin E, sunflower, coconut, almond, soybean, argan, and palm.Discover the right foundation for strong, beautiful hair with New CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY a range of shampoos and conditioners that feed your scalp and give you stronger, more beautiful hair in just 7 days."Nowhere does it say who this product was targeted for. It wasn't till I received the package when I saw it was for "Relaxed and Natural" hair. After reading others' reviews, I have to say that I wouldn't dare try it.It is a lovely product. I just don't have the hair for it.8/3/12

This is not a "balm". This is hair grease. Those in the ethnic natural hair community will recognize this ingredients list for what it is-terrible:Petrolatum, Mineral Oil, Paraffin, Lanolin Wax, ParfumAfter these, then the botanical extracts come in. The hair grease formula kills it though. I refuse to use it because it's the same old stuff that has been sold for years and has frankly done nothing for the maintenance of ethnic hair.Had I know what was in it to begin with, I wouldn't have requested it but I'm glad I can expose it for what it is.The term "balm" is totally misleading and as ingredient listing goes, the small amount of herbal extracts in this product is not enough to make up for the grease base.Clear needs to stick with what they know which is obviously not ethnic hair care.

Reading the description, I was expecting a cream moisturizer. It's a light hair grease. It does have some smoothing properties and of course, will make your hair shiny. The fragrance is light and pleasant. As for its promise to give you stronger hair in 7 days, I don't know and probably never will. I use so many products on my hair that I can't attribute any changes to any one. I do like it and depending on price, I'd be willing to buy it again.
