column4: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
column9: No instructions, no information, guessing on how to use it!
column10: The stuff smell great, but resembles Vaseline in thickness. Am I supposed to heat this stuff? Wash my hair and clop it in? Try and get it in my scalp? So I tried to rub it in my scalp. By the time I was done, I could have put on leathers, a T-shirt, rolled a pack of smokes up in the arm, tucked a smoke behind the ear, and time-traveled back to 1955. Total greaser. OK, so I let the stuff stay in my hair while I worked around the house.  About three ours later I took a shower. Shampoo #1. About 25% came out. Shampoo #2. A little more. Figured I would leave it at that.My hair was still "greasy." Next day, my hair looked limp and lifeless, and my scalp was constantly itchy.I'm not sure who this is marketed for. With no information, it's a gamble.  If you need a product for a 1950's Greaser look, you're all set. For my hair (I'm a 50+ white male) it's a waste of time. The product probably works great for the right scalp and hair type, but the marketing manager for this product needs to be fired.

As a name brand hair-prep from the 50's once said in its advertising - "A Little Dab'll Do Ya!" and this is So true with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm. I have short hair, so I used only about 3/4 teaspoon of this on my hair -- it spread like oil and covered every strand of hair in seconds. My hair looked ultra oily, almost like I had used Macassar oil.After a decent interval (hours later) I shampooed it all out with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY Ultra Shea Cleanse & Nourish Shampoo, and thought I would need to use an extra application of shampoo to get this all out of my hair -- but not so. One shampooing SEEMED to suffice. However, later on in the morning I noticed my hair was STILL greasy amd not behaving like it usually does. So I had to shampoo my hair again, to get out the oil.Although CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm has many SUPERB ingredients (including Argan Oil), which I am sure will contribute to a cleaner, healthier scalp (and hair) this formula is too greasy -- I can only imagine what might have happend had my hair been longer -- or very long. I even tried using it as a face cream -- and it just SAT on my skin for hours -- SO what is this supposed to do for one's scalp, if it just sits on the surface??? I don't see any reason for using this.BUT yes, it does smell GOOD.But as far as using it on my hair -- I plan to use it only occasionally because the greasiness is too much of a bother for me. Sorry.UPDATE August 6, 2012: Well, I hate to say this but this (used very sparingly) makes a GREAT foot cream. It even softened my callusses (wear socks because this is still greasy)

This product is truly as awful as everyone says.  Wish I would have read these reviews before going to Walmart.  Now I've got a week full of twice daily washing to try and get this slime out of my hair and my hair will probably be drier and more brittle when I'm done than it ever was before I started!

Quite frankly, I'm not sure if I'm using this product correctly. There are NO instructions about how to use this on the package OR Unilever's product website. I put it on, worked it in and rinsed it out, kind of like a conditioner. It's just OK, and seems a little sticky to me and hard to remove. That would seem to make sense since it's three first ingredients are petrolatum (the main ingredient of petroleum jelly), mineral oil (also a petroleum product) and paraffin (another petrolum product that has a wax subset. There are also plant based oils in here, but they come about halfway down the list of ingredients, so I wouldn't call this a "natural" product. It does have a mild, not unpleasant scent...more like this line's shampoo (as opposed to the very strong frangrance of the line's conditioner). Until I figure out how this is to be optimally used (likely have to find where to send an inquiry email), I'm giving this a "just OK" rating.

column9: I thought it was for balding men
column10: OK, I thought this was for balding men. You know, the guys with the bald patch at the top and the frizz around the edges?My boyfriend has a balding issue, and his hair that does grow is coarse and frizzy, and his scalp gets so dry and irritated I thought this was a perfect product for him to try. I use a conditioning balm from biolage that I LOVE, and this, well, looked like it was for guys.So, I handed it to my boyfriend and he said, "Where are the instructions?" and low and behold, THERE ARE NONE!Then he gave me a strange look, opened it up, and said, "It smells good, but I think I am the wrong color to use this." Then it occurred to me, this is for...well, not white boyfriends of uninformed white girls.He did rub some on his scalp, and all it made him was greasy. Maybe he is the wrong color to use this, but it came with NO instructions at all, and none in the description, so it is not MY fault.

After five days straight standing around, often in the harsh sun, and the annual Comic Con here in San Diego, I gave this stuff a whirl on my fried hay like mane. It did seem to help me bounce back. I just hate the feeling of putting any kind of goop in my hair. But I've felt worse, and it did seem to help rehydrate my locks and scalp. Kind of acts as a shaping cream, but not super well. Keep a comb or brush with you to break it up.

It's hard to add to much to a review here other than to join in the choir.  I picked this up because my wife loves trying new hair products, and I always try them with here.  I didn't know anything about this other than the name "Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm" which sounded pretty simple and universal.  Like everyone, when I got it I wasted time scouring the package for directions (Surprise! There are none!) and then just gave it a shot.After reading several of the reviews here, it looks like this is a race-specific product, of which the packaging gives no clue.  Maybe there are some secret code words I am missing, but I have "natural hair" as in the hair on my head is natural.We have two kinds of "natural hair" in my household, and this didn't work for either of them.  My wife (Asian; long hair) gave up after one try and said it was way to greasy.  Me (White guy; short hair) was a little more persistent.  I tried it on dry hair and wet hair and moist hair, but to no avail.  It works pretty good as a hair gel, and is powerful enough to stick my hair straight up. I could have used it during my punk rock days to stand up my Mohawk, but then there is the overpowering scent to go with it. I don't think it will replace my standard hair gel anytime soon.It seems like this is more of a marketing fail than a product fail. It has a pretty specific market and use, and is not as general as the name and packaging would lead you to believe.

While I have liked the other products in this line, using this was a disaster. My scalp has been itchy, with signs of dandruff, and I thought since the other products were so helpful this would be good as well. Yikes.For starters, there are no directions on the jar so what to do? It's very greasy but I took a handful and rubbed it into my scalp and massaged. So far, so good. I left it on my scalp for the rest of the evening, to give it a chance to work. The horror started when I tried to wash it out. After shampooing it three times, I gave up and just let it dry. The next morning I was a mass of greasy-looking curls. I'll be washing my hair every day until I get rid of this, but I certainly won't try it again.

column9: No directions. Called customer service. Ended up with a real mess on my head anyhow.
column10: The only directions for use that came with this product, if they can be called that (which I submit they cannot), read as follows: "1. Cleanse 2. Smooth 3. Soothe 4. Seal."Huh?I was clueless, so I called the 800 number at the bottom of the ingredients list, got connected to Customer Service and asked how I was supposed to go about using their product. The rep told me to massage the product into my scalp right AFTER shampooing, while my hair was still wet, then to "pull it through" my hair with my fingers and the result would be not only a healthier scalp, but also shinier hair. What I got was a head of hair that could have easily won auditions for revivals of "Grease,"  "Jersey Boys" and maybe even "West Side Story." Good thing I tried this on a day when I didn't have to be seen in public, as it took four very thorough shampooings  before there was any way I was going to be able to take my head out of the house that day. Anybody here have Travolta's number? 'Cause I've gotta nice big fat jar of stuff with only about a teaspoon's worth gone missing and it's looking for a good home.

column9: It's not a Caucasian hair product.
column10: I too was confused by the label and directions. The Clear Shea line in the gold bottles is intended for ethnic hair. Silver bottle line is for Caucasian type hair.  I too didnt know they had different product lines and thought this was a conditioner treatment but the #1 ingredient is petroleum jelly.  I have very curly dry hair but putting petroleum jelly on is not going to do anything forcme but make my hair look like I put petroleum jelly on it. I know this product has its purpose but it's not made for my hair type. I really can't see how this can nourish any human beings scalp. It's not the fancy ingredients it says it is. It's mostly petroleum jelly.
If you use this after you shampoo you may have to shampoo again.  Also, there aren't clear instructions for use on the container.  I'm still not clear if this a hair conditioner or not?

column9: There are NO directions with this product!
column10: If you read all the reviews listed here you are going to find that there are NO instructions on how to use this product.  What a poor idea on the part of the manufacturer.  Give me a break!  To not tell customers the proper way to use your product to achieve the best results is stupid.  Various of these reviews list all the ways that those of us participating in the Amazon Vine program, have experimented in how to use this product.  We should not have to guess at all but we did have to.I for one, will give this product one more try after reading some of the comments listed here...for example using it after a shampoo and towel fry, very scantily and see if I get a better result.  After my shower today I've been walking around like a "greasehead".  Simply cannot wash it out of my hair.  I hate it!

Let's start by looking at the list of ingredients: Petrolatum (petroleum jelly), mineral oil, paraffin, lanolin wax, fragrance... So, there's more perfume in here than any magical "nourishment" ingredient, and far more grease than anything else. Even the nourishment ingredients are nearly all oils.This stuff would be great if you want to spike up your hair. Myself, I hate greasy hair and that's what you get when you use it. It is also nearly impossible to wash out, even using Clear's own shampoos.No sir, I don't like it.

I have liked the other products by this company so I gave this a chance.My husband and daughters have dry scalp and I thought this might help. It's a good thing I got it free because it is going in the garbage after one try. I looked all over for directions on how to use this product I even searched online and found nothing so I shampooed and then tried to condition there scalps with this stuff. It was like putting peanut butter in their hair. It felt like vasalen. Once their hair dried it was an oily mess that wouldn't wash out. So if you like the oily look this is for you:} P>S another reviewer said Dawn will help take it out. Thank you it did help:}

This product is for ethnic hair but nowhere on the label; or even in the description here on the Amazon site does it state that!! I was offered to try this for the Amazon Vine program and I was very excited to do so. My scalp is very dry this summer and I was hoping this would work. As soon as I opened the jar I realized that this is NOT for me! Plus there are absolutely no directions on the jar anywhere! At the very least the manufacturer needs to re-label this product.

column9: not sure who could use this product.
column10: The product description on line that I read, doesn't mention that this is for relaxed and natural hair.  when I got the product, the container says it's for Relaxed and natural hair..  Relaxed to me means curly hair that has been chemically relaxed.  I wouldn't have got this product, had I known that.  Typically, the type of hair that gets straightened is very thick and dry, so this product could be for them.  I would still question even that though, knowing how difficult this stuff is to wash out. With no instructions with it there's no telling how exactly to use this.  As a former hairstylist, I've seen similar looking products used on straightened hair to help smooth it down with a flat iron, but  It's not advertised to use that way.It's thick and by the other reviewers seems to be very difficult them to wash out too.  Maybe similar to putting vaseline on you hair.  It says for the scalp and hair, but to even get on my scalp, it would get on my hair, so not a product for me.

I ordered this because my hair has been puffy, dry and out of control lately. I was looking for something to tame it and bring it back to health. I have used scalp treatments in the past with good success and thought this might get the same type of results.The packaging doesn't list the ingredients on the outside of the label, but the face of the product says, "Shea butter." I don't know why I presumed that meant that this is a natural product because it's not. The first two ingredients are petroleum and mineral oil. Shea butter is number 6 out of 13 ingredients. If you are looking for other unnatural and potentially unsafe ingredients, it also contains perfume. The rest of the ingredients are natural oils (coconut, sunflower, palm, etc).There are no instructions for how to use this. In the past when I've done a scalp treatment, I've used a generous amount on warm, wet hair, massaged into the scalp, coated to the ends of the hair, left on for about 20 minutes and rinsed out. Not sure if this is how it's intended to be used, but I'd guess not. I think this was WAY too much product and left on much too long. You can't get it out. It's greasy and clings forever. After five washings, it still looks the same. I haven't worn braids in years, but that is how you see me today because otherwise you'd see me looking crazy with greasy, stringy, heavy looking hair.The product doesn't say, but I think this is made for African-American hair which I do not have. That would have been good to know in advance. The only other time I used a product made for African-American hair, I had the same results. Oh, wait a minute! Maybe it does indirectly say that it's for African- American hair. The label says, "for relaxed and natural hair." My hair is natural and relaxed, but God made it that way. I didn't think about those terms not applying to me.So my hair is really shiny/greasy- not a good thing in the heat where I am sweating because all the dirt is sticking to it. That's not really what I had in mind. Needless to say, I have big regrets about giving this a go.

There is nothing special or unique about this product. I noticed people are upset that the bottle didn't have instructions. I was upset at that as well but, to not publish the ingredients, that is just beyond irresponsible.

column9: Instructions? Would it have hurt to put some on this product?
column10: I am giving this product a two star product review mainly because there are absolutely no instructions on how to use it on the container.I am a caucasian 56 year old female with hair that tends to be dry on the ends and have a sporadically itchy scalp.  I thought this product would help when I saw it advertised on the Vine program.  And it does - if you use it correctly.I was one of the users that thought this was a conditioning product (put on, wash off).  I used way too much and ended up with beyond greasy hair.  It took four washings with Dawn dish detergent and four regular shampooings to get this stuff off my hair.BUT...After all that, I used just a LITTLE bit in the palm of my hand (like less than pea size) on my damp hair.  It gave my hair a very nice sheen and controlled the flyaways.  And it does have a wonderful fragrance.I cannot imagine a manufacturer NOT putting instructions on their product, though.  Yes, this might be for African American hair as other reviewers have pointed out but nowhere in the advertising or on the balm itself does it say that.  So two stars (and I almost gave it one) but I did try a second time, after reading other reviews.

There isn't much to say about this product other than it works. I gave it to a family member who has a problem with a dry scalp and she said that this product reduced the itching and she loves the way it smells.

I requested this product because I have very dry hair. I guess I did not understand what type of hair would benefit best from this product. I will blame the makers of this product for NOT having any directions on the package OR clearly marketing their product to the right hair types. I am caucasian and I believe this product is made for African American hair/scalp. Once I applied this product, I COULD NOT GET IT WASHED OUT. Took forever.Seriously, people. Market your products correctly {or maybe I'm an idiot}.

column9: Trust me. You don't want it.
column10: I began using this product soon after the Clear Scalp & Hair Shampoo and Conditioner. Love those products. Don't like this one.First, it gives you NO CLUE how to use it. Do you use a little? A lot? Do you rinse it? Or is it a leave-in product?The packaging doesn't tell you!After some experimentation and web research, I decided it seems to be a leave-in product.If you use it, which I don't recommend, do so SPARINGLY. It makes just-washed hair look and feel greasy.Given the benefits of the other products in the line, I can't say for sure this one wouldn't be good for your hair. I can only say I couldn't stand using it often enough or long enough to see whether it had any effect.After a couple weeks, I threw it away.

I was very satisfied with the Clear brand shampoo that I received, but this "scalp and hair beauty therapy" product is way too greasy, and I'm not really sure of its intended purpose. Is it a hair straightener? Is it simply for nourishing the scalp? It's hard to tell since there are no directions. Open the container, however, and dip your finger into the contents and be prepared to spend a bit of time trying to remove the residue. My fingers were greasy, and remained so after scrubbing them with soap. I didn't even consider placing this in my hair.Based on the ad on Amazon that show an African-American woman, I assume this product is for African-American hair. It was surely not for me, hence the rating of one star.

I am not one to give a bad review for I like to find something good about a product. This has nothing good about it. It comes with no directions and I am not really sure what it is. The label says it is for scalp nourishment but I am not sure what that means. I opened up the jar to find a really buttery substance much like vasoline. I put a little on my scalp as I do have a problem with dry skin especially on my scalp but it was so greasy I could not stand it. BOY was I sorry, I could not wash it out fast enough and to my dismay it did not wash out right away and I had to keep washing my hair for a few days before it finally did come out. Needless to say the jar went into the garbage. Do not waste your money! Strangely enough the Clear Shampoo is really good product and I love it. This one is a bust!

column9: might makes a nice furniture polish
column10: I tried this product because it has a lot of things I like and routinely use in it: shea, argan, almond oil, and I am always looking for natural, plant-based products.  It might well make your hair shiny, because it doesn't come out (I have washed my hair twice now... and am off for a third round :(I was a bit skeptical when I put it on, as it has the consistency of wax mixed with petroleum oil.  Thick, so thick it is difficult to apply evenly (or in a thin layer).  It does smell nice, I will give it that, so- there's the 1 star (I could not give it a zero).I used this after I washed my hair last night and it felt greasy, so I washed it again.  It didn't come out.  I washed it again, and went to sleep.  In just a few minutes, I will be washing it again :(  :( and hoping that I can get it out this time, and that it did not ruin the sheets.Consider this review not so much a recommendation as a warning.______________________________________________________________________update: I have now washed my hair 4 times and have not been able to get it all out :( It feels greasy, damp & heavy,  and is getting all over my clothing , sheets.  I would say that this is singularly one of the worst products I have ever used.  I would not even recommend a trial, unless you are willing to live with it.Because of all the nourishing oils, and the consistency, it might make a nice furniture or (wood) floor polish, but unless you like the greaser look, I would not put it on your hair (and am hoping a third wash will get it out of mine).It even made my dog mad! He usually gets walked before I get in the shower, but today he just has to wait.___________________________________________________________________________some hours later... after 6 shampoos (twice by my hair dresser, I came home & tried her recommendation:  Liquid Joy.  Two rises with dish soap got most of it out.  This is being posted for those who tried it and feel like the only way to get it off is to shave their heads (my stylist actually suggested that- laughing :P  If you have not tried it... think seriously about what you are getting yourself into.I read some of the other reviews and it seems maybe it's good for some people with different hair, different issues.  I wish the manufacturer were honest and said that!  I liked my hair before I used this stuff.  Now... I just hope I can get the last of it out.

column9: Works for dry and textured hair
column10: After reading many reviews on this product I had to leave my 2 cents. Reading comprehension is key people, the labeling is just fine but it clearly says on the product "for relaxed and natural hair" which means it is aimed for people who textured, curly or hair that has been chemically altered to be straight...ie the hair that many black and some latina women have. It's amazing how many of you are upset because a product did not cater to your hair type...but its understandable because you're used to everything being for your hair type and skin color. Don't worry though, you've got entire aisle's at drugstores for your hair, I'm quite sure you'll be able to find something else to suit you. Welcome to my world, the world of trial and error when it comes to products for my highly textured hair, its nice to be able to pick up a product designed for my hair type.That being said, the product actually isn't that bad, its much better than the shampoo and conditioner which did not give me enough moisture and left a film on my hair. It left my hair extremely moisturized and not greasy, I didn't even need to apply my coconut oil to my ends for a few days because my hair was just fine. It also smells really good. I will agree with other reviewers that it needs better instructions but as someone who is used to to using these kinds of products, I made it work just fine.

This made my hair extremely greasy. I have very thick wiry hair, so when I got this I thought it would give a really good deep condition to my hair. It turned out so greasy that it was very difficult to get it out. I ended up using dish soap like another reviewer did, but then my hair got really dry again. I ended up using the old VO5 hot oil treatment, and it brought my hair back to life again. I have to admit I was sweating it out for a while.

column9: Use lightly on the ends of white hair
column10: I have another hair balm and was able to compare the ingredients, they are very similar to another product made for white hair, specifically split ends. If you have split ends, this will seal in the ends and keep them from drying and splitting more. Just be sure to use so very little. Rub your hands together and smooth through the ends of your hair. I really like this but the instructions are poor, even for black hair.

column9: Jar of mayo would be better
column10: At least I know mayo would be easier to wash out. And it does actually work. Lord this stuff obviously has to run it's course and wear off. Dawn dish soap might help, but it will dry out your hair and scalp more so. It made me look like a mangy dog that had been dipped with a concoction of sulfur and gramas old bacon grease. Yucky, nasty, unbelievable results. My family could not believe the product came from a jar made for hair and scalp. It got all over my bed linens and pillows. My hubby refused to sleep in the bed with me until I aired out the mattresses and washed the linens several times.

column9: For Ethnic Hair. Not clearly stated though
column10: This is for ethnic hair. The marketing is a a bit poor for it, and it doesn't explicitly say so on the packaging. I thought it would be good for my thick hair for after swimming. It is not.I did, however, give to one my my friends who can benefit from it. She noted that it works very well, adding needed moisture to her hair. It is not overly greasy as many other hair products for her can be. She recommends it.

Well, the product does smell nice, but that's its only attribute in my opinion.  First of all, there are no instructions as to its use.  Does one apply it after shampooing and then rinse it out immediately?  Should one leave it on for an hour or perhaps overnight?  How often should it be used?After finding no answers to my questions, I looked on-line and much to my surprise, others had many of the same concerns. And, like me, some were surprised that this product was meant for the African-American user and not for Caucasian hair.  Even now, looking at the jar, it states "natural hair."  Well, my hair is natural but my L'Oreal shampoo states that it's for fine hair, permed hair, thick hair, etc. but "natural" hair?  I would not recommend this product.

column9: It wouldn't be racist to tell Amazon customers who this product is for
column10: Because my scalp is sore, secondary to a sunburn (a cap is better than a visor when you're in the sun, I've learned) this seemed to be the ideal product for me.  But the tub provides no usage instructions (leave on, rinse, apply to a dry or a wet head) that I went online, and discovered[...]that this product line isn't aimed at me, a Caucasian female with fairly fine hair, at all.  The models on the website are all African-American!  I'm well aware, from Caucasian friends and relatives who have adopted African-American children (or who are in mixed relationships, with their children therefor having "black hair") that different products and different haircare techniques are required.  This isn't a secret, and I don't understand why Amazon isn't more forthcoming, on their product page, about who this product is aimed at.

column9: Not for my hair, very greasy
column10: For one every product I buy comes with directions, but for some reason CLEAR products including this don't. That being said I tried to put it the way I thought it should be used and it's very greasy. I don't like it at all and wound up trashing the container of it. I will add there is a LOT of product in this container so for the value it's a good deal, but for the use factor it doesn't even provide any benefit to me and only issues.I'd have to say for normal, straight thick hair pass on this one.

column9: I'm sorry, but I find nothing to recommend this product
column10: First, there are no directions such as how often it's recommended to use, or as to just how to apply it.Now I'm a guy and maybe it's much more for women.  However I don't like the way my hair stays greasy until my next shampoo.  I like other Clear products, but this one doesn't do it for me.

I would like to submit a useful review on this product however, it arrived without any directions.  The container states that it's good for dry scalp and if you lift the label the ingredients are listed underneath.  That is it.  No directions.  Is this used and rinsed?  Is the product left in the hair?  If rinsed, how long should it be left in before rinsing.  I am very disappointed.  Very poor planning and design.

This clear and clean smelling hair beauty cream surprised me. One thing was tht it as a classy color.. the packaging that matches almost any bathroom without sticking out like a neon sign. The other was there was no loud perfume smell or ugly coloring. It does what it says... nourishes your scalp which helps during drying weather without making your hair a greasy mess. Yes, yes, and yes I will continue to use this product.

This product should receive bad reviews for the labeling alone.  The directions ("1. Cleanse. 2. Smooth. 3. Soothe. 4. Seal.") are ridiculous and make no sense.  Worse, the ingredients can only be seen if you peel off the back label.  And what do we find as the first ingredient? Petrolatum, a product otherwise known as petroleum jelly.  This malicious product has been found in breast cancer tumors.  Applying directly to the skin inhibits the skin's ability to breathe.  (Do an internet search of Petrolatum and you'll quickly find the same research results.)  Oof, bad.  Once it's in your hair, plan on it staying there through 6 or 8 shampoos (unless, as another reviewer has suggested, you use a detergent on your hair that can unhinge the petroleum molecules).  This product is not recommended for humans or animals.

This product sounded terrific in the Amazon description, but when I got it I was shocked that the first ingredient listed is Petroleum Jelly.  Seriously!  No wonder so many reviewers have had problems with their hair looking greasy after using this.  I have thin, straight light brown hair and even a tiny amount a vasoline (petroleum jelly) is going to make it look terrible.  And petroleum jelly (made from oil, and not fancy natural oil like jojoba and the like, but the kind of oil that they make gasoline and motor oil from) is going to take a lot of washing to remove from my hair.I was just about to put it on my hair when I happened to glance at the ingredients and I'm so glad I did!  I definitely do not have the kind of hair that would respond well to this product.  I have a lot of friends with thick, dark curly hair so I'll ask around to see if any of them would like it.

column9: If I wanted hair this greasy, I just wouldn't wash it!
column10: I have curly hair; like seriously curly hair. Additionally, it gets all frizzy whenever it's even the least bit humid. I have tried deep cleansers and balms before so I thought that I would take a stab with this one. The first thing I noticed is that the smell was fantastic! I wanted to put a wick in it and burn it like a candle. The second thing I noticed is that it was very greasy to the touch. Previously, I have put balm in my hair while washing and waited 15 minutes or so and then washed it out. Other times, I have only used the products once my hair is clean and dry and I use it to style. I tried both of these ways and ended up with the same disaster on my hands: greasy, gross hair! You might ask why I tried both of these ways and didn't just read the instructions. Funny you should ask! There are no instructions or directions on the container....AT ALL. I looked everywhere and under all of the labels and found nothing.Therefore, I was left on my own to try to figure it out. When I put it in my hair while washing, it took almost a week to get my hair to stop feeling greasy. No matter how many times I wash it, it looked like I had dipped my head in a deep fryer. When I used it for styling, the same problem occurred!Maybe I am from another hair product planet, but all I can say is that you should pass on this product. That being said, I kept mine because I like the smell!

column9: Old style product that requires moderation
column10: This product is advertised as a  "Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy" and it is. I have a dry scalp and this has been helping. This product seems to not be advertised correctly though it does what it advertises.  Be aware that there are no instructions on its proper use. The oils needed to aid your skin is contained within a petroleum jelly base and this is what you apply. I apply a small dab directly too the scalp after you have dried your hair and I actually avoid getting on my hair as much as possible. If this was the 1950's the 'Greasers' would be using this too slick back their hair. I look at this as a treatment and not a product used all the time. If you get this in your hair it will be like you put petroleum jelly in it and you will have a hard time washing this out.  Note: Though I do not put this on my hair in very small quantities it would add a shine too your hair.

As a Viner, I like to review products that I wouldn't necessarily purchase for myself, and this is one of them (because it's not intended for Caucasian hair). I also like to try to use products in ways they weren't intended for.This stuff is great on my horny-toad feet! (I mean, why not?) I go barefoot all the time, and my feet have been just dreadful, cracked, scaled, just really horrible. I soaked them in soapy water for about ten minutes, rinsed and briskly toweled them off, and then massaged liberal amounts of this intense scalp nourishing balm into them. What a difference! It worked a lot better than other foot treatments I've tried. The oils are pretty quickly absorbed, and my feet smell good, too. It's really quite a luxurious experience.This is a pretty large jar, 3.5" in diameter, so it should last for a while. I like it!

Omg! Is anyone reading what's in this crap! Mineral oil and petroleum! Two no no's for heathy hair and scalp! What's wrong with these people? That shit clogs the pores on the scalp and hair follicle. Why would anyone looking to maintain hair health use this?

column9: Horrible Marketing Leads to Gross Greasy Surfer Girl Look
column10: My adult daughter's review: From the name and the advertising, it seems that this balm is a deep conditioning treatment for the hair and scalp. The large jar came with no instructions at all on the packaging. Opening it up and seeing the very large amount of thick, sweet-smelling balm filling the jar gave no further clues. What to do? Use a dime sized amount? A handful? Use on wet or dry hair? Leave in or rinse out? Put on the ends of hair only, or over the whole head? Unsure, I dived into the shower and plopped a half of a palmful over my entire head, but concentrated it mainly on the ends of my long straight hair. Instantly, I regretted it. My hair felt like I had completely coated it with Vasoline or Aquaphor, and no amount of rinsing or shampooing could remove it. Once it dried, I had thick greasy strands hanging limply from my head, making me look like a lazy teenaged surfer. Not exactly the look this mother of three generally goes for. I read a ton of magazines and have tried about a million hair products over the years, so the fact that this baffled me is even more indication that DIRECTIONS ARE VITAL. It may be a good product, if used correctly, but who knows what correctly is? I plan to use the rest of the giant tub on smoothing calloused feet and maybe as a flyaway smoother on dry hair.

column9: For relaxed or natural hair (African American)
column10: I see tons of bad reviews on here and I would have to say they are very wrong. This is more so for african american hair. And we need the moisture to keep our hair healthy. We are not washing it everyday and this stays in your hair. That's what we want. I really like this product. You can apply it directly to the scalp or you can put it in your hair and rub on your hair. The smell is lovely. Doesn't smell like old school GREASE! If you want a great product to add to the mix, I would suggest using this.

column9: FAR MORE USES, BEST BODY MOISTURE EVER for EVERYONE
column10: I am amazed how horrible the marketing is on this wonderful product. Whoever designed the label with no instructions should be moved to another department or just fired.In the islands we use coconut oil on our skin hair etc. and this is used in a similar way with truly wonderful results. It is far more then a scalp moisturizer it is fantastic on your whole body! Here is the best way to use this product.Take it with you in the shower and wash as usual. Before drying off lightly touch this product with your wet finger tips (do not dip into it you, just want to lightly rub the surface) and rub it into your hands, you use very little. Then while you are still very wet rub your hands through your hair from scalp to ends. Also use it the same way on your face and body and then towel dry and comb through your hair. You use very little and it leaves your skin and hair like silk. I am caucation with straight fine hair and it leaves my hair silky and shiny and my skin as soft as ever even works great on dry heels! If your hair or body feel greasy you simply used too much.I love this product as a body and hair moisurizer, it's tragic how poorly this is being marketed with no explination whatsoever on what to do with it! Great product with the worst label ever. use a little and you will love it a lot!

column9: People are using this the wrong way....
column10: I think the problem with this product is people don't realize that this is a product to use to seal moisture into the hair.  It does say SEAL on the product but if you don't know what that means, you will end up with a problem.  I took a small amount and used it on my damp hair to seal the moisture after shampooing and conditioning and using my leave in.  It can also be used on dry hair to add moisture or sheen.  Basically this is a what a lot of us african americans use as hair or scalp oil to be used to keep hair from being brittle.  Please don't use as a conditioner or deep conditioner as it is not meant for that.  I found it did its job just fine when used in the manner intended.

column9: Use Very Lightly! Or better yet, Save Your Money.
column10: Ok. So I bring it home (from Wal-Mart) and look for the directions on the jar.. What Directions!?Since my hair is dry especially on the ends and in my excitement of actually finding something to help my problem, I immediately hop into the shower and start gobbing this stuff all over into my hair/scalp. Oh NO! That was a BIG MISTAKE!! I had the greasiest head of hair (and I have very long hair).. UGH!And let me tell you, washing it out with your average shampoo won't cut it. I contiued to wash multiple times for two days until this morning in a moment of desperation (lightbulb turned on) I run into my kitchen and snatched the Dawn dishwashing liquid which did help immensely after two good latherings. It's not all out but I'm on my way..Buyer beware of what you are getting yourself into when you see this innocent looking jar of "hair therapy".

I have very frizzy hair so I was really excited to try this product. I wasn't holding out much hope that this five dollar balm would be able to cure years of hair frizz problems, but I was wrong. Clear Scalp & Hair is the real deal.The balm took a couple tries to work, but I definitely noticed a difference. My hair felt softer and didn't stand up as much. I didn't get the greasy feel that I was worried about at all.If you have hair frizz issues, give Clear Scalp & Hair a chance. The product is not very expensive and I noticed a big difference. I found it to be an excellent product that I would definitely try again.

First of all, I accidentally ordered this.  I'm not African American so the product was not for me.  So I gave it to an African American friend and together we reviewed it. She has short natural hair with no processing or chemicals on it.1.  No directions.  Really?  It didn't matter to my friend who knew immediately what it was for and how to apply it.  But we're both the kind that would like to see directions.2.  Smell was wonderful.  The texture was like Vaseline.3.  My friend said the product did exactly what it was supposed to do.  It sealed in moisture.  Both of us could see how gunky and oily it could get if applied improperly.Bottom line:  For the price and ease of use, this ranks high.  A little goes a long way so be frugal with it.

I read the previous reviews for this scalp balm; I'm glad that I decided to get it anyway. There are a number of ingredients in here that would make one think that this would be heavy, but it wasn't. As someone who deals with dry scalp, I'm always looking for hair/scalp oils to use. Sometimes, I  miss the mark and get something that weighs my hair down, and makes it overly oily. Considering that this is hair "grease" this was light and fluffy, compared to the others that I've  used. It had a pleastant smell, and didn't make my hair greasy. I put it in my hair 3 days ago, and I haven't had any itching. I will happily use tyhe rest of my sample and buy some more

This stuff is VERY greasy. It is not made for my type of hair. Once in, getting it out was a nitemare.  Mind you, my hair does smell really nice and my scalp feels great.  But my hair looks like I was auditioning for Grease!This was very poorly marketed and labeled.  For some users, it might be great. But not for most of us.

column9: Seems like it's more a hair treatment than a scalp treatment
column10: Clear Scalp and Hair Therapy - I thought the name spelled out what I was looking for, but the only way this could help your scalp is to apply it directly to the scalp.  The consistency of the product is very much like shortening ... and requires as much shampoo to get it out of your hair as if you had used shortening.  It has a nice, but very strong fragrance.  If you are looking for dry scalp relief, keep looking (and please let me know if you find something!).

I ordered this product to try and I have to say I am not sure how I feel about it.  It smells great but it makes my hair feel gross and it is hard to wash out. There was not directions on how to correctly use it so I have no idea how to use it. All the directions said were "cleanse", "smooth", "soothe" and "seal- but i don't actually  know what that means. I think this product would be nice if there were actually directions on how to use it.

column9: I hesitate to even do this review...
column10: I don't want to give this low stars because of my own misinformation but also can't give it "5' because clearly it was of no benefit to me...I was unaware this product might be more suited to African American hair as the shampoo commercials for the same maker predominantly feature white people.  In any event, the product is akin to putting Vaseline on my scalp and I haven't used it very often.  I can use it in the shower as an additional conditioner and wash it out, however.  I noted the review on here from an AA person and they were happy with the product so really, I would direct you to their review for a more informative look into said product.  On a positive note, it does smell very nice and their shampoo and conditioner are quite awesome.

CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm is not for me. I was extremely satisfied with the Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy Volumizing Root Boost shampoo I received. I thought I would give the Clear Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm a try. I am really sorry that I did. The product has no directions for using it and it was entirely too greasy for me. If it is made for African American hair, the label should say so.  I do not recommend this to anyone.

column9: Naturally curly & color treated hair can benefit from Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm
column10: First off I do understand that this product was not intended for my hair, but that doesn't necessarily mean that it doesn't benefit it. My hair is now just below my shoulders, naturally curly and color treated. Additionally I live in the rainy Pacific Northwest which encourages more frizziness than I care for. Because of all of these things I tend to use many products on my hair to be able to keep the style that I like.My routine usually has me conditioning daily, but only shampooing every two to three. This keeps my hair from drying out and much easier to manage. For styling I use both mousse and hair spray to finish it off. Thankfully I've found a mousse with low alcohol content, but that's next to impossible for a hairspray. Even the ones that are recommended for "less frizz" or to protect from humidity I find dry my hair out horribly. So with trial and error, I have found that sometimes products like CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm can help prevent that dryness when used in small amounts.For this particular product I use approximately a dime size amount warmed up and rubbed through my hands, then applied ONLY to my hair ends.  I do this before applying any other products and while my hair is still lightly damp. The result is that my ends don't frizz out from the dryness and humidity, but that they also don't look greasy or oily from too many hair products. I've been very pleased with the results I've had and because of the amount I use I can expect this tub to last a very long time.*I've also added a picture of my hair into the customer images, showing me a week into using the product on a daily basis.

I don't know why they don't label products clearly. Whatever it is, I have straight baby fine hair that is now FILLED with grease.  I thought it was a conditioner-type product and was excited to moisturize my hair.  OOPS.  This product would probably be very nice for someone with more course, curly or kinky hair and possibly helpful for a dry scalp...maybe for black people?  Duh.  I hate politically correct BS.  Hair products aren't hate products.  The MAIN INGREDIENT IS PETROLEUM JELLY...which I am too old and blind to have read BEFORE I slimed my hair.I do like the smell of the product and I didn't want to knock the rating because it may be a wonderful product for African American hair or someone with hair that is very similar.  But if you have straight long fine hair, I would stay away.  I will be using Dawn dishwashing liquid for DAYS to get this out.

column9: This is for relaxed and natural hair, and it works very well!
column10: I read some of the other reviews and, yes, some of the reviewers don't understand what a balm is.  You apply it to your hair and scalp after you've washed, conditioned and dried your hair (I suppose you could apply it to your hair before you dry it, too, but that's not how I use it).  It softens the hair and moisturizes.  I have natural hair (I'm African American), and this works really well to soften my hair.  Use a small amount.  The jar will obviously last a long time.  I'm not wild about the scent.  But after a while I don't notice it.

column9: Hard to give a Clear Review
column10: and I say that because this product isn't designed for my hair.My father is Caucasian, my mother is Vietnamese.  I have a lot of hair.  I wouldn't call it oily, but in the summer it can look that way if left to it's own devices.  My hair is a little longer than shoulder length and I have rather heavy bangs.In the Virginia summer, my ends can FRIZZ.  And I dislike it, so when I was given this to try, I thought it would be right up my alley.As others have mentioned, there are no directions on the jar, but I gave it a shot.  Let me say this...it smells wonderful!  And I thought I would use it like a leave in hair treatment.  Since it is so thick (someone else said almost like shortening, and I would agree with that!) I used just a bit and coated my hair with it.My hair felt nice as it was drying, but a few hours later it felt heavy, and rather greasy.  I didn't like the way it felt,and I jumped in the shower again to wash it out.The more I looked at it the more I began to think this is not for women with my hair type.  While looking online I did indeed find the product, and it is marketed for African American women.I was very surprised to find that the main ingredient in this is petrolatum.  The same stuff in AD ointment.  WHY would you to put that on your hair?As I stated, it is hard for me to give a proper review as it isn't made for my hair type, but I can't imagine anyone wanting to put AD ointment/Vaseline on their hair.

I have 4a/b/c hair and have read tons of materials about which products are best for our hair type. I thought that it was best to get away from petroleum,  and mineral oil, which are the two main ingredients in the Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm. However, I gotta go with what I know and not what I read. This stuff works!! It totally coats and seals in moisture for my porous, dry quickly hair. It is VERY light and a little goes a long way. Now, when I was growing up, everybody had long, flowing hair, when their mama's greased their scalp twice a week and they wore protective styles. What did our mama's grease our scalp with? THIS STUFF, minus the shea butter. I'm going back to the old school ways with a new school twist on it.

I have a problem with the ingredients of this item. All of the cheap ingredients are listed first. Things like Petrolatum, Mineral Oil and Paraffin. Then comes fragrance. Then come the cool sounding ingredients like Shea Butter, Coconut Oil, Wheat Germ Oil and Aloe. In other words there's less Shea Butter which is part of name of the item than there is fragrance and it only takes a minute amount of chemical fragrance to scent up an item like this.I don't like it when companies put infinitesimal amounts of positive sounding ingredients in a product just so they can add them to the ingredient list. Basically this is a gel of petroleum and wax products with scent. It feels very oily on the scalp. The scent is unpleasant. I really have nothing positive to say about it.

column9: It worked just like it is supposed too for severly dry scalp. Great short hair dressing for men or women.
column10: I am native american and had the worst bout of dry scalp ever. I applied this liberly and it stopped the itch immediately. I let it set for 2 hours then I washed out most of it. I combed throught the rest and put my hair in a pony tail for a week. It cleared up my dry scalp problem. It also is great hair dressing for men and boys or anyone with short hair.

column9: Grease for your hair, and door hinges, and bike chains, and...and...and
column10: Wow! This was not what I was expecting. After having pretty good success with CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil, 3 Fluid Ounce, I was thinking this would be like a gel version of that, but this is nothing more than a big tub of Vaseline from a different manufacturer. It feels slick on the fingers, but goes onto the scalp and hair sticky, as in Elmer's All-Purpose Glue Sticks, Large, 0.77 oz Each, 3 Sticks per Pack (E5022) sticky. Using just a little dab, my hair was compacted onto the top of my head for the rest of the day. I tried to use a little less the next day and ended up shampooing it out. I prefer my hair to have a little flow to it and not leave me looking like a Bob's Big Boy doll. The first (and main) ingredient of this is petroleum jelly (petrolatum), so, this shares the same uses as Vaseline. I wouldn't recommend putting this on your head unless you are absolutely sure nothing else will control your hair and you really want to keep every single hair from moving for an entire day. As for me, I'm going back to my Fekkai Glossing Cream Hair Products 4 Oz.

Upon selecting to receive this product I thought "hip hip hooray"!  Awesome hair masque for my poor, dry hair and scalp.When it arrived - I noted it seemed a bit "thick", reminded me of vaseline.Well, the instructions say...oh wait, crap...no instructions.  Well, whatever.  I'll just smear some on my super long, white girl hair and then do a lot of hair tosses in my husbands direction waiting for him to compliment me on my commercial ready tresses.Then I washed my hair, this seems a little hard to get out. No big deal, we'll just rinse, lather, repeat.......again.......and again.My arms are tired, my baby is awake, and my hair still feels like I dumped it into a vat of pure petroleum.Pretty much because I did.My husband asked me if I was trying something new, while gently hinting that it wasn't good.  He's a smart man.I came to read the other reviews and see if maybe it was user error, and to find a solution to de-grease my mane. This is when I realized I was not alone.Excuse me, while I go buy some Dawn dish detergent.

column9: It works, but leaves my hair oily- Great as a skin softener
column10: OK- to be fair I ordered this thinking it was for all hair types, but I suspect it is meant to be used for more coarse, thick hair- not my Swedish blonde strands. While it does work very well, it leaves my hair with an oily appearance. Something I a not looking for. I also liked the gentle smell of honey and Shea butter. When left with the dilemma of having so much left in the container after deciding it wasn't made for my locks I wondered if it could be helpful to other dry skin areas. I rubbed a bunch into my feet (I teach and am on them all day long so they were cracked heels and sides) and put on a pair of socks for bed. When I woke up the next day they were so much better looking! I repeated this process three nights in a row and my feet look pampered and soft. While I understand this is not the "recommended" use of this product it REALLY works for dry skin too. I would continue to buy it just for this use.

I'm a 53 year old caucasian woman with very long color treated hair.  I've used the shampoo, conditioner, and scalp oil in this line and they seemed to work very well so I was psyched to try this product.  I thought it would be like a deep conditioning cream but it was more like the consistency of Desitin which unfortunately made my hair greasy.  I had to wash my hair twice to remove all the residue because the balm wouldn't soak into my hair.This balm has a nice scent and I'm sure that if you have very thick, curly or coarse hair you might want to give this product a try.  Also, if you are a swimmer you might give this a try as well.  Back when I was a swimmer I used to coat my hair with a product similar to this, put it in a braid and then cover it with a swim cap.  The product kept my color treated hair from turning into green staw on long swims.  Since I no longer swim, I've been using the Clear Scalp Nourishing Balm on my elbows and heels.  Waste not want not.

I wasn't sure about this product, but thought I'd give it a try.  I have course, thick hair and have difficulty with dandruff.  It does leave your hair a touch greasy, so I use it at night to nourish so I can wash it out in the morning and have no dandruff flakes.  This product is a balm, so it's thick and comes out similar to sculpting gel (although it does not style!).  It smells like fresh coconut, reminds me of a day at the beach, very nice! It goes on smooth and really soothes.  In addition to helping with dandruff, I got a sunburn on my part and used this and it prevented my scalp from being dry and grossly peeling! Overall, this is an AWESOME product and I will be using it regularly.

column9: Good stuff, complete lack of information.
column10: I have baby fine hair and everything weighs it down.  When I was younger it was also oily and I had to wash it every day and never bothered with a conditioner.  Those days are over.  Now if I don't use a conditioner I tend to look like something that should be standing out in a cornfield scaring away birds.  But conditioners still tend to weigh my hair down so my options often seem to be scarecrow or Moe (Three Stooges, for you young'uns.  Look him up.)I thought I'd try the Clear nourishing balm because you never know, right?  Well frankly, even after I got it, I wasn't sure what the heck to do with it because there are no instructions for use.  NONE.  It's best guess time.  So I tried applying it to dry hair, very sparingly, and the result was pretty darn good.  It softened my hair and made it look less straw-like.  And surprisingly, my hair wasn't gummy the next day.So then I tried it on damp hair.  I shampooed, toweled off, and applied a small amount, massaging it in well.  Then I toweled again lightly.  And THAT was the best choice by far.  My hair dried soft and reasonably manageable (as much as it ever is) without being limp or greasy-looking.  It's still looking pretty good even on the second day.So based on my experience, what you need to do is run your fingertips over the surface of the balm, then rub your hands together.  Once the balm is distributed over both hands, rub them through damp hair.  If you want to towel off afterwards, fine, if not I imagine it'd still work pretty well.Some people are implying that this is made for softening and taming African-American hair, and that might be so; I really couldn't say because again, the information given is pretty slim.  All I can say is that for this old white woman with dry, fine hair, it works pretty well so long as I use it frugally.It got a star off for the complete lack of information given on the label.  There's no real excuse for that.

column9: A little dab will do ya.
column10: I am Caucasian and I have thick frizzy hair, since I also bleach my hair I deal with breakage. I'm always willing to try a product that can offer any kind of nourishment or deep conditioning for my hair so I thought id give this Clear scalp and hair therapy Ultra Shea a try. Upon opening the container (which is quiet large for the price) I noticed the texture is pretty similar to Vaseline nursing jelly its also reminded me of this body butter I used to use when pregnant. But I still wanted to try it so I figured that since a lot of people had a hard time getting it out that maybe they put to much on.There are no instructions on the container or on Amazon.com so I use my shampoo and conditioner as always then gently  grazed my finger across the top twice, rubbed my hands together and massaged it through my hair and got out.I put no other product in my hair and when I went to straighten my hair I couldn't believe my eyes! My hair had absolutely no frizz and was so silky smooth,and I also had a lot less breakage then when I usually straighten my hair.  I mean I can tell if you put to much its gonna be greasy so just keep in mind a little goes a long long way.Overall this is a great product (if it is used correctly) at a great price I however gave it 4 stars due to lack of directions. This is a product that I will continue to use for years to come and I will be recommending it to others!

Though I have been satisfied with this company's shampoo and conditioners, my small delve into the rest of the hair products hasn't left me nearly as impressed.  The CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil, 3 Fluid Ounce left my hair feeling oily and limp no matter how little was used.  However, this balm is a much better way to go when it comes to dealing with with a dry scalp.  The balm smells wonderful, and a little goes a long way... but even the mistake of too much didn't leave my roots looking greasy.  I find this best to use right after the shower... I massage a small amoung into my scalp, then blow-dry. My scalp feels great, my hair looks good.  I also ran a tiny bit over my hair before straightening, and was pleased with the results.  Very  nice scalp treatment.
Solid Shea Butter.  That is much too nourishing for the hair, any hair, maybe for very brittle hair.  This is a bad idea badly conceived.

Like the hair oil they have I think this product name/description is misleading. The product name is "Ultra Shea" and the product features emphasize the "Nutrium 10 moisture lock system" (a rich blend of shea butter and natural oils, including vitamin E, sunflower, coconut, almond, soybean, argan and palm). Yet, when you read the ingredients, the first four ingredients are:  Petrolatum, Mineral Oil, Paraffin, Lanolin Wax. The "featured" ingredients don't come until AFTER fragrance on the ingredient list, so that means there's not much of them at all in the product, yet they are emphasized in the product features.Having said that, I still like the product. I have frizzy, curly hair and I have used petrolatum products before for my hair and they help control the frizz. My favorite petrolatum type product is Alberto VO5 Conditioning Hairdressing. This product is very similar to that.

Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy Ultra Shea is intensive moisture for your scalp which presumably helps healthier hair to grow. It has a nice scent.  You can smell the Shea butter with hints of floral mixed in. The product is very thick, about the consistency of Vaseline. That's not surprising considering the first several ingredients are oil and wax -petrolatum, mineral oil, paraffin, lanolin wax. Then there's some fragrance, more oils, Shea butter, and more oils.My scalp tends to get dry, so I thought this might be a good product to help with that problem. My hair is long and fine, which made me hesitant to use too much. I didn't want it to weigh down my hair in an effort to moisturize my scalp. The directions aren't very explicit - 1. Cleanse  2. Smooth  3. Soothe  4. Seal (in bold type). I took that to mean I washed my hair as usual and used this product afterward to seal in moisture. I used a pea sized amount and found a little goes a long way. When my hair dried though, it looked like my roots were greasy. I washed my hair again and it looked clean. I think my hair is the wrong texture to use this product, but I have found another way to use it. Years ago, I had an Aveda product to tame fly-aways and it felt just like this does. If I take a small amount of the Ultra Shea, less than a pea, and rub it in a thin coat over my palms, I can then gently wipe my palms down the sides of my hair to keep any wispy strands in place. It also adds some shine to my hair. So I don't use it as it's intended, but it's a product that works for me.

I got this for my husband who's always complaining about how dry his scalp is. Unfortunately, he has straight, fine hair and is Caucasian, so this product wasn't exactly suited to his needs. It is very greasy, even when just a little is applied, and takes several washes to get it all out. I read some of the other reviews and there seems to be a consensus regarding how it's better suited to African American hair type and not so much for Caucasian hair types. One other thing is that this product contains Petrolatum.

Even though this is made for African American hair, I thought it might help my husbands dry hair/scalp. Well, it totally coated his hair to the point of greasy. Even using a small amount was way too much. The ingredients are very bad. First ingredient is petrolatum. This is a toxin made from petrol bi-products. We will not be using this again.

column9: Didn't realize it was for African Amer hair.
column10: I purchased this not realizing it's intended audience is for African American hair types, I have straight white girl hair.  There were no directions and it didn't wash out easily; it was very greasy; it made a goopy mess for me, now having said that I think if you had the texture of hair that this product is truly intended for then it does work.

column9: Great Product... If you are in the target market.
column10: Notice that lovely black lady in all of the ads for this product? Well, about 75% of the U.S. population is going to regret purchasing this. Unless you happen to be among the other 25% who have round, ultra-curly, kinky hair and a dry scalp (mostly African Americans, some Hispanics, some Indians, some Jews, and a few whites--Irish & Italians primarily), you might not enjoy your experience with this. This product is meant for people who have a skin type where they do not wash their hair daily, as it would mean a loss of moisture and this dandruff. Most of the population (usually white people) have flat, bone-straight, feathery hair with an scalp naturally gets so oily it requires washing at least every two days, if not daily. Apply this product will make their hair too oily, and attempts to shampoo it out will be rather difficult. LOL. There is a reason why so many call it "grease").There relatively is nothing wrong with this product, apart from the fact that they didn't do a good enough job in letting people know who the target market is, and thus, plenty of people with the wrong hair/scalp type ended up suffering with it. Perhaps that lovely black lady should have been put on the container to clear up confusion.I personally like this product. It is better formulated and lighter in application than most hair products targeted towards African Americans. I feel that I can moisturize my entire scalp and not need too much of this product to accomplish that. It also smells a lot better than many of its leading competitor products (e.g., Blue Magic, Dax, Ultra Sheen).Another reviewer commented that they disliked the fact that this product because it contained mineral oil. Well, mineral oil can be good or bad, depending on your hair type and personal biology. For some people, it dries their scalp out and for others, it locks in moisture. The ingredient itself is harmless and is GRAS (generally recognized as safe) by the FDA, which is the safest an ingredient can get.

column9: A good hair and scalp balm
column10: I've had problems with my scalp and hair being dry with different hair products and usually my hair is just flyaway fine.  But...this balm makes my hair feel soft, thick, and full.  First, I wash my hair and comb it out. Then, while it is still wet, I put a dab or two on my hands and starting at my scalp I smooth it through my hair.  Next, I blow dry my hair on the low setting.  My hair looks great, it isn't greasy and my scalp isn't dry and flaky.  The very faint shea scent is pleasing.  I would prefer Unilever not test on animals...after all how many animals have you seen that use hair balm?  I rated this at four stars and would have given it five if Unilever didn't do amimal testing.  If function outweighs process you may consider it at five stars as this product works nicely and I would recommend it.

column9: Maybe I am one of the odd ones or just have intensely dry hair
column10: I have pale skin, blue eyes and light yet thick hair. I used a tiny bit of this product on my hair.  Not the scalp mind you, but the ends of my hair.  Maybe a dime size of it. It seemed to make the ends really nice. I am not sure if that is the use of it, for products in this line seem to not have directions, or they say to treat the hair with it, so it really isn't a scalp product.  Unless you have a really dry scalp and use a very small amount of this.

When I first tried this balm, I did apply too much and when I washed it out there was no greasy or waxy feel.Now that I've been using it to moisten my dry ends after each shampoo, I can tell that thee is a reduction in split ends and the brittleness of my processed hair.It has a lovely soft fresh scent and it helps increase shine.Just remember less is more with this balm.Since I experiment with hair colors from time to time, this jar is definitely handy to have on the shelf.

column9: Great stylish balm for dry hair
column10: I've tried the CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Nourishing Scalp & Hair Oil, 3 Fluid Ounce and I loved it, so I decide to try the balm next. It's a great product, very concentrated and it has a nice scent like the oil, but it will last longer. This product is for dry hair, truly dry hair, the kind that one applies some of this balm on tonight and the next morning, the hair had absorbed it. I have such hair, my hair is also curly, and long. So this balm helps me to stylish it, and keeping it shining too.With this product less is more, one only needs to rub a little amount of the balm between one's palms before applying it all over the hair and scalp. It keeps the hair in place if stylished in a braid or a chignon.Its main purpose is to seal the hair from humidity, and this is easily accomplished. The best way to do this is to use the same method I described above,  applying a smaller amount of the balm to the hair right after it has been styled with the hair dryer. It will seal the hair, preventing it from becoming frizzy. This is something I learned years ago from my hairdresser, who uses a very similar, but more expensive  product to accomplish this. I definitely recommend this one to anyone with dry, frizzy hair.

I have to start out saying I am caucasian.  This product is made for African American hair.  This is basically just a tub of Vaseline.  I am very disappointed because I got this after reading this was for dry scalps.  In the winter my head gets very dry and I can only wash my hair every 5 days or so.  But when I got this home and I saw the for natural or relaxed hair on the front I knew it wasn't for me.  Not only that but there are no directions as to how to use it.This product just wasn't for me but was marketed like it was.  I'm disappointed because I would like a product like this but I have a tub of vaseline already at home so I don't need another one.2 stars because even though I didn't care for the product it did smell nice.Update:I have been taking a VERY small amount, a petite pea size, and rubbing it into my scalp then shampooing it out and it has left my hair quite silking and manageable.

column4: Jean  Yates "jean, jewelry designer, book and...
column10: Clear Scalp & Hair Beauty Therapy severely damaged my hair. I had to wash it out three times, the first time I shampooed it out. Then my hair was a tangled, horrible mess.It broke my hair as I gently tried to comb through it.Residue was still in my hair until the next time I washed it. I then was able to get it out.However, by that time my hair was badly damaged and broken in places. I feel it is my duty to warn you that if you have fragile hair you might want to stay away from this product. Stick with your favorites and do NOT try this just because it is inexpensive. I have quite beautiful hair and I am sorry I tried this product.

This product is wonderful for my itch...scalp that is.  Clear Scalp came from Amazon at the best price and I wanted to give it a try since I do not have dandruff, but do/did have a terribly itchy scalp from summer heat and chlorine from the pool.  It works magic after just one or two uses in nourishing the scalp and prevention of that terribly itchy head!!  You won't know if you don't try...this is not a shampoo for dandruff...it works to nourish the scalp!!  Now I have a 'NO ITCHY' head.  CLEAR SCALP & HAIR BEAUTY THERAPY Ultra Shea Intense Scalp Nourishing Balm, 6.7 Fluid Ounce

column9: Vaseline and baby oil....not for all hair types
column10: When this came into Vine, I was excited to see it! I thought (from the limited description) that it would be an intense in-shower conditioner cream. But, it's not. When I opened it, I had two thoughts immediately: wow does this smell great, and ... this looks like a bucket of lanolin.  NO instructions on usage whatsoever! Luckily I figured out that it was not something you use in the shower, or I probably would look like someone who had not washed their hair in a year.  The only inkling I had that this was PROBABLY not a product for my hair, was the "for relaxed and natural hair' on the front.I scooped out a tiny amount...half a teaspoon, and worked it through damp hair. I have thick frizzy curly hair, but it's whitey-girl hair. Um, yeah. This is not ok for my hair at any rate of usage. It feels so gross! But for anyone of a different ethnic background this stuff would probably be great.  The first ingredient is petrolatum (basically Vaseline) and mineral oil (baby oil) so if nothing else I could use this as a body moisturizer! But I'm going to pass it on to my friend from Israel with the most gorgeous corkscrew curls.  Someone else mentioned that they liked this as a flat iron balm; no way would I use this as that. Basically you are going to fry this `oil' with the flat iron. I tried it on a section of my ends and it just made them dank and lank and it left a heavy coating all over my flat iron that had to be cleaned off. My advice would be not to use it for that, unless you want to ruin your hair or your flatiron. What a mess!On the plus side, it smells FABULOUS! A sweet, dulce kind of smell. Almost a butterscotch or butter pecan. LOVE the smell!

column9: Poor Product Description On Unilever & Amazon's Behalf
column10: Had Amazon written in its "product features" that Ultra Shea nourishing balm was intended for relaxed and natural hair, I would have known better (buzz words for ethnic hair).  Unfortunately I took Amazon's brief description (scalp dryness) at face value.  Only when the package arrived were the words "relaxed/natural" clearly visible on the jar.  One look at the product confirmed that this is not intended for Caucasians with dry hair.  The first four ingredients listed are petrolatum, mineral oil, paraffin and lanolin wax.  Instead of posting those ingredients which might have helped online consumers better understand what they are purchasing, Amazon describes the above ingredients as part of a "Nutrium 10 Moisture Lock System."  Who should I blame, Unilever or Amazon, for such lousy advertising?I'm certainly unqualified to review a product clearly not made for my hair type.  My jar of Clear Scalp & Hair Therapy nourishing balm will be passed on to someone who can appreciate its use.  I give low ratings for inadequate product description, not performance.  In the right hands, it's probably a wonderful and useful product.  Please rewrite a more clear product description to alleviate all this confusion.

column9: Made for African or Polynesian-type hair - 4a/b/c, maybe 3a/b
column10: It's a shame to see this product get so many poor reviews, but it is due to the terrible labeling and the complete and utter lack of instructions on both the product and on the Unilever website at the time of this writing.Hair is classified on a scale of 1 to 4.  You can have several types of hair on your head.  Type 1 is straight hair.  Type 2a is wavy, and can be straightened and curled easily.  Type 2b is wavy, prone to frizziness, and hard to straighten.  I have a combination of type 2a and 2b, and when I was younger, had type 3a/b. This was way too greasy for my scalp and hair.Type 3a/b hair gets curlier and wavier as it gets longer, and is not as shiny as type 1 or 2.  Type 4a/b/c hair is often referred to as "natural" or "African" hair, and it is actually the most delicate of all hair types, thereby requiring a lot of care, plus appropriate use of moisturizing products.  That's what this Balm is for, type 4 hair, maybe some very dry type 3s, and if you read the five star reviews, you will see that folks with this kind of hair love it and know how to use the product.So, I am giving this three stars because it is not a good product as marketed, namely, without guidance or instructions.  It may be a good product if you have the right kind of hair, and in that case, you should give it a try.

I love the Clear Scalp shampoos and conditioners, so naturally I JUMPED at the chance to get this.  I, like others who have shared was fooled by the labeling.  It's really an ethnic product, which I did not initially know.  It wasn't for me.  As another US reviewer noted, it might be okay as a light coat on dry ends, but I would not go beyond that.  As another reviewer on Amazon US noted, I will pass this along to someone I know who could use this for its indended purpose.I do have the shampoos and conditioners from Clear Scalp and love them, especially the Ultra Shea Smooth.  The Ultra Shea has an especially pleasant aroma and is wonderful.Had I known this was really an ethnic product, I would not have chosen it.  I am giving it a 1-star rating because there are no instructions and it comes with no head's up as to its intended consumers.  This didn't work for me, but I'm sure it will work for its intended consumers.
THIS PRODUCT SUCKS. IT MAKES YOUR GAIR ALL GREASY AND IT TOOK 3 WASHINGS BEFORE IT CAME OUT.  I WANT MY MONEY BACK. HOW DO I GET IT BACK////

Warning!!! That's exactly what it should say on the jar....along with instructions on how to use it. This product is NOT for Caucasian hair....unfortunately I'm learning the hard way:-( I got this product as a hair masque that would help my dry scalp....WRONG....what it did do is leave me with the most heavy greasy hair, since it cannot be washed out. I have very long hair, and I have never used this much shampoo in my life. The Dawn dish washing detergent help some after 2-3 latherings. This is the biggest mistake I have ever had with hair products.Save your money and learn from our mistake

As so many other reviews here state, this product is terribly labeled.  There are absolutely no directions whatsoever on the packaging.  This is very greasy if used as a hair treatment that you wash out, it will not wash out without several washings, or some type of clarifying shampoo.I have colored and damaged hair that is course and wavy.  My scalp gets dry and flaky, so I thought this would help.  Apparently, this is a product that is intended for African American hair, but no where does it say that.  The only hint is that an African American woman is used in the photo advertisement.  Use of the product makes it clear that this product does not belong on my hair.The marketing and labeling is simply deplorable for this product, and causing people to waste money on a product that was never intended for use on their hair type.  This needs a serious design overhaul.

column9: I like it, but not for every day use
column10: While I'm not African American, I do have very crazy-curly and dry hair, and on top of that, chemically treated. I have found that moisturizing isn't enough, one needs to nurture and constantly feed your hair. I've used hair vitamins for a long time, and now when I saw this product that claims 'Intense Scalp Nourishing' I had to try it.It comes with no instructions of use, so I had to do my own googling. Here's the tiny bit of instruction I found: [...]The first time I put it on I deemed it greasy, but the fact is it only feels that way at first. It seems that the roots actually drink it up because a little while later my hair was not extremely greasy. While the actual process of putting it on is a little bothersome, I really like it.Just to be clear, if you have thin oily hair, THIS IS NOT FOR YOU. I *do* produce oil, so while I like the product and it smells good I still don't put it on as soon as I wash it. I wash my hair every 3rd day, so on that third day I apply it and wear it up. But I can feel a softer, not-so-dry hair and scalp now.

Despite using my magnifying glass,  was unable to learn exactly how this product is to be used. It is very thick and I have no idea if it is to be applied to damp hair after washing, to dry hair before washing, or to be used as a brilliantine.
