There are zipper openings on similar pouches with re-sealable sticker strips that fold down over a ziplok type closure which could easily prevent a spill and provide for a second serving.  THE CHOKING HAZARD OF THAT HIUGE GREEN BUTTON SEAL IS MY BIGGEST CONCERN.Now, as for who liked it - well, everyone!  Babies of the age mentioned had a blast eating the Pear sauce, since that's what it is really, not noticing anything they shouldn't like because when we served it, I made sure to ask fellow moms not make faces and to just say :"Yummy pears & spinach!" with a smile.  Preschoolers who tried it liked it and for the older kids, we snuck it into home-made yogurt with no other sweetener other than tiny bit of agave syrup drizzle on top for them to stir in along with chopped, chunked pears.  Nobody complained at all; not even the parents eating the yogurt until after I told them what it was.  Then they all claimed they could taste the greens straight away - yeah.. right! NOT!Now,  If you eat the product plain, I admit, the first bite has a bright bloom of broccoli or spinach flavor, depending upon whom you ask, but once you take a second spoonful, you hardly notice at all.  I would eat this mixed into my yogurt for flavoring if only to induce my children to enjoy it even more.  The kids never noticed or cared. It goes to show you how much we pass down our own food prejudices to our kids.  If WE wrinkle our nose at something, so likely will they.  Better to just let them try it in a neutral atmosphere.This leads me to my other reason for wanting to try this -- I have an older relative who has had throat cancer & after several surgeries can now only eat pureed items or those horrid sugary liquid nutritional drinks.  I was hoping to try this out on my relative and see if she would enjoy this as a nice change of pace and she did!  However, she can only manage about 1/2 of the pouch per sitting, which is a recommended serving.  There's really not enough vegetable matter in here to make this a decent regular option over say, juiced kale, spinach and carrot, mixed into homemde yogurt but I gave it the ole college try!  A neighbor who is elderly and insulin dependent took two packages to carry in her purse and told me they were terrific options for correcting too strong a dose of insulin or for preventing a blood sugar crash between meals.Given these positive experiences with older folks,  I think Baby Gourmet might wish to consider branching out and thinking about these specialty markets too.  Diabetics and people with swallowing and/or digestion issues need a good, Organic, BPA -free option just as much as Babies do.  Baby Gourmet already has a winning formula and manufacturing set-up.  Perhpas they'll consider this other merket.  I've written to them about it in hopes they will consider possible other applications for their good , BPA-free foods!While I still am disappointed that there's no appreciable protien or calcium in a baby food advertising itself as a Fruit & Greens Mix, I like the product well enough to want to try their other flavors and to continue buying this one as a good Prepared baby Food Back-up option for when I do not have the time to m ake my own baby food (other than Breast milk!).  I am VERY appreciative of the fact that Baby Gourmet makes a tasty product even adults can enjoy and further, that their label is ACCURATE by weight.As has been pointed out by fellow Vine Program member, Work of Life,  Happy Baby Organic Baby Food isn't quite so honest about their content.  Like  Vine Member, Work To Life, I highly rcommend the following book: Feeding Baby Green: The Earth Friendly Program for Healthy, Safe Nutrition During Pregnancy, Childhood, and Beyond and I also recommend the follow-up book by the same author, Raising Baby Green: The Earth-Friendly Guide to Pregnancy, Childbirth, and Baby Care to any of you who are striving to raise healthy children in a grocery store amnnd marketing world full of deceptive labels and advertising.  These are great books to give as Shower gifts along with books on Breastfeeding asuch as: The Womanly Art of Breastfeeding: Seventh Revised Edition (La Leche League International Book) and the nphone number for the local chapter of La Leche League!Happy feeding everyone!  And let us remember to be kind to other Viners who do their best to write more than the mandatory # of words.  I know I get a nunber of down-votes becuase of my rhuematoid condition that makes it hard for me to type with perfect accuracy.  Likewise, I try only to Up-Vote other Vine members who have taken the time to upload images, share real experience and go beyond the bare minimum required of them.  if I don't like a review - I merely pass it by.  Let the Non-Viners be the Judges and Juries.  I value other Vine Members' time and effort as I hope you do too.

column9: delicious and nutritious and perfect for on the go
column10: Giving a baby a nutritious meal is one of the utmost important responsibilities of being a parent. Doing so on the go is becoming harder and harder in our society, which favors fast food over everything.Baby Gourmet's product is a puree of organic ingredients, without added natural sugars. In fact, the sugar content of each 4.5 pouch container is about 1 gram.This puree is like a green smoothie for your baby - guaranteed to provide energy and nutrition without any allergens. Unlike processed foods and/or yogurt, this product is meat free, dairy free, nut free, gluten free, egg free. The ingredients of this product are an organic pear, an organic broccoli, organic spinach, absorbing acid (vitamin C, most likely to keep freshness), and organic lemon concentrate. That's it. No unnecessary additives.Although feeding homemade food is best, this is a close replacement for homemade nutritious food on the go.Full disclosure: I tried one of these to see what it would taste like before subjecting any babies to it. And what do you know? It was absolutely delicious! It brought back memories of what my mom fed me when I was little - apple sauce purees, purees with pears, purees with plums, etc. Baby Gourmet's product didn't taste overly green, overly purred, or sugary. The texture was smooth.I'd recommend these as the choice for baby food on the go.

These are very convenient and require no refrigeration its texture is simalar to applesauce, and it taste fine. My lil one is not terribly in love with it but she tolerates it. I like thats it healthy and relatively mess free-which is awesome for kiddos that like to feed there self. You can try it cool or warm. Main negative would be that its a little pricey.

This baby food tastes good.The pouches are great...open it, squeeze some out, and put the lid back on to easily save the rest for later.My little guy liked this...it did constipate him though (the broccoli I think).I'm planning to purchase other flavors soon.

I like this baby food because it contains nothing but organic, whole food ingredients.  The packaging is also handy, it comes in a flexible pouch that appears to be space saving.  The packaging is BPA free, however I do not know if it is lined with another type of plastic which may be equally nasty.  I tried the Juicy Pear and Garden Greens - it has broccoli which is a super food, however I would add a small caution because it contains spinach.  Spinach has oxalic acid which depletes calcium, so it is not advised to eat spinach more than once a week.  I see this product as a great, healthy choice if you need a packaged food product for six months or older babies.  I see this product being especially useful when traveling with a baby since it does not need to be refrigerated.Update to review - taste test by three kids:  I taste tested this product with three kids ages 2, 6, and 10.  The two year old immediately spit it out on the floor.  Six year old got the worst pickled prune face at the taste of it and groaned, and the 10 year old shouted "disgusting"!  The verdict?  The taste of this food is pretty bad to children of many ages.

column9: Kids are happy campers, but not begging for more
column10: I fed this to our young toddler (I know, not the intended audience) and she enjoyed it.  However, she hasn't aggressively asked for more as is the case with her favorite foods.  That's the only reason it gets a 4-star.
Good, nutritious food and very easy to use. You can just hand your baby the squeeze packs and let them eat. Nice that the food is organic, too.

column9: My 19 Month old is not a fan
column10: I am so bummed, as we have 10 of these left, and they are not cheap, but my 19 month old will not eat this flavor.  She happily eats similar purees by HappyBaby, Ella's Kitchen, and Plum Organics, pretty much daily.  She dug into these right when they arrived, but wouldn't finish the first one.  I was surprised, because she rarely turns down a pouch, but since then, she has refused to try it again.I tried it myself, and find this flavor to be more "green" tasting than the other brands.  The others are definitely sweetened more by fruit, where this one leans more toward a grass flavor.  I am guessing that we've trained our little one to prefer the sweet with the other brands, so if this is an early food, it will probably be fine with your little one.At any rate, you can't beat the convenience.  We carry pouches around in my purse, the car and keep a big stash on hand at home.  I feel like these are far healthier snacks, than the raisins and fruit snacks my older two ate on the run.  Considering my 19 month old has been primarily on table food for almost a year, I am shocked that she still loves the pouches so much.She loves the fruit flavors by this brand much more than this one.

Well, let me start by saying this product smelled pretty good (and that says a lot for baby food as it usually makes me want to wrinkle my nose and say ick!). My baby girl seemed to enjoy the taste and ate a good half of the pouch in one sitting.  I even took a little lick myself and it was surprisingly tasty.  I wasn't thrilled about the opening being on a slant.  My baby enjoys holding these pouches herself to suck out the food and she had a difficult time gripping it properly while getting her mouth around the opening.

column9: From the point of view of someone trying it as snack food, seems alright
column10: Others were kind enough to provide the nutrition info...to me the salient facts are:80 calories per pouch (2 servings x 40 cal), no protein or fat...all carbs 9 g, 2 of which are fiber.No strange ingredients - just pear, broccoli, spinach, vitamin c, and lemon juice concentrate.Made in Canada.On the plus side it does taste alright...kind of a grassy pear flavor, lightly sweet, but not super sugary (which in my mind is a good thing...why condition kids to like a lot of sugar so young?)The cap is nice as it makes it resealable.So I'll admit I don't have a baby...got it because I was curious about using it for a snack (easier than keeping a bunch of veggies at my desk...)  I have to admit, I like the flavor just fine, but the texture is...well...it's baby food.  Which is to say kind of like thick mucus.  I'm sure babies are fine with it.  For me I could add it to a smoothie or something but at that point I'd rather add my own veggies.  Plus it has vitamin c but not a lot in the way of other vitamins or minerals or protein....the food bank was the lucky recipient of the rest of these.I guess for adult snack food it boils down to - taste good, convenient packaging, texture off putting.For babies - not too sweet, very natural, can't comment as to whether this fits dietary needs or not.

column9: Delicious, but possibly unwieldy for little hands.
column10: Ok, I admit it. You caught me. I, a grown adult, eat baby food on occasion. Only the fruitier ones, but still. I will insist until my death that it is no different from eating apple sauce. In any case, on to the review!I was a little hesitant at the "garden greens", anticipating some kind of strange, grassy mixture. It was nothing like that though, mostly pear, and naturally sweet.I love these little pouches, they are (sorta) resealable and easy to eat on-the-go. They aren't very substantial, nutritionally, with only 2 gm fiber per pouch. Definitely a better snack than a candy bar though!I can't imagine holding this bag with tiny child hands though. It's squishy and I can see it slipping right out of your little one's fingers.They are great refrigerated, but do not need to be. They come in boxes, in a box, in another box, which seemed a bit unnecessary in terms of packaging.Now I am craving one!

My toddler grandson does not eat too many foods, but will eat some baby food fruits and veggies.  However, this did not go over, and he wants nothing to do with it.  That being said, it is a good product with organic and healthy ingredients, so I didnt want it to go to waste.  I find it helpful to add a spoon or two to his potatoes, and I also make pancakes, adding some of this in place of the liquid.  Both of those methods work.  I think for younger babies starting out, if you introduce this earlier, you will have much better luck.  One other thing, I've seen a few companies try out this packaging, and personally, I don't like it.  I find it hard to squeeze out all of the food, and can be messy.  It's ok for travel, but otherwise, I wish they would just stick to the glass jar.

column9: Taste not bad. But expiring in 6 months
column10: The taste of this baby food isn't bad, and my baby likes to eat it. I wonder am I not getting the freshest shipment or this product just has a shorter shelf life than other leading brands. My order is expiring in 6 months from the day I received it.

Baby Gourmet Juicy Pear & Garden Greens is quite tasty. I make green smoothies all the time that taste similar, but this is a little sweeter.  The packaging is very convenient for travel or emergencies. One package is 4.5 oz (128g) which is suppose to be 2 servings of 40 calories each. Per serving, there is no fat, sodium or protein and 9 carbs, 2 of which are fiber.  However, the label says % Daily Value: 2% protein, 25% of Vit A, 70% Vit C, Calcium 0% and Iron 2%. I'm assuming that is per serving. It is gluten free.  I'd certainly keep the cap away from baby, but it is very large and has slots in it.

I admit that I don't know much about babies. I don't have one of my own. But I received this Baby Gourmet pack through the Amazon Vine program, and gave it to a friend of mine to feed to her seven-month-old daughter. Let me tell you, that kid LOVES her some Baby Gourmet! She is a picky eater but cannot get enough of this stuff. The fact that it's nutritious and organic is a big bonus. I think we have a winner here.

column4: Scary Gertrude,  the Bad Sheriff for Life "Li...
column9: Never let them see you sweat
column10: I'm always trying to find ways to get vegetables into the small children without causing a standoff at the O.K. Corral.Luckily, mine have become enchanted with snacks that come in squeeze packets, especially the GoGo Squeez Applesauce on the Go and GoGo SqueeZ AppleBanana, Applesauce on the Go.  I thought I would slip pear sauce into the mix without them noticing.Unfortunately one of them can read and he read it and pointed out the words garden greens to his little brother and sister.  Then he pointed out the picture of broccoli on the front.  Both of them looked up at me with their sad eyes that said, "Why, why would you sneak broccoli into our snack drawer?  Why?"Never let them see you sweat."You try it!" "No!" "No!" "No!"So I tried it and I tried really hard not to make a face.  I tried really hard to think of it as 2g fiber in 40 calories.It doesn't taste like pears, exactly, but neither does it taste like broccoli.  It kind of reminded me of eating a pear salad on a small table while sitting in a sidewalk café and drinking a tall cool glass of ice tea.  Pureed, though, pureed.

This is organic baby food and it comes in a convenient pouch which easily slips in a diaper bag. I love that it doesn't come in a glass jar. Love that it's organic and healthy, free of dyes and preservatives BUT the baby hated it. He doesn't like veggies, so this could be the issue, but after first bite he made the worst face and would have nothing else to do with this food. I tried again and he refused again. I really wanted him to like it. I'm actually glad he doesnt because it is very expensive. It's cheaper to make your own purees but this is very convenient if your baby likes it.

Baby Gourmet has a good idea here - organic food makes mommy feel good about what she's giving her baby, and at the same time it tastes good for the baby.  This particular variety, Juicy Pear & Garden Greens, does taste good as far as baby food goes.  You taste the pear more than the green (which tasted mostly like broccoli to me), and you certainly don't smell the green (odor goes a long way with mommies, especially if it gags you to spoon it into the baby's mouth!)My biggest problem with this food is not the food itself, it is the packaging.  "Organic" implies that the food is not just healthier for your (or your baby's) body, it also suggests that it is better for the earth itself because there were no chemicals used & therefore no pollution to the earth caused by growing the food.  It is hypocritical to then produce the food in packaging that simply has to be thrown away because it has no recycling options whatsoever.  The packaging for this food is completely unrecyclable, as far as I can figure out.The cap, although hard plastic like many other food containers, has no recycle symbol on it and therefore cannot be recycled in most recycling programs.  The actual food pouch is just like a juice pouch, which also cannot be recycled in curbside recycling programs - the best some juice companies have done so far is ask you to clean the pouches and turn them in to be repurposed (or make crafts with them yourself).  The plastic spout on this pouch makes it even harder to do something like that, and the truth is most people don't repurpose, they just throw it out when there are no recycling options.While it is convenient, the packaging leaves much to be desired, and would lead me to purchase one of the other organic baby food options out there just because I could then recycle the container when I'm through.

I always try to taste any food I give my child before i give it to him. Well after tasting this Juicy pear and garden greens gourmet baby food, I would not wish this upon any child. It tastes horribly bad and I cannot even see giving this away.

My wife and I are L-O-N-G past the baby- rearing years. Our son is grown and gone.So I found a family member to give this to.She was very appreciative.She told us that "the kid" (my fault , don't remember names well) really enjoyed this product. "The happy face" was in motion during feeding time. I guess I will have to (gladly) take her word for it.

I received this from the Vine Program and tested it on my 3 month old granddaughter. There were times when she would spit it out and other times she would take it with a grain of salt. Honestly, her opinions were mixed and we really couldn't tell if she actually liked it or not. So for this one, I'll say, she'll take it or leave it. I'm interested in knowing other's opinions and experiences.
I wasn't sure about the pear spinach combination but this comes off as a fruity applesauce with no real flavor of the spinach.

column9: The obvious hole in BPA-Free product claims
column10: This Baby Gourmet baby food claims that it is BPA Plastics-Free and Organic. They make these claims boldly and prominently. And thus it is fair to critically examine them and their motives and products and claims and prior corporate history when rating these premium products. I guess we could have reasonable faith in the two features, USDA Organic and BPA-Free, even though we really wouldn't know anything about how these foods are grown, manufactured or packaged unless we were experts and had accurate data on the entire production chains. However, there is still an obvious major hole in BPA-Free product claims today. Many alternative news and safety organizations/groups claim that plastics manufacturers and food companies knew for decades that BPA was highly dangerous for humans, and yet they still chose to go ahead using it for food either through willful negligence and greed, or outright intent to poison the American population (for various conspiracy theories/realities). If that's true, and it certainly could be--since the same companies now are conceding that BPA could be dangerous--then the big obvious hole in the story now is that all these same companies are NOT certifying that the CURRENT plastics and substances they use for packaging and processing are not dangerous and harmful, to the best of their knowledge. Anotherwords, they eliminated the BPA, but the same potential problems could remain, dangerous impurities and toxic substances, and the manufacturers have included no promise, guarantee or certification on their products that they promise and certify they are telling the truth that they know of no potential likely dangers in the current new generation materials and processes. Therefore, the only logical conclusion to draw, based on past behavior, is that these companies and corporations cannot be trusted, you have no reasonable expectation that they can ever be trusted, or will ever deserve to be, and therefore any use of products for babies mass-manufactured by Anyone, let alone major food companies and corporations, or any profit-seeking entity, whose only agenda is profit, should not and must not be trusted or relied upon, and you proceed in using them at your own (your children's) risk. (And, even if they did do such certification, as we have learned in the past 20 years, the certifications of governments, corporations, companies, and indeed most NGO's/think tank's/activists/and lobbyists are worth about as much as the paper they're printed on.)

***I ordered these bags of baby food in the expectation that a baby I personally know, seven-month-old Julius, would just pretty much lap them up, which would save his parents a fair amount on their food budget.  As it turns out, as the result of a long series of carefully measured, double-blind observations involving a large experimental sample size and of course a large control group, it has been ruled out that any explanation other than a constitutional aversion to spinach causes Julius to vomit.  Shortly after Julius eats spinach, he vomits.  Not just mostly but every single time.And I don't mean regular vomiting.  I mean what's called projectile vomiting, which you can look up, in which the vomitus can be exprelled WITHOUT WARNING at astonsihingly high rates of speed considering they're coming from a seven-month-old baby who can barely sit up yet without help.  Julius has ejected vomitus as far away as 10 feet at first burst, which is pretty impressive and a little dangerous if you happen to be leaning over him at the moment.As it turns out, his parents and the other people who take care of him DO have a preference whether Julius eats spinach.  Not surprisingly, they do NOT like it when their baby unexpectedly and at skin-stinging velocity pukes in their faces.  You might call them selfish to deprive him of spinach, but I don't.This product contains spinach in every bite, er, squoosh, so I am unable to test it in the field, on the ground, in real time going forward.  I can say that the fact no one fed Julius this product several times has saved exactly that many episodes of his unwanted projectile vomiting.  For this I add 1 star.However, I also did offer some of the Juicy Pear & Garden Greens version to my dog, PheyeG'hdeaux, and he refused after the first taste.  And this is a dog that will happily eat cat poop and long-dead squirrels.  For this I subtract 1 star, so we're back to 5.NOT A CHOKING HAZARDUp to a certain age, infants instinctively try not only to put things in their mouths but also to swallow them without regard to whether they are swallowable or even tasty.  Few seven-year-olds would try to swallow half a pair of dice, but Julius, at one-twelfth that age, isn't yet that smart.  If he tries to swallow an object of the wrong size and shape, it will get caught in his throat in such a way that his trachea, his breathing tube, is obstructed.  Julius will eventually exhibit gross symptoms of his respiratory distress -- his inability to breathe -- but that won't matter if no adult is looking.  If enough time goes by his brain will suffer anoxia, if enough more time goes by some of the neurons as well as other cells in that brain will perish, and if enough more time goes by Julius will be rendered unconcsious, and if the ultimate amount of time goes by he will die of asphyxiation.So it's important that the cap for this product not be swallowable by anyone with tastes as undiscriminating and survival instincts as undeveloped as seven-month old Julius's.  If it were the cap to the valve stem of the left front tire of your car, that would be one thing, or any of the other four tires, because the likelihood that cap will be reachable by your version of Julius is so low.  But the likelihood the cap to a pouch of baby food will be reachable by an infant is much higher.  The manufacturer has chosen a design for the cap that makes it all but impossible for Julius to swallow it or otherwise be harmed by it.  In fact, you may safely dip this cap in honey and dust it with sugar and hand it to him and walk away.  Or her.First, it's way too big for even an adult to swallow.  I took the opportunity of being in the same room with a pouch of this product and the family's well-known big-mouth.  I asked her to determine whether she could swallow it, and after explaining my reason I watched as she tried really hard for ten seconds or so and deemed it "Not possible."  The collar at its widest measures 1.257 inches.  The height is 0.628 inches, which as you probably know is equal to 0.009373 smoots.Second, the collar that surrounds the threaded part is mostly air, i.e., except for these four thin ribs or vanes, the collar is floating outside the threaded part, which means if the infant does manage to get it wedged at the top of the trachea where it enters the mouth, not only can air still pass through but any of the baby food itself can pass through.NOT NOT ORGANICUnfortunately, this is a product that's referred to as organic.  The main ingredients -- pear, broccoli and spinach -- are "organic," and it contains no preservatives unless you count ascorbic acid and organic lemon juice.  The problem, of course, is that without preservatives the product is more likely to spoil, to go bad.  And going on the assumption that foods labelled organic are more expensive to get from soil to spoon, the price of this product is surely higher than it would be otherwise.  For its being organic I subtract 1 star.EXTRA TESTING-- The goop, while it might be perfectly healthful for a baby, is a perfectly dreadful substitute for taco sauce, salad dressing, or the Alfredo sauce on a Parmesan-besprinkled bed of liguine.  Trust me.-- You might be wondering how well the goop inside, which does taste like pear and even kind of has the grit of pear, works as a substitute for, say, floor-tile mastic.  I laid four one-foot linoleum tiles in a quarter-inch bed of Baby Gourmet 1 Simple Purees 6 Months+ Organic Juicy Pear & Garden Greens, 4.5-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 12) and waited a whole 24 hours, at the end of which time the tiles were not even remotely well-stuck to the subfloor but did attract a LOT of ants, so many that we needed the services of a professional exterminator, for which we will be suing Baby Gourmet for an amount in excess of $25,000.-- When you fire a Marlin .22 caliber rifle at the pouch from ten yards away, the bullet passes through quite readily and embeds itself in the right door of the 2012 Hyundai Sonata that is parked in the driveway of your neighbor three houses west, who will start out incredulous and end up irate.For these defects I subtract no stars, I just thought you should know.PRODUCT DESCRIPTIONFinally, the Product Description on Amazon is comical.  It starts this way:"We think every mom has a morbid fear of feeding their babies vegetables . . ."  First, I find it sad that whoever wrote this decicded to say "their babies" when it should have been "her babies."  One thing we know for sure about anyone who's a mom is that that person is a female, so the excessive political correctness of not using the gender-specific pronoun here is also comical.But second, and more important, I find it incredible that the people at Baby Gourmet really believe "every mom has a morbid fear" of feeding vegetables to her baby.  Not just some moms, not just many moms, not even most moms, but EVERY mom.  That's just stupidly wrong.  And it's even wronger when you remember that it's a MORBID fear, one that is on a par with fearing death itself.  Whoever wrote this is telling us that the people at Baby Gourmet sincerely do believe that EVERY mom has a MORBID fear of feeding vegetables to her baby.  This is insultingly false, and it gives you permission to question everything else they say.  This is an example of offering for sale a solution to a problem that doesn't exist till the marketers create it.Also, I have to point out that the description goes on to say "thus we have made a blend of Organic Pears, Organic Broccoli and Organic Spinach that taste well, out of this world actually!"For the comical mistakes in the Product Description I subtract no stars.  For the outrageous lie I subtract 1.Five stars plus 1 minus 1 minus 1 minus 1 am 3.***

column9: Healthy but my toddler daughter did not finish it.
column10: I know this is advertised for 6 months on but I figured since my toddler daughter (20 months) eats other snacks out of a pouch. I would give this a try.This food is high quality and very handy to give to a baby.  My daughter and did eat most of the food from the pouch, but did not finish it.  She is actually very good about trying new things, but if she does not love the new food, she stops eating it.  Since she ate most of it and it is of very high quality, I would rate it highly, but not a five star rating for an older baby.  I think most babies start liking sweeter food as they become toddlers and their food experiences broaden.  This food is not sweet, due to its high quality and nutritional value, and would probably be excellent for a sitter stage baby.  I was hoping my toddler daughter would like it, but she was not too fond of it.  Of course each child will have his or her own likes and dislikes in foods.  If you want a high quality, nutritional food that is easy to store and serve, then do try this.

column4: Karissa Eckert "Devourer of all books fantasy"
column9: Great snack; but too broccoli tasting for kids
column10: My son (who is five) and I eat these types of things a lot for snacks.  They are especially handy while hiking or camping since they don't require refrigeration.This puree has mainly pears and broccoli in it.  I enjoyed eating them as a snack, but my son didn't enjoy the strong broccoli after taste.This is comparable to Ella's Kitchen Organic Baby Food Broccoli, Pears + Peas (4+months), 3.5-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 7); they taste very similar and the packaging works in a similar way.All in all I thought these were tasty and enjoy eating them for snacks.  My son did not like the taste though; he thought the broccoli after taste was horrible.  These are great for when you want to bring fruits and veggies that are portable and non-perishable.

I think this is a very healthy baby food that tastes great too.  It mostly tastes like pears, but there is that hint of spinach and broccoli that comes as an aftertaste.  Of course, the taste of pears is probably the most appetizing of the three so that is a good thing.  It tastes great warm or cold too.Although the packaging is a little different than other brands we usually get (glass jars or plastic cups), it works well.  The spout is good for pouring some into another container with no mess.

column9: Gourmet, Organic Food Choices for New and Old Babies
column10: The younger generations are all about being healthy and using natural products, which I suppose is good. So I am not surprised at all that moms in today's world are interested in organic, natural products for their babies and toddlers.One of the leaders in producing organic baby foods is Baby Gourmet, an Edmonton, Canada, company founded by Jennifer Broe with the help of her sister, Jill Vos. Their organic food products come in a slim pouch that allows mom or dad to easily squeeze the food onto a spoon. When baby grows into a toddler he or she will be able to feed themselves straight from the package with ease.All of their foods are organic with no thickeners or fillers, no added sugar or salt, are Kosher in BPA-free re-sealable packaging, and carry USDA, FDA and organic certification.For my nephew I choose the organic juicy pear and garden greens choice for 6 months-plus (Stage 1) which also is gluten free, nut free, with no dairy, egg or lactose. The box contains six 4 ½-ounce pouches. Other choices for 6 months-plus include: Orchard Apple, Carrot and Prune; Simply Sweet Potatoes; Sweet Potato, Apple and Chicken; and Harvest Pear, Pumpkin and Banana.I didn't want to take away from my nephew's enjoyment so did not taste the pears or greens but he downed the whole package without complaint. And it its OK with him than I can certainly recommended it to you.

The very first time my grandkids, ages 16 months & 2 1/2 yrs., tried Baby Gourmet Organic Simple Purees Juicy Pear & Garden Greens Pouches, they asked for seconds. At that time, I didn't realize that one pouch is actually 2 servings. They each had 4 servings that day! A couple days later my grandson wanted another helping of spinach tortellini but I decided to give him one of these pouches instead. He looked at me with a huge smile & said, "I love these things!"Curiosity got the best of me so I sampled the puree. It's not watery & holds its shape on a spoon.Surprisingly, I could taste the broccoli/greens & the pears.These are not only great for meals, but can be used as a take-along snack.Ingredients:Organic pear, organic broccoli, organic spinach, ascorbic acid, organic lemon juice concentrateno artificial ingredients, no added sugar, no thickeners/fillers, no added salt, gluten free, kosher; USDA, FDA, and organic certificationEdited to add that 4 servings a day caused the 16 month old to have messy blowouts in her diaper.  I think most Mom's will know what I'm talking about. This was discovered because both kids love these so much that we gave them a pouch for snacktime too. 4 servings a day of the Juicy Pear & Garden Greens proved to be too much for the 16 month old, but the 2 1/2 year old didn't have any problems.5 stars

column9: Cool packaging concept...but is this really a necessary product?
column10: I hate to get up on a soapbox here, but I didn't feed my daughter baby food.  When she was very young, I gave her whatever fruits and vegetables I was having in a mesh feeder, and I ground up meats in a simple, hand-cranked baby-food grinder.  That didn't last long before I just cut up everything (soft, of course) in very small pieces, and then there was no looking back.  I would regard prepackaged baby food as only a fallback item.But if you need or wish to use prepackaged baby food for any reason (hey, no judgment here!), Baby Gourmet is as good as any, but at over $2 for a 1/2-cup container, it seems way overpriced to me.  I do like the convenience of the foil package with the integrated feeding straw.  This particular variety tastes like pear ground up with grass (i.e., not good at all), but it's a good idea to mix fruit with vegetables, so I'm not really complaining about it.  I just don't find anything to particularly recommend about the taste.Overall, this is a nicely packaged, quality product that most mothers won't need often (if ever), but, depending on your situation, it may have a place in your life (if you really want and/or need to use baby food and you don't mind paying a ridiculous price).  You could certainly do worse.

For clarification, all of the enclosed pouches are a MIXTURE of juicy pear and garden greens. I was confused until after I received them.  Now, on to the review!Flavor: really tastes like solely pear. You can barely taste the greens mixed in, which is perfect, since babies love the fruit flavors. Even to myself, it's not bad!Consistency: NOT watery like some other annoying 1st stage foods, but still nice and smooth and runny ENOUGH that it's still good for some of their first foods. This was a huge plus for me... so many of the "1st stage" ones are practically impossible to feed because they spill so easily.Package: A+ for this one. I hated having glass jars for baby food, plus you have a tendency to spoon out of them and then the food goes bad quicker.  In this one, you just squeeze it out  into your bowl, and since there is no contamination, it lasts longer. Yes, I know, I know, they still say to toss after 24 hours, but that, quite frankly, is ridiculous.  Yes, if you have just put a spoon with saliva into your food, then I would too, but that's not the case with these new & neat pouches!  The drawback is that you have to have a bowl, which is not as convenient if you are out and about. But I mix most of the baby food with oatmeal anyway, so it was a benefit for me.So overall, I definitely recommend!

I tried this myself before offering it to the baby.  My initial reaction was that it tasted unusual.  Not bad, just unusual.  The "unusual" flavor was quickly replaced with the sweet aftertaste of pear.  Mmmm... that was actually pretty good.  I had some more.  Yup, unusual... mmmmmm pear.  I wound up eating the whole thing.I was running late the other morning and didn't have time for breakfast.  I saw this sitting in the cupboard and thought, "What the heck" and slurped it down on my way out the door.  Mmmmm pear!  It was about as filling as a Pop-tart but much, MUCH healthier and at least as good.  That's what I love most about this, I think--everything in this package is organic and there are no sweeteners or anything like that, so it's a good, healthy meal.Recommended (especially if you have a baby).

Offset pour spout!  Why don't all these baby food pouches have this design?  It's a lot easier to use!These are really tasty.  Yes, I ate some.  It's sweet and a little sour (just a little), and babies love this stuff.  Particularly for veggies, this is a great idea for getting babies familiar with this kind of food.  It pleased the one who eating some now.  It's easy to dispense and the package is very easy to carry.The ingredients list is refreshing.  No preservatives or dyes.  The sweetness is natural, too.The pouches can be twist shut after you open, which is handy if you're on the go and your baby only needs a little food.  The portions can last two meals per pouch, depending on your baby.I think this is a great product, but it's on the expensive side, so in my opinion is a four star value.

column9: Great as a secret add in!
column10: I know, it's baby food and I don't have small babies in the house. I do have younger children, picky eater younger children! This food was absolutely perfect for the reason I used it - to slip it into the foods my picky eaters will actually eat to give them more nutrition. Oh yes - it is slightly sweet, but it blends oh so well into everything! Spaghetti sauce, ketchup for dipping fries, BBQ sauce for dipping nuggets, salad dressing over a bed of greens, pancake and waffle batter, and even into smoothies! Yes, the taste was mild enough to even it get into oatmeal and cream of wheat with not a peep for the little ones.So, for those with babies - I can't see a baby turning this down. And - even when your baby outgrows the "puree" stage - keep buying this! When your 3, 4, or 5 year old goes through the picky stage this is a great way to sneak some additional nutrients into their diet.Some baby foods have a smell that turns non-babies off and this one didn't have that at all. I could handle the taste and smell easily. This means they were a good add in to my own milk kefir and mocha smoothies. Definitely recommend and will definitely buy in the future!Ingredients: Organic Pear, Organic Broccoli, Organic Spinach, Ascorbic Acid, Organic Lemon Juice Concentrate.Expiration date was approximately 4 1/2 months after delivery, so didn't have to be used right away, but not long enough to be forgotten about on a shelf.

As a 'Stage One' food, meant for 6 months old babies, this serves its purpose - introduce the baby to new food textures and to tastes other than milk. It's a time when babies continue to receive most of their nourishment from milk but they are now taught to accept and eventually enjoy some variety.It shouldn't come as a surprise that the product contains no protein, it's meant to be that way. Everything else appears to be clean and well balanced, the taste mild enough to ensure acceptance from the baby and everything, according to the makers, coming from an organic source. At 40 calories per serving (2 servings per pouch) it will not make a baby fat unless the baby was fed a couple of pouches per feeding session.We found the packaging to be convenient because the little bags are easy to store and to dispose but not everyone may 'get' squeezable pouches.Contents (for brevity, I will not write 'organic' before each of the ingredients but the maker claims they are so):- Pear- Broccoli- Spinach- Lemon juice concentrateAlso, Ascorbic Acid (source of vitamin C)Other features - things that it does not have:- no fillers or thickeners- no salt or sugars- no dairy, egg or lactose- no gluten- no nutsI can't see how you can go wrong with this. It's worth trying giving it to a 6 months old baby. If the baby rejects it, you can still try again a couple of weeks later. Our test subject seems to enjoy the treat.______________________________________Note:And... yes, the cap and the pouch itself are potential chocking hazards but, so is just about anything else in the house so make sure that the little one is not given the opportunity to try to swallow either.

column9: No mess, easy reuse, great for on the run
column10: There are a couple of different aspects of this product.  The first being the food itself.  Simple, organic, healthy, as much as it can be anyways and still be shelf stable.  The expiration dates seem to be short, which is reassuring that there are not many additives in it, however you might want to keep your eye on it.The packaging is the other aspect of this.  Since you can easily squeeze it out on to a spoon without touching the spoon, you can easily seal this up and use it again without worrying about bacteria from your child's mouth.  The alternative is the kid could just eat the food directly, which is great if the kid can do it and is going to eat it all anyways.  This makes it great for on the go.I don't think there are many downsides, unless your child doesn't like the greens mixed with the pear, since it does make the taste a bit strange (at least to my adult palette).

Baby food is one of those things I have been around a lot, I helped raise my little brother and I have a lot of friends with babies, so used and tasted a lot of baby foods, from Gerber to Beachnut, and various organic brands.So this one, is a little different, at least in its packaging.  I like the pouch in that it is easy to squeeze out in to a bowl and then store away, and I think its more travel friendly then say, carrying a glass jar, but in terms of the taste, it taste just about the same, to me, as any other baby food, it still taste like stale cook fruits and vegetables, but that's not a bad thing, since pretty much all pre-made baby food is that way.  I would say, if you are going to get this baby food, its main attracting factor is the packaging, and not the food itself, though it being organic is a plus.God Bless ~Amy

Baby Gourmet is the name of this baby food.Wonderful, organic baby food, which means it is good for the eater, and good for the environment.  This particular variety is juicy pear and garden greens.  The ingredients are:  organic pear, organic broccoli, organic spinach, vitamin C, organic lemon juice concentrate.This particular variety is for 6 months+.Wonderful, no fillers, unsweetened, organic, BPA-free packaging.  What more could you ask for?

I try to make as much of my own baby food as possible. Sometimes I can't do that, so I substitute with jars. I am a die-hard Earth's Best fan, but was open to trying something new.I have to say that I am really impressed with this baby food. It is certified organic and comes in a variety of tasty flavors that my 8-month old daughter loves. I was worried about the plastic packaging, but was glad to see it is BPA-free. The packaging is also very user-friendly; it's easy to open, easy to close, and easy to store.I still like the fact that Earth's Best comes in glass jars, but I will definitely try more flavors of this baby food in the future.

The short version:  These would probably be fine and palatable to a baby/toddler.  If you are looking for food for an older kid with eating issues/food aversions/texture issues etc... they are smooth as regular apple sauce, but the flavor made my son spit it out.  I thought they tasted good, but I'm not the one with the food aversions (or at least not the same ones)...  My son did eat plenty of green veggies as an infant that he won't touch now (even if pureed), so your mileage may vary.Our family regularly consumes more of these baby food "pouches" and fruit sauce "pouches" than I imagine most families who have an actual baby at the suggested "stage".  My son has autism and has quite a few issues with eating so not only does something have to taste good, it has to be uniform in consistency, and it has to look and smell acceptable to him.  He is 8 and he will eat baby food puree (Earth's best in the little glass jars) that doesn't have any "gummable" chunks that older babies usually get.  Add in that we have G6PD Deficiency and follow strict dietary rules and there are few "convenience" foods that are suited to our needs...My son adores the Revolution Foods pouches but will not touch home-made apple sauce (even if hidden in reused baby food jars)... Some of the Ella's Kitchen pouches he adores and others he hated so much that he will go through the entire fridge shelf of pouches just to make sure none of those flavors have infiltrated...I was hoping that this Baby Gourmet Simple Puree Juicy Pear and Garden Greens pouch would be a great way to get some Broccoli and other green goodies in his belly.  They do have some added ascorbic acid, which is contraindicated in high doses for folks with G6PD deficiency, but I calculated the potential dose and for us (your mileage may vary and you should consult your pediatrician or hematologist about ascorbic acid and any other contraindicated substances) it was ok.  My spouse joined us in the pouch taste test.I think they taste good- like pear-apple sauce with a hint of broccoli/greens.  It kind of reminded me of when my mom would serve us pork chops and potatoes, apple sauce, and spinach for dinner when I was a kid (sans the pork chops).... My husband thought they were just as good as any of the other ones we have tried.My kid took two slurps of it and ran to the toilet to spit it out.  He declared that it tastes like the apple sauce went bad.  I disagree, but as far as what purees come into our house, his opinion is very important.  I think that if I diluted one of these with two regular apple sauces it might "dampen" the loudness of the veggies enough for him to eat it but I'm not even sure about that.  To me the green flavors weren't that "loud" but they definitely made this "not pearsauce/applesauce blend"...  Definitely not a "sneaky chef" sort of food for our family, but I'll probably try other flavors out as they are still an extra little boost of goodness for adults on the run.

Great source of nutrition.  LOVE the packaging: easy to dispense, does not make messes when opened!  Our test baby (adorable baby Caleb, aged 5 months) LOVED it, I think he would eat every meal, I think.  He liked it after many failed attempts with other brands with ANY green vegetable.  This child may be pre-programmed for picky eating (as BOTH parents are terribly picky eaters) and yet he truly loved this.  This kiddo can eat a whole package in one sitting---and asks for more!  A total hit!  TRY IT!!!!!!

We have 9 month old twins and our babies love this baby gourmet juicy pear and garden greens.  That's the true test, if your baby eats it!  Ours eat it every time.  It looks green and a bit odd but they gobble it up.  There is nothing funky on the ingredients list that cause us concern either.  Overall we are very happy with this organic baby food and are babies are happy with it as well!

column9: Good, Wholesome Food for Your Infant Child
column10: Going organic is all the rage and organic versions of our favorite foods continue to appear in places we may not expect. One is baby food and one brand to offer the organic seal of approval is Baby Gourmet Organic Simple Purees Stage 1. Intended for babies age 6 months and younger, this food offers infants the same natural food goodness that adults have been enjoying thanks to the organic/green movement.This baby food is loaded with vitamins for an infant's good health and well- being. The product is kosher and the packaging is BPA free. These are all good qualities for a baby food and they are befitting a product promoted as organic and natural.But what about the taste? If a baby won't eat the food, then it makes no difference how healthy it is. Thankfully, babies do like this food. They eat it just as quickly as they do their other food and they have no problem finishing a full package, which isn't necessarily all that large. The texture is smooth and the digestion appears to be easy.One potential issue some may have with this baby food is its expiration. The expiration date is about five to six months in the future and I assume it is due to the all- natural, preservative free composition. This is a much shorter time frame than that of most canned baby foods, so you have to be careful not to purchase so much that your baby cannot consume it before the expiration date.Baby Gourmet Organic Simple Purees Stage 1 is, overall, a very good quality baby food with wholesome ingredients and good nutrition. The cost of about three dollars per container is a tad much, but this is a product of quality and most would agree that price is worth it for the good health of their infant family members.

column9: Simple. Tasteful, Great for Outings, Baby and Toddler Approved, Yum!
column10: These pouches are very handy and a delicious item for baby. My toddler is 22 months and still loves these. We have tried in other brands and flavors, but after having received a box of these to try  out she has found her new favorite. She seeks theses out, knows where we hide them and definitely loves them. Best of all, mommy loves them too. They are very handy with traveling, just toss a pouch in your diaper bag and go. You don't need a spoon for these either, very easy opening, that babies and toddlers seem to enjoy eating out of. We had our neighbors try them, ages 3 and 11 months and the kids wanted more. 3 for 3, we definitely recommend them.Ingredients are simple - Organic pear, organic broccoli, organic spinach, ascorbic acid, organic lemon juice concentrate

column4: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
column9: Baby loves it, simple to use, lasts 24 hours after opening
column10: Not sure if it was the baby's mood, but whenever we feed her this food, she eats every last drop - loves it.  The food combinations chosen for baby foods boggle me.  Juicy Pear and Garden Greens just don't seem like a palatable combination, but it's a winner.  As with other pouch foods, this lasts 24 hours after opening when refrigerated.My only complaint - the pouches are just placed in a box - no padding, etc. Of the two boxes, one pouch had opened up and partially drained into the box. It had the inevitable rotten vegetable smell when opening.  Tossed out the open pack, checked the rest. Washed them all of the sticky, greenish mess.So if you order a couple of boxes, open then up and inspect for leaks!

column9: Sneaky mom used this to add nutrition into the diet of a picky eater.
column10: I chose to try this product not because I have an infant, but because my pediatrician recommended it to help my picky 7-year-old get a more balanced diet.  The puree is supposed to be added to things such as spaghetti sauce and smoothies.The first pouch I actually tried myself-just to see what I was up against.  I thought it tasted pretty good. The first taste was a bit "green" but then I could taste the pears.  So, since they come in a cute pouch (and my son LOVES yougurt and applesauce that come in pouches), I thought I'd give it shot.  Open, taste, spit. No-go straight out of the pouch.I've since added it to smoothies, pancake mix, and oatmeal.  He was unable to detect it in any of those. Tonight, I'm trying it in the spaghetti sauce.  If it works, I will try some of the other flavor combinations in recipies.For the purpose that I used this for, I give it 4-stars. It would have gained a 5th if my son would have liked the taste straight out of the pouch.

column9: Finally, an impressive organic baby food product
column10: This product is one of those products that just cause you to say Wow and finally.  We have tried very hard to feed our children organic products after a major medical scare doctors traced to hormones found in non-organic milk. Anyone who has ever gone down this route will testify to 1) how difficult it can be and 2) how expensive it can be. This product makes it a little easier.  You also need to be concerned with truth in advertising as the organic market is still self-regulated (an analogy would be the real -estate industry and the classic Realtor symbol, which is largely self-regulated).  Look up Organic Consumer's Association for more information.Before I continue my review, many people will complain about the natural sugar contained in the pear or banana. That is true.  However,as I said before, it is a difficult road to go down and you have to be practical.  It is completely unrealistic to expect to find the perfect organic baby food your child will eat- even if you created it yourself. You have to find the balance you are comfortable with, so don't sweat it as you go down the this road.Baby Gourmet Organic Simple Purees Stage 1(6 Months+) Juicy Pear and Garden Greens Baby Food, 4.5-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 12) is a product that is easily handled and dispensed- thus making it invaluable for traveling.  WARNING-  Keep the cap away from children however.  It could be a choking hazard. If you are on the raod, the contents dispense in a less messy manner than similar products.  Must have something to do with the thickness of the non-recyclable BPA FREE container.  It works out well however, because it produces less mess yet allows a child to still self-dispense the contents.  Each package provides 2 servings so be sure to double the nutritional information if your child eats the entire package.  The product does not require refrigeration, dispenses easily, seals easily, and fits nearly anywhere. The ingredients in this product are all based on real food products and does not "source" other products that are based on soy (such as DHA sometimes added to baby food on the pretense that it enhances brain development).  Many will complain about the high carbs and low protein count.  However, the only proven perfect food for babies up to 18 months is human mothers milk with an increasing need for protein as the child develops (my wife elected to breast feed our children for 2 years).  Clearly carbs are a major societal issue but I am out of my realm to realistically suggest a solution. I am just trying to strike a solid balance for my children.  In that regard, and comparatively, this product provides an ample solution when balanced with organic protein sources.Our children both loved the taste of the product as did we.

column9: great for eating on the go...
column10: I prefer glass jars for my kids because I'm not a huge fans of them eating from plastic so much. But I understand that there are times that you need a meal on the go with minimal mess. This seems perfect for that situation. And I feel that the company is doing as much as they can to make it a safe product with these pouch things being bpa free and all.My only complaint is that one pouch leaked in shipping. It didn't leak too much, but that makes me hesitent to order more off amazon. I know that amazon would replace any that leak, but I don't like hassel in ordering online.I feel the review is for the product, and this stuff is great! I tasted it and it tastes very close to applesause but not as sweet. I do like the container design and my youngun is able to eat it by herself with just a bit of me helping to squeeze.It may sound probably dumb to give a great review with all the qualifiers (bad plastic, leaking product), but we really do like them. I would definately suggest them.

I originally got these for my 11-month-old, but my 2.5 year old begged to try one and so I gave in. They were a hit with both of my kiddos. I like that they are made of organic ingredients and seem to be a decent size pouch (bigger than some other ones that I've found at the grocery store). I tasted it myself and it tasted a bit like a green smoothie, you could taste the veggies, but it was definitely sweet and tasty. It got five stars from this family. :-)

column9: Good alternative to the homeade stuff
column10: The ingredients are: pear, broccolli, spinache, lemon juice, and Vitamin C (absorbic acid).That's pretty much what I put in his homeade purees, except the absorbic acid, which is a perfectly safe ingredient.  My 8 month old loves this stuff.  And it's green, which is awesome.And I love the pouch.  It makes it really easy to have on the go -- you can squeeze out just enough to put on a spoon (or my finger when I'm in a pinch), and the spout is safer than a jar because there's less room for contaminants to get in.And I've tasted it myself -- it tastes good!  I mean, I'm not personally going to snack on it, but it tastes like what it is -- broccolli, spinach, and pear, and all those are pretty good-tasting foods.Recommended.

column9: Tasty, convenient, and not too messy
column10: I tasted these before I handed them over to the littles.  The pear really does "overpower" the brocolli, but the veggie taste is just underneath.What I Like:Easy to take alongRequires no refrigerationTexture just like applesauce, so it's not "weird"The "spout" is the only hard part, so it's not terrifying if your kid walks around with this thing hangin' out of his/her mouthWhat I Don't Like:Baby / Toddler can get overzealous and SQUEEZE a mess rather quicklyMess factor isn't a deal breaker for me - it's baby food, after all!  I think these are pretty cool for picnics, beach days, and whatever else you might need a cooler or picnic basket for!  They're also probably a great pick-me-up for low blood sugar if you don't have anything handy but the diaper bag!

I am impressed that the flavor of spinach & broccoli is as mild as it is considering pears are the only fruit added (though pears are listed first in the ingredients).  This is a much more pleasant way to sneak in some greens!  I did notice that some pkgs. seem to have a stronger spinach flavor & taste less sweet than other pkgs. of the same case.Green veggies are never a big hit so it was nice to find something that is well tolerated!  Some brands are down right awful, as I'm sure you know.I really prefer glass but the portability of the pouches can't be beat!  I love how convenient they are & the variety keeps expanding.  So perfect when I need to grab & go.  Jars for home.  Pouches for travel.I look forward to trying more Baby Gourmet flavors.

My darling little daughter just turned six months and received the okay from the pediatrician to start eating solid foods.  Baby Gourmet's Juicy Pear & Garden Greens puree was her first taste at something other than breast milk and rice cereal, and did she ever love it!These purees are great first foods for babies.  They are easy to swallow and easy on the digestive system.  My daughter absolutely loved the taste and was constantly reaching out for the spoon between bites!I, too, tried the Baby Gourmet food, and was pleasantly surprised by the delicious taste.  It had the perfect amount of pear to sweeten the vegetable taste without making a child too accustomed to a sugary taste.  In addition to its yumminess, I had peace of mind giving my daughter a product free of chemical additives, pesticides, and fertilizers.  Being that she is my first child, I only want the best for her, and I believe Baby Gourmet is amongst the best in baby foods.

Our granddaughter is 10 months old and so I got these for her as her parents are really into organic foods.  Our daughter has been feeding her these now for a couple of weeks and they are just about gone!  It turns out that not only does she like the taste of them but also the pouch has an opening that makes it easy if they are on the road or at someone else's house without a baby spoon to feed her by squeezing the package and the puree comes out easily through the opening.  A great buy and a terrific product.  Our daughter plans to buy more herself!  Highly recommended.

Judging from how my grandson didn't take his eyes off the spoon (since we served this sample at home using a small dish) from the minute he tasted this combination, he obviously would rank it as five stars for taste.  There is no doubt that it is made of first quality ingredients, so five stars for that, as well.So why four stars?  Just judging from the competition, it is seriously over-priced.  This is not the only brand of organic baby food on the market.  While I can't compare its taste to the other equally high quality brands since my daughter-in-law makes the majority of his food from scratch, this seems to rank as the costliest.  On the other hand, the convenience of its packaging makes it ideal for long trips or outings.So, five stars for quality, taste and packaging, minus one for price.

Obviously most parents know the advantage of having vegetables mixed in with fruits for babies that tend to be a bit picky.  My daughter hasn't responded any differently to this mixed into her morning cereal than she did with fruit alone, so that tells me that the flavor must be appealing.  I appreciate the fact that you can see the flecks of greens in the product as well, it comes much closer to the homemade purees my wife has made.  The price of these is a bit higher per ounce than some of the other pouches, like Plum Organics, but it's still not bad considering how much food you get in the Amazon package.  This has been a hit in our home and I'm looking forward to trying their other flavors!

I know this was intended for babies/toddlers but it's good for preschoolers too! I wanted to see if my 3 year old son would enjoy it and he does! I pack in his lunchbox with his favorite organic Peanut Butter Sandwhich and a fruit or baby carrots. We pack it along as we go to long hikes, outings or preschool and he gulps it up! I sampled a bit and it's not overly sweet but just the right amount of flavor and full of nutrition for growing minds. Much better than a juice box! But just in-case they get extra thirsty it's always a good idea to have purified water nearby =)

column9: Siberia and Small-Town Hoosier votes 2 thumbs up
column10: Organic is huge if baby's health is key. Ixnay on chemicals. Natural foods for the best of growing starts. Baby Gourmet Juicy Pear & Garden Greens has a mix of 2 fruits and 2 veggies: Organic Pear, Organic Lemon Juice Concentrate, Organic Broccoli, & Organic Spinach. A wellness start in baby food.BUT WILL BABY EAT IT?Grandson Frank gave it the test with consent and assistance from his mom. Frank is half Russian, half American. A cold war free opinion from a 7-month-old objective tester. He has his way of expressing his likes/dislikes, piercingly. Nyet, robustly.Frank tried juicy pear with greens and ate it with a "Mmmmmmmmmm" and no mess, then after having finished it he said: "ammm...ooo...uh..." I guess it was his opinion of it, so you can interpret it as you wish. To me it seemed he was saying something like "Taste's like chicken" or "Mmmore mmamma mmore gooood fruit and veggies." That's when Frank got a little possessive and demanded the other eleven easy-open recap-able pouches be saved for his grandparent visits. Being a pushover grandparent, I agreed, me being a pineapple-green beans fan anyway.I did notice the nutrition facts. Due to health I personally must watch things like fats, trans fats, & sodium. ZEROg for each of these. To heart-healthy watchers that means perfect. Plus 70% Daily requirements of vit.C, 2g fiber and 25% of vit.A in just a half pouch. Frank's a big eater, like his PaPa, and ate the whole pouch, not a drop missed, spit, or blown.HE LIKES IT, FRANKIE LIKES IT!Like milk, the cost is a bit higher compared to non-organic foods on the shelf, so since the taste and nutrition value is confirmed, it boils down to what the budget allows and "is your child worth the extra?"

My 22 month old toddler absolutely loves the pouches of baby/toddler food.  I have bought her the fruit flavors of several different brands in the past.  When I read the ingredient list on these (organic pears, broccoli, and spinach), I was rather doubtful that she would like the taste.  To my surprise, she seems to prefer these over the sweeter berry flavored pouches that we also have right now.The pouches are very convenient to keep in the diaper bag, and are a good snack for when we are out of the house.  My daughter prefers them cold from the refrigerator, but will also eat them at room temperature.  They only require refrigeration if they have already been opened.  For a younger baby, you can squeeze the food directly onto a spoon.  My toddler likes to suck the food out of the pouch.My only complaint about the pouches is the high price.  In all fairness though, the competing brands are about the same cost.

This uniquely packaged baby food has a lot going for it, not the least of which is its organic cachet. With no sweeteners, fillers or salt added , a parent can be assured of pure and wholesome ingredients. The pliable, metallic container is quite unique with its plastic spout and lid. No need to worry about breakage when dropping the baby food, though bursting can occur to an errantly stepped on package.We like that the Baby Gourmet food is easily transporable and that any left over food may be refrigerated for up to 24 hours. Other foods have a longer after opening lives and longer shelf lives also. Our shipment of Baby Gourmet reaches its expiration date five months after we received it. That should be no problem because it'll easily all be gone within a month.But what about taste and satisfaction? Our grandson loved this food from the first spoonful and ate it eagerly. Subsequent feedings have produced the same positive response. Our daughter let Gabe chew on the spout for a minute while she held the food "bag"; this was great fun for Gabe but not a practice I'd recommend. To feed Gabe the Baby Gourmet food, we screw off the plastic lid and squeeze the food into a bowl or empty baby food jar. Our 8-month-old charmer readily finishes off the entire containerful in one setting.There are only a couple negatives for me with this product. One is the cost which may fall in time. The other is the packaging itself which as others have mentioned doesn't appear to be recyclable. When our grandson visits, Mrs. Spudman and I like to stock up on the recyclable glass baby jars that come in handy for all sorts of projects and storage of tiny objects.The Baby Gourmet foods are a product of Canada.

I have two daughters, one is 2.5 years old and the other is 13 months old and they have absolutely loved the Baby Gourmet Organic Juicy Pear and Garden Greens flavor.  Both of my daughters tend to be picky eaters in that they won't eat the same thing at back to back meals, but they constantly demanded these for breakfast, dinner, and lunch.  The squeeze pack was suitably sized for a meal, and the offset valve (rather than being directly in the center) allowed both of my daughters to feed themselves.  I've tried a number of similar products on the market, but have yet to find one that my daughters enjoyed as much as this particular flavor.I will admit that the price seems high, but compared to other offerings and in looking at the weight to price value, I find these to be comparable to other brands on the market.Also we had less incidents of messes with the Baby Gourmet Organic packaging because my daughters couldn't open it on their own and because the product didn't squeeze out as easily when they grasped the package (which has been my experience with other brands).

column9: Gourmet "organic" baby food at a premium price.
column10: The current catch phrase among baby foods is "organic".  Unless one actually harvests and purees organically grown fruits and vegetables directly from a garden, all manufactured, processed, and packaged baby foods can't be considered truly organic.  Baby Gourmet has provided consumers with a good selection of "organic" baby foods that's worth a try.Likes:>Easy to use pouches; just remove cap then squeeze and feed.>Package claims no artificial ingredients, unsalted, and unsweetened.>Gluten and nut free (for babies that are allergic).>BPA Free packaging (safer for babies).>Our 13 months old baby really liked the "Juicy Pear and Garden Greens" puree and gulped it down unassisted.>Provides good source of Vitamin C (140% DV).>Good selection of different fruits and vegetables packs made for babies from 6 months+ to 8 months+.Dislikes:>Parent supervision always necessary or the baby may make a mess and squeeze the puree out everywhere.>Don't leave the cap around the baby; potential choking hazard!>Premium price at $0.51 per ounce.compared to what we've also tried: Organic Baby Organic Summer vegetable ( 24x4 OZ) at 0.18 per ounce.  However, Amazon does offer a great subscription service that lowers the Baby Gourmet price to 0.43 per ounce.Bottom Line:Premium organic baby food comes at a premium price.  Well worth it if one's baby likes eating it.

I was really excited to get these because I've seen babies sucking on these pouches around town.  Now that my baby's eating solids, I wanted to see what all the rage is.  I love them for many reasons!-First, they're ORGANIC,  no fillers added.-Second, they TASTE GOOD (of course I tasted!). What's more is my baby loves it more than any food he's tried so far.  He couldn't get enough.-NUTRITIOUS:  Baby gets his greens--broccoli and spinach--mixed with sweet pears.  You can actually see the green flecks of goodness.-TEXTURE:  Fruits and veggies are well-pureed, perfect for stage 1.-3 WAYS TO FEED: 1-Squeeze into bowl and spoon feed, 2-Squeeze directly onto spoon, 3-Squeeze into baby's mouth or let baby suck it out through plastic tube.For the first serving, I mostly spoon fed my baby, but once I let him suck on it, he wanted to keep sucking it down.-QUANTITY: There's a lot of food in there!  2 servings per pouch, 4.5 oz pouches-CONVENIENT:  Of course it's convenient because you can feed your baby nutritious, organic food without dirtying even one dish or utensil.  Convenient because you can feed on the go.  Convenient because the cap twists back on so you can save the rest for later...-The one DRAWBACK would have to be the PRICE.  These are pretty expensive for a pouch of food.  But it is organic, and for now, I expect to pay more for that.I'm sold on these, but because of the price, for me, these will be a "sometimes" food bought for convenience and travel.  In fact I plan on taking these on vacation with me so I can feed my baby in his stroller, on the run. I'm actually excited to give it a try!And by the way, after I'm done here, I'll be searching to see what other varieties Baby Gourmet offers...Happy feeding!

column9: So delicious that even my 1 year old enjoys it!
column10: I don't have an infant right now, but I still decided to give these Baby Gourmet Purees a try.  I did literally eat a couple bites myself.  The pear flavor was definitely stronger than the flavor of the greens, but I could tell there were greens in there.  I wasn't sure if my 1 year old daughter would like it or not, but I gave her a bite anyway.  She wanted another bite, and another, and another.  Then she grabbed the pouch and sucked the puree right out of the straw itself.  I guess that means she liked it!  And if a one year old whose been eating flavorful table foods for months will eat it, then a 6 month old will definitely enjoy it.Even though this baby food is pureed, thin enough for a baby just beginning to eat, I like that I could actually SEE flecks of green in it.  I could see that it had garden greens in it, which definitely made me feel like it was a healthier and more natural baby food choice.  As your baby grows, you can stir in a baby cereal to thicken the puree.I'm not sure why it's in a pouch rather than a jar or a plastic container, but I like it.  The twist-on cap can re-seal the pouch after you pour out exactly as much as you need.  Then it can be stored in the refrigerator until you're ready to serve more to your baby.  I'm sure they don't want you to allow your toddler to suck on the straw-like spout, and I'm sure it introduces germs into the rest of the food if you do that.  So, just because I let my toddler do that, doesn't mean it's the smartest way to handle this baby food.  The pouch should be easier to transport in a diaper bag than a glass jar and should seal better than the flimsy plastic containers with click-on lids.So from myself, my one year, and my friend's 9 month old ... we definitely recommend the Baby Gourmet Stage 1 baby foods.

column9: AWESOME Baby Gormet Pear & greens for all ages. 18 month and 11 year old loved this green squeezable organic Veggie fruit pouch.
column10: Organic portable veggie fruit pouch great for everyone adults or elderly, not just for infants, babies or toddlers.  Shelf stable, easy to keep handy in car, in bag, or in pantry for quick grab in go fruit. 18 month old just inhaled it in less than 2 minutes. She loves broccoli. My 11 year old Aspie said it was excellent. He loved the spinach taste.  He also likes that the spout is on the side better.  I tried it and got sweet pear with hint of spinach. All in all a great  making it easy to get greens in your family. My 11 year old son suggested to  Organic Gormet try making it iwht apple. Apple goes better with spinach.

I think this is a great product for the picky 2-year old eater (obviously younger children who are not ready for solid foods would also really benefit from this product.  It can be sucked directly from the pouch or squeezed onto a spoon for feeding).  My son (the aforementioned picky eater) eats fruits but no veggies, so I thought these pouches would be a good alternative to supplement his diet.  He considers them a "treat" and gobbles them up.  They are also a great traveling food-- perfect to pop in my purse when we are heading out.  I love that they are organic, convenient and don't need to be refrigerated (unless you open it).

My 8 month old baby went bat guano over this puree!  She was a crazy person, and gulped one down in about 45 seconds, no exaggeration.  She then wailed until I opened another one and she sucked that one down just as quickly, too.  I just opened it and let her suck it right out of the pouch, kind of like a Capri Sun for babies, although you could put it in a bowl, which probably would have slowed down her eating.  9 ounces of food in 3 minutes, that is a lot.  Which is partly why I didn't give this product 5 stars, because this stuff is expensive!  No way could I afford to give these to her often, especially not 2 at a time, even with subscribe and save they are almost two dollars a pouch.  Yikes!  But the other reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because with all the good stuff these have, ORGANIC veggies, gluten free, no sugar, no additives, BPA free packaging, the packaging is a real environmental waste.  It would be a 5 star product if the packaging was recyclable.  They could at least use less plastic on the cap (the cap does make the package resealable, though, which is nice if you have a baby that actually doesn't eat the entire container, can't say I know what that is like!)  But for taste, 5 stars all the way!  And they are great for travel, no chance of broken glass containers of food.

I'm not looking a Gift Horse in the Mouth but it would have been nice to try the other flavours on my grand-daughter. However, the 2 boxes we received were both Juicy Pear and Garden Greens so I thank my blessings (and amazon Vine) and am reviewing that flavour.I made 100% of my daughter's and son's baby food and know how long that took. In today's much busier world with two working parents, providing very healthy food for babies is tough. I also never gave my children anything that I wouldn't find tasty, so I knew that I needed to try this product before I experimented on my grand-daughter.I squeezed the contents from the intriguing packaging into a small bowl. First I tried it at room temperature and then heated it as recommended (bowl set into warm water, NOT microwave!) and tried the remainder of it that way. BOTH versions were good but I enjoyed it cool, much moreso. When cool, the pears dominated; when warm, the greens dominated. I was amused that the flavour was very similar to a gourmet chilled soup that I make in the summertime. :)My grand-daughter just finished an entire package of this in a wee bowl (with my help) and she LOVED it! I like the fact that it's not just fruit or just vegetables but BOTH. As it stands, we'll power through what we received and then go on the lookout for the other flavours available.Both my daughter and I really appreciated the convenient pouch, which makes feeding the baby very simple when you are out and about. No glass to break and you can squeeze the puree onto a baby spoon, making feeding a snap. Baby, mom and me all heartedly recommend both the product and packaging.

I like the packaging and the ingredients but my son (20 months) hated the taste. He eats pouches all the time and has had similar veggie combos and loved them. Not sure what is was about this flavor but he just spit it out and refused to eat it.

column9: Two year old is the test dummy. Sorry :>)
column10: When Amazon offered this baby food I thought "Wow! just the thing for the little guy when he starts on solid food!" Unfortunately I didn't consider the expiration date.  Don't get me wrong! I wouldn't expect ,or WANT ,a baby food with no preservatives to last indefinitely.  It's just something to consider if you plan to stockpile or you're giving it as a gift for a baby who won't be on solid food for a while.I think the food is most commendable for what it DOESN'T have.
